synthesis.even-composite-doublet-needs-a.formal:
Let the modes be tower planes, $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$, with the canonical anticommutation relations (Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) and $v^{*} = w$ (Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}), each carrying a channel that is either a member of an isospin doublet, $(\delta, \uparrow)$ or $(\delta, \downarrow)$ ($\delta$ in a finite set of further labels: species, colour, momentum, generation), or a singlet $s \in S$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the real algebra they generate, $\mathcal{A}_{D}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{S}$ the subalgebras generated by the doublet and by the singlet modes, and $\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, p_{S})}$ the span of the products $xy$ with $x \in \mathcal{A}_{D}$ of parity $p_{D}$ and $y \in \mathcal{A}_{S}$ of parity $p_{S}$. Isospin acts by commutators with $T_{+} = \sum_{\delta}a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{\delta\downarrow}$, $T_{-} = T_{+}^{*}$, $T_{3} = \tfrac12\sum_{\delta}(n_{\delta\uparrow} - n_{\delta\downarrow})$, with Casimir $C = (\operatorname{ad}T_{3})^{2} + \tfrac12(\operatorname{ad}T_{+}\operatorname{ad}T_{-} + \operatorname{ad}T_{-}\operatorname{ad}T_{+})$; a hypercharge is $Y = \sum_{x}Y_{x}n_{x}$ with real channel weights equal on the two members of each doublet.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Selection rule.)} $\mathcal{A} = \bigoplus_{p_{D}, p_{S}}\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, p_{S})}$, each summand invariant under $\operatorname{ad}T_{j}$ and $\operatorname{ad}Y$, and every eigenvalue of $\operatorname{ad}T_{3}$ on $\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, \cdot)}$ lies in $\tfrac12p_{D} + \mathbb{Z}$. Hence every element of half-integer isospin, in particular every doublet, is odd in the doublet modes, and an even one lies in $\mathcal{A}^{(1,1)}$: it is odd in the singlet modes, so it needs $S \ne \emptyset$. For one doublet pair of modes and any singlets, $C = \tfrac34$ on all of $\mathcal{A}^{(1, \cdot)}$, and on $\mathcal{A}^{(0, p_{S})}$ the eigenvalues are $0$ and $2$, the latter with multiplicity $3\dim\mathcal{A}_{S}^{p_{S}}$. The lowest even doublets are the bilinears, for each $\delta$ and $s$ the four (upper, lower) pairs
\[
(a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{s}, a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}a_{s}),\quad (a_{s}^{*}a_{\delta\downarrow}, -a_{s}^{*}a_{\delta\uparrow}),\quad (a_{\delta\downarrow}a_{s}, -a_{\delta\uparrow}a_{s}),\quad (a_{s}^{*}a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}, a_{s}^{*}a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}),
\]
of hypercharge $Y_{\delta} - Y_{s}$, $Y_{s} - Y_{\delta}$, $-(Y_{\delta} + Y_{s})$, $Y_{\delta} + Y_{s}$: a bilinear doublet of hypercharge $\pm\tfrac12$ needs $|Y_{\delta} - Y_{s}| = \tfrac12$ or $|Y_{\delta} + Y_{s}| = \tfrac12$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Pair modes of a doublet are quasi-spins.)} On one null generator, in the notation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins} (window $I = \{-N, \dots, N - 1\}$, $\rho_{q}(M) = \sum_{k}a_{k}^{*}Ma_{k+q}$), let $W$ be a diagonal matrix of real channel weights. If $[W, M] = hM$ with $h \ne 0$, $M$ is nilpotent, hence not normal if nonzero, so for $N > q$, $\rho_{q}(M)$ is not a canonical boson on the edge-clean vectors, and if $M^{2} = 0$, $B = \rho_{q}(M)^{*}$ on the chiral sea $\Omega$ has $|B^{p}\Omega|^{2} = (p!)^{2}e_{p}$ over the $q\operatorname{rank}M$ squared singular values, zero for $p > q\operatorname{rank}M$. Every component of a doublet of pair densities has $T_{3} = \pm\tfrac12$, so its matrix satisfies this with the isospin weights ($\pm\tfrac12$ on the members of each doublet, $0$ on singlets), and with the hypercharge weights when its hypercharge is nonzero. For the hopping $M = E_{(\delta\uparrow), s}$: $M^{2} = 0$, $\operatorname{rank}M = 1$, $|B^{p}\Omega|^{2} = (p!)^{2}\binom{q}{p}$; on edge-clean vectors $[\rho_{q}(M), \rho_{q}(M)^{*}]$ is $q + 1$ with one extra bulk particle in channel $\delta\uparrow$ and $q - 1$ with one in channel $s$; and with $M' = E_{(\delta\downarrow), s}$, $[\rho_{q}(M), \rho_{q}(M')^{*}]$ acts on edge-clean vectors as the bulk isospin raising density $\sum_{k\ \mathrm{bulk}}a_{k,\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{k,\delta\downarrow}$.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (i) and (ii) are proved. \emph{Reading (argued).} The rung field's oddness does not exclude a composite doublet of two kinds of fermions: the condition is a singlet constituent with matching hypercharge. Particle-pair doublets reduce to hoppings by the particle-hole reflection of the singlet planes. No component of a composite doublet is among the exact (normal, neutral) pair bosons of a generator; each is a quasi-spin of finite capacity, canonical only in a contraction over many sites. This concerns the composite's charges and statistics, not its gap.
synthesis.even-composite-doublet-needs-a.technical: Let tower modes carry isospin-doublet channels and singlet channels. (i) The algebra they generate splits by the parity of the doublet factors and the parity of the singlet factors; isospin and hypercharge act within each part, and on the part with doublet parity $p_{D}$ the isospin-3 weights lie in $p_{D}/2 + \mathbb{Z}$. So every doublet is odd in the doublet modes, and an even doublet is odd in the singlet modes: a composite doublet needs a singlet constituent, and that is the only condition parity imposes. With one doublet pair of modes the doublet-odd part is entirely isospin one-half and the doublet-even part is isospin zero and one. The simplest even doublets are the doublet-singlet bilinears (two hoppings and two pairs), of hypercharge $\pm(Y_{\delta} - Y_{s})$ and $\pm(Y_{\delta} + Y_{s})$, so hypercharge one-half fixes the singlet's hypercharge from the doublet's. (ii) On a null generator a component of a doublet of pair densities has isospin-3 weight $\pm\tfrac12$, so its channel matrix is charged under the isospin weights (and under hypercharge if the doublet has any), hence nilpotent and never normal. As a corollary of the stored helicity-one theorem (\claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(iii), (iv)) read with isospin weights, whose argument uses only real weights, it is never a canonical boson on the edge-clean vectors, and when $M^{2} = 0$ (for example a single doublet-singlet hopping, or nonzero hypercharge with all doublet channels of one hypercharge) on the sea it is a quasi-spin of $q\operatorname{rank}M$ sites; without $M^{2} = 0$ the quasi-spin count can fail. For a doublet-singlet hopping the capacity is $q$, the norms are $(p!)^{2}\binom{q}{p}$, the commutator on edge-clean vectors is $q \pm 1$ according to a bulk particle in the doublet or the singlet channel, and the two components' mutual commutator is the isospin raising density. Reading (argued): the composite doublet is allowed by parity, needs a singlet constituent, and its components are quasi-spins, canonical only in a contraction; its gap is a separate question.
synthesis.even-composite-doublet-needs-a.lay: The Higgs field comes in a pair of components, an isospin doublet. The graph already showed that such a doublet cannot be built from the Higgs field's own tower modes as an even, boson-like element. This result says what it takes instead: a doublet built from fermion modes is boson-like only if it combines an odd number of doublet fermions with an odd number of fermions that carry no isospin, the simplest case being one of each, and the charges must then match so that the pair has the Higgs field's hypercharge. Such pairs exist, so the composite route is open as far as charges go. But each component of such a pair mode, on a single light ray, is never an exact boson because it carries charge, and for the simplest such pair it behaves like a finite bank of two-state switches rather than an exact boson; it approaches boson behaviour only when very many such sites are pooled.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors} each plane gives a mode $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$ with $\{a_{x}, a_{y}^{*}\} = \delta_{xy}$, $\{a_{x}, a_{y}\} = 0$, and $v^{*} = w$ (the mutual adjointness of the ladder pairs, Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}). One plane's algebra is spanned by $1, v, w, vw$ (since $e = v + w$, $f = v - w$, $ef = wv - vw$), so $\mathcal{A}$ is spanned by the ordered monomials $\prod_{x}m_{x}$ with $m_{x} \in \{1, a_{x}^{*}, a_{x}, a_{x}^{*}a_{x}\}$, and these are a basis (there are $4^{n}$ of them for $n$ planes, the dimension of the algebra). Call a monomial's \emph{doublet degree} the number of its factors $m_{x} \in \{a_{x}^{*}, a_{x}\}$ with $x$ a doublet channel, and likewise its singlet degree; their parities are $p_{D}$, $p_{S}$. Writing a monomial with its doublet factors first (a sign) shows it is a product $xy$ with $x \in \mathcal{A}_{D}$ of parity $p_{D}$ and $y \in \mathcal{A}_{S}$ of parity $p_{S}$, and conversely every such product is a combination of monomials with these parities. So $\mathcal{A} = \bigoplus\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, p_{S})}$.

\emph{(i).} The isospin generators and $Y$ are combinations of $a_{x}^{*}a_{y}$, even in both kinds of modes. From the relations, $[a_{x}^{*}a_{y}, a_{z}^{*}] = \delta_{yz}a_{x}^{*}$ and $[a_{x}^{*}a_{y}, a_{z}] = -\delta_{xz}a_{y}$, so $\operatorname{ad}(a_{x}^{*}a_{y})$ is a derivation that maps each doublet mode operator to a doublet mode operator (or zero) when $x, y$ are doublet channels, and each singlet one to a singlet one when they are singlet channels; hence $\operatorname{ad}T_{j}$ and $\operatorname{ad}Y$ preserve the doublet and singlet degrees of every monomial up to terms of the same parities, and each $\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, p_{S})}$ is invariant. In particular $[T_{3}, a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}] = \tfrac12a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}$, $[T_{3}, a_{\delta\uparrow}] = -\tfrac12a_{\delta\uparrow}$, $[T_{3}, a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}] = -\tfrac12a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}$, $[T_{3}, a_{\delta\downarrow}] = \tfrac12a_{\delta\downarrow}$, and $\operatorname{ad}T_{3}$ kills $a_{x}^{*}a_{x}$ and the singlet modes; as a derivation it is diagonal on the monomials, with eigenvalue the sum of the factors' weights, an element of $\tfrac12(\text{doublet degree}) + \mathbb{Z} = \tfrac12p_{D} + \mathbb{Z}$. An element with a component of half-integer isospin has a component with a half-integer eigenvalue of $\operatorname{ad}T_{3}$, so its $\mathcal{A}^{(0, \cdot)}$ part cannot carry it: every $\operatorname{ad}T_{3}$-eigenvector with half-integer eigenvalue lies in $\mathcal{A}^{(1, 0)} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{(1, 1)}$, and if it is even (total parity $p_{D} + p_{S}$ even) it lies in $\mathcal{A}^{(1, 1)}$, which is zero when $S$ is empty. For one doublet pair of modes, $\mathcal{A}_{D}$ is the algebra of the two rung-type planes of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower-and-its-modes-carry-no-even-doublet}(2): its odd part (dimension $8$) has Casimir $\tfrac34$ and its even part (dimension $8$) Casimir eigenvalues $0$ (multiplicity $5$) and $2$ (multiplicity $3$). Since $\operatorname{ad}T_{j}$ acts on $xy$ as $(\operatorname{ad}T_{j}x)y$ ($T_{j}$ commutes with $\mathcal{A}_{S}$, being even and built from doublet modes, which anticommute with singlet modes), $\mathcal{A}^{(p_{D}, p_{S})} \cong \mathcal{A}_{D}^{p_{D}}\otimes\mathcal{A}_{S}^{p_{S}}$ as an isospin representation with $\mathcal{A}_{S}$ inert, which gives the stated Casimir values and multiplicities. For the bilinears, take $\delta$ fixed and compute with the two rules above: $[T_{+}, a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{s}] = 0$, $[T_{-}, a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{s}] = a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}a_{s}$, $[T_{+}, a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}a_{s}] = a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{s}$ (with $T_{+} = \sum a_{\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{\delta\downarrow}$), and $T_{3}$ weights $\pm\tfrac12$: a doublet. The other three pairs follow in the same way (the minus signs in the lower components come from $[T_{-}, a_{\delta\downarrow}] = -a_{\delta\uparrow}$, with $T_{-} = \sum a_{\delta\downarrow}^{*}a_{\delta\uparrow}$). For hypercharge, $[Y, a_{x}^{*}] = Y_{x}a_{x}^{*}$ and $[Y, a_{x}] = -Y_{x}a_{x}$ give the four values listed.

\emph{(ii).} A channel matrix $M$ with $[W, M] = hM$ has nonzero entries only where $w_{\alpha} - w_{\beta} = h$; a nonzero entry of $M^{n}$ needs a chain with weight differences summing to $nh$, impossible once $n|h|$ exceeds the spread of the weights, so $M$ is nilpotent, and a normal nilpotent matrix is zero. This is the argument of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(iii), which uses only that the weights are real numbers; the weights there are the helicity weights, here the hypercharge or isospin weights. By its clause (ii) a nonzero non-normal $M$ gives a $\rho_{q}(M)$ that is not a canonical boson on the edge-clean vectors ($N > q$), and by its clause (iv), when $M^{2} = 0$, $B = \rho_{q}(M)^{*}$ on the chiral sea has $|B^{p}\Omega|^{2} = (p!)^{2}e_{p}$ over the $q\operatorname{rank}M$ numbers $\sigma_{s}^{2}$, zero for $p > q\operatorname{rank}M$. A component of a doublet of pair densities has $T_{3} = \pm\tfrac12$: its matrix has $[W_{3}, M] = \pm\tfrac12M$ for the isospin weights $W_{3}$ ($\pm\tfrac12$ on the members of each doublet, $0$ on singlets); and if the doublet has hypercharge $y \ne 0$, also $[W_{Y}, M] = yM$. For $M = E_{(\delta\uparrow), s}$, $M^{2} = 0$ and $\operatorname{rank}M = 1$, the singular value is $1$ and $e_{p}$ of $q$ ones is $\binom{q}{p}$. On edge-clean vectors the window identity of the cited clause (i) gives the value $q\operatorname{tr}(M^{*}M) + \rho_{0}([M, M^{*}]) = q + \rho_{0}(E_{\delta\uparrow,\delta\uparrow} - E_{ss})$, which is $q + 1$ with one extra particle in channel $\delta\uparrow$ at a bulk momentum and $q - 1$ with one in channel $s$; and for $M' = E_{(\delta\downarrow), s}$ it gives $[\rho_{q}(M), \rho_{q}(M')^{*}] = q\operatorname{tr}(M'^{*}M) + \rho_{0}([M, M'^{*}]) = \rho_{0}(E_{\delta\uparrow,\delta\downarrow})$, since $M'^{*}M = E_{s,\delta\downarrow}E_{\delta\uparrow,s} = 0$ and $MM'^{*} = E_{\delta\uparrow,\delta\downarrow}$; on an edge-clean vector the edge momenta are filled or empty in every channel, where $a_{k,\delta\uparrow}^{*}a_{k,\delta\downarrow}$ acts as zero, so only the bulk remains.

\emph{Reading (argued).} The rung field's oddness (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower-and-its-modes-carry-no-even-doublet}) does not exclude a composite doublet of two kinds of fermions: (i) says exactly what it requires, a singlet constituent, and how the hypercharges must match. Particle-particle doublets reduce to the hopping case by the particle-hole reflection of the singlet planes ($f \mapsto -f$ on those planes exchanges $v_{s}$ and $w_{s}$, reverses the singlet sea and the sign of $Y_{s}$), so they too are nilpotent with charge $\mp(Y_{\delta} + Y_{s})$ and isospin $\pm\tfrac12$. So no component of a composite doublet is among the exact (normal, neutral) pair bosons of a generator; each is a quasi-spin of finite capacity, canonical only in a contraction over many sites, as the helicity-one modes are for the photon. This bears on the boson statistics of a composite Higgs, not on its gap.

synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity.formal:
Let a window carry $L$ tower planes with null pairs $v_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j})$, $w_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} - f_{j})$, $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, $j = 0, \dots, L - 1$, the Witt pairs of Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} read with $v_{j}$ as creators, $n_{j} = v_{j}w_{j}$, $\hat N = \sum_{j}n_{j}$, $*$ the adjoint ($v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$), and the density modes $\rho_{q} = \sum_{j = 0}^{L - 1 - q}v_{j}w_{j + q}$, $1 \le q \le L - 1$, of Theorem \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} (each lowers the level index by $q$). Let $T = \sum_{q = 1}^{L - 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Window Sugawara identity.)} For every $L$, exactly,
\[
T = \sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1).
\]
For $L = 2M$, with $k = j - M$, the half-integer weights $k + \tfrac12$, the sea $k < 0$ filled, $H = \sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} + \tfrac12M^{2}$ and $\mathcal{Q} = \hat N - M$, this reads $H = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + T$: $H$ vanishes on the sea and is at least $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. There is no edge correction, although $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ is the edge operator of the stored result. An energy $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j}n_{j}$ equals $aT + g(\hat N)$ for a real $a$ and a function $g$ if and only if $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + b$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Linear dispersion and the phase flow.)} $[H, \rho_{q}^{*}] = q\rho_{q}^{*}$ and $[H, \rho_{q}] = -q\rho_{q}$ exactly. In a tower level $\Cl(L, L + 2)$ with kernel bivector $J = g_{1}g_{2}$ ($J^{2} = -1$, commuting with every plane generator), $e^{JtH} = e^{JtM^{2}/2}\prod_{k}\bigl(1 + (e^{Jt(k + 1/2)} - 1)n_{k}\bigr)$ is unitary for real $t$ and $e^{JtH}\rho_{q}^{*}e^{-JtH} = e^{Jqt}\rho_{q}^{*}$: every density wave of wave number $q$ turns at frequency $q$ with the unit $J$, whatever its position in the window.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The band of the null vacuum.)} On a horizon generator, with $P = I_{4}\,d/du$, the null vacuum $\omega_{0}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator} and the band modes $g_{k} = h_{k}\otimes\eta$ of width $\Delta$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi), $\ip{g_{k}}{Pg_{l}} = \delta_{kl}\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$: the compression of $P$ to the span of the band modes has the half-integer weights $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$, and on the window $k = -M, \dots, M - 1$ its second quantisation is $\Delta\sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} = \Delta(H - \tfrac12M^{2})$. The restriction of $\omega_{0}$ to the window is the sea, the ground state of $H$, with $\mathcal{Q} = 0$ and $\rho_{q}$ annihilating it. On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of the infinite band, $H_{\infty} = \sum_{k \ge 0}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k} - \sum_{k < 0}(k + \tfrac12)(1 - n_{k})$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty} = \sum_{k \ge 0}n_{k} - \sum_{k < 0}(1 - n_{k})$ are finite sums on each vector, and on $\mathcal{D}$
\[
H_{\infty} = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q} = \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}q\,b_{q}^{*}b_{q}, \qquad b_{q} = \rho_{q}/\sqrt q ,
\]
with $[b_{q}, b_{q'}^{*}] = \delta_{qq'}$ on $\mathcal{D}$: in each charge sector the energy is that of free bosons of frequency $q$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Luttinger coupling.)} Take two families of window modes, $R$ with weights $k + \tfrac12$ and sea $k < 0$, and $L$ with weights $-(k + \tfrac12)$ and sea $k \ge 0$, with density modes $\rho_{R, q} = \sum_{k}v_{R, k}w_{R, k + q}$ and $\rho_{L, q} = \sum_{k}v_{L, k + q}w_{L, k}$, both lowering the energy by $q$. For a finite set $S$ of wave numbers and real $g_{4, q}$, $g_{2, q}$ ($q \in S$) with $|g_{2, q}| < 1 + g_{4, q}$, let
\[
H = H_{R} + H_{L} + \sum_{q \in S}\Bigl[g_{4, q}\bigl(\rho_{R, q}^{*}\rho_{R, q} + \rho_{L, q}^{*}\rho_{L, q}\bigr) + g_{2, q}\bigl(\rho_{R, q}\rho_{L, q} + \rho_{L, q}^{*}\rho_{R, q}^{*}\bigr)\Bigr],
\]
$r_{q}$ the root of $g_{2, q}r^{2} - 2(1 + g_{4, q})r + g_{2, q} = 0$ with $|r_{q}| < 1$, $\beta_{q}^{*} = \rho_{R, q}^{*} + r_{q}\rho_{L, q}$, $\gamma_{q}^{*} = \rho_{L, q}^{*} + r_{q}\rho_{R, q}$ and $\omega_{q} = q\sqrt{(1 + g_{4, q})^{2} - g_{2, q}^{2}}$. On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of both infinite seas, $H$ maps $\mathcal{D}$ into itself and
\[
[H, \beta_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\beta_{q}^{*}, \qquad [H, \gamma_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\gamma_{q}^{*} ;
\]
the Heisenberg equations of the density modes close linearly, with real coefficients. On finite windows the same relations hold exactly on every vector whose two families are edge-clean at depth $\max S$, and do not hold on every vector off that subspace (the check exhibits one where they fail; on others, such as the vector with both families empty, they still hold).
\end{enumerate}
All clauses are proved. \emph{Reading.} The kinetic energy of fermions with linear dispersion is already, on every finite window and with no edge correction, the quadratic form of the density waves plus the charge term $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$; the finite size shows only in the commutators of the density modes, not in this energy. Density-density couplings keep the dynamics quadratic in the density waves and so solvable.
synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity.technical:
On a window of tower planes, let $\rho_{q}$ move one fermion $q$ levels down. The sum $T = \sum_{q}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$ equals $\sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$ exactly, as an identity in the algebra, on every window: the kinetic energy of fermions with equally spaced levels is the quadratic form of the density waves, and with the levels $k + \tfrac12$ about the sea it is $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + T$, the Sugawara (Kronig) form with the charge term. The finite window shows only in $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$, which is an edge operator; the energy identity itself has no edge term. The identity needs the linear dispersion: an energy is a multiple of $T$ plus a function of the number exactly when its levels are equally spaced.

Each density wave of wave number $q$ raises the energy by exactly $q$, wherever it sits, so with the kernel unit $J$ of a tower level the flow $e^{JtH}$ turns $\rho_{q}^{*}$ at frequency $q$. On a horizon generator, compressing the null momentum to the band modes of width $\Delta$ gives exactly the weights $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$, the half-integer offset being the band centre; the null vacuum restricted to the bands is the sea, the ground state, and on the finite excitations of the infinite band the energy is $\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2} + \sum_{q}q\,b_{q}^{*}b_{q}$ with canonical $b_{q}$.

Coupling two families of opposite orientation through their densities, with constants $g_{4}$ (within a family) and $g_{2}$ (between them) on finitely many wave numbers, keeps the Heisenberg equations of the densities linear; real normal modes $\rho_{R}^{*} + r\rho_{L}$ have frequencies $q\sqrt{(1 + g_{4})^{2} - g_{2}^{2}}$. On windows this holds exactly on the vectors that are edge-clean at the coupled depth.
synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity.lay: Fermions on a line whose energy levels are equally spaced have a hidden description: their energy can be rewritten exactly as the energy of ripples in their density, plus a term that only counts how many fermions were added or removed. This is the core of how fermions in one dimension turn into bosons. The result shows that the rewriting holds exactly even for a finite stretch of levels, with nothing to correct at the ends, provided the spacing is even. Each ripple then carries an energy proportional to its wavelength number, which is what a sound wave does. When the ripples of two streams moving in opposite directions push on each other, the motion stays simple: new combined ripples form with a changed common speed (slower or faster, depending on the two couplings), and the problem can still be solved exactly. On a horizon line the lowest-energy state the series uses is the state with no ripples.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} the $v_{j}, w_{j}$ satisfy $v_{j}^{2} = w_{j}^{2} = 0$, $\{v_{j}, w_{k}\} = \delta_{jk}$ and distinct planes' generators anticommute; $n_{j} = v_{j}w_{j}$ are commuting idempotents with $[n_{l}, v_{j}] = \delta_{lj}v_{j}$ and $[n_{l}, w_{j}] = -\delta_{lj}w_{j}$, and $\hat Nw_{j} = w_{j}(\hat N - 1)$. Theorem \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} gives, on a window, $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = \sum_{k < q}n_{k} - \sum_{k \ge L - q}n_{k}$, $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q'}] = 0$, and for $q \ne q'$ a cross commutator $[\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ supported on the lowest and highest $\max(q, q')$ modes that annihilates every vector edge-clean at that depth (the lowest $\max(q, q')$ modes filled, the highest empty).

\emph{(i)} Moving $w_{j}$ past $v_{j'}$, $\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q} = \sum_{j, j'}v_{j + q}w_{j}v_{j'}w_{j' + q} = \sum_{j}n_{j + q} - \sum_{j, j'}v_{j + q}v_{j'}w_{j}w_{j' + q}$. Summed over $q \ge 1$, the first term counts each $n_{l}$ once for every $q$ with $1 \le q \le l$, giving $\sum_{l}l\,n_{l}$. In the second, write $\alpha = j + q$, $\beta = j'$, $\gamma = j$, $\delta = j' + q$: the sum over $q \ge 1$ and $j, j'$ is the sum $X$ of $v_{\alpha}v_{\beta}w_{\gamma}w_{\delta}$ over the quadruples in the window with $\alpha + \beta = \gamma + \delta$ and $\alpha > \gamma$, each once. Let $S$ be the same sum over all quadruples with $\alpha + \beta = \gamma + \delta$. Renaming $\gamma \leftrightarrow \delta$ preserves the index set and $w_{\gamma}w_{\delta} = -w_{\delta}w_{\gamma}$, so $S = -S = 0$. The part with $\alpha < \gamma$ has $\beta > \delta$, and the renaming $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta) \mapsto (\beta, \alpha, \delta, \gamma)$ maps it onto the part with $\alpha > \gamma$, with the sign $(-1)^{2} = 1$: it equals $X$. The part with $\alpha = \gamma$ (then $\beta = \delta$) is $D = \sum_{\alpha, \beta}v_{\alpha}v_{\beta}w_{\alpha}w_{\beta} = -\sum_{\alpha}v_{\alpha}\hat Nw_{\alpha} = -\sum_{\alpha}v_{\alpha}w_{\alpha}(\hat N - 1) = -\hat N(\hat N - 1)$. So $0 = 2X + D$, $X = \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$ and $T = \sum_{l}l\,n_{l} - \tfrac12\hat N(\hat N - 1)$. With $j = k + M$, $H = \sum_{j}j\,n_{j} - (M - \tfrac12)\hat N + \tfrac12M^{2} = T + \tfrac12\hat N^{2} - M\hat N + \tfrac12M^{2} = T + \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. On the sea every $\rho_{q}$ vanishes (a fermion at $j + q$ would have to drop to an empty level $j < j + q$, and in the sea every level below a filled one is filled) and $\mathcal{Q} = 0$, so $H = 0$ there; $T$ is a sum of elements $\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q}$, nonnegative in every state, so $H \ge \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}^{2}$. If $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + b$, then $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{j}n_{j} = aT + \tfrac{a}{2}\hat N(\hat N - 1) + b\hat N$. Conversely, on the one-particle vector $v_{j}\Omega_{0}$ ($\Omega_{0} = \prod_{l}w_{l}v_{l}$ the empty projector), $T$ acts as $j$ by the identity and $g(\hat N)$ as $g(1)$, so $\varepsilon_{j} = aj + g(1)$. The check verifies the identity as an equality of elements of $\Cl(L, L)$ for $L = 1, \dots, 6$, the sea form for even $L$, the one-particle values of $T$, and that weights $j^{2}$ are not of this form for $L \ge 3$.

\emph{(ii)} From $[n_{l}, v_{j}w_{j + q}] = (\delta_{lj} - \delta_{l, j + q})v_{j}w_{j + q}$, $[\sum_{l}\varepsilon_{l}n_{l}, \rho_{q}] = \sum_{j}(\varepsilon_{j} - \varepsilon_{j + q})v_{j}w_{j + q} = -q\rho_{q}$ for $\varepsilon_{l} = l + c$, and the adjoint gives $[H, \rho_{q}^{*}] = q\rho_{q}^{*}$. In $\Cl(L, L + 2)$, $J$ commutes with the plane generators and $J^{2} = -1$, so $e^{Jt\varepsilon n_{k}} = 1 + (e^{Jt\varepsilon} - 1)n_{k}$, the factors commute, and $(e^{JtH})^{*} = e^{-JtH}$ ($J^{*} = -J$, $H^{*} = H$). Since $J$ commutes with $H$ and $\rho_{q}^{*}$, $\operatorname{ad}(JtH)\rho_{q}^{*} = Jqt\,\rho_{q}^{*}$, and summing the exponential series of $\operatorname{ad}$ gives $e^{JtH}\rho_{q}^{*}e^{-JtH} = e^{Jqt}\rho_{q}^{*}$. The check verifies the commutators for $L = 2, 3, 4$, unitarity, and the phase $e^{Jqt}$ at the Pythagorean point $e^{Jt/2} = \tfrac35 + \tfrac45J$, and that weights $j^{2}$ give no such relation.

\emph{(iii)} In the $P$-spectral representation $h_{k}$ is $\Delta^{-1/2}$ times the indicator of $[k\Delta, (k + 1)\Delta)$, so $\ip{h_{k}}{Ph_{l}} = 0$ for $k \ne l$ (disjoint supports) and $\ip{h_{k}}{Ph_{k}} = \Delta^{-1}\int_{k\Delta}^{(k + 1)\Delta}p\,dp = \Delta(k + \tfrac12)$; tensoring with the unit vector $\eta$ changes nothing. The compression is therefore diagonal on the $g_{k}$ with these weights, and its second quantisation on the window is $\Delta\sum_{k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{k}$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi) the restriction of $\omega_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii), symbol $\chi_{(-\infty, 0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$) to the band modes is the product state with $n_{k} = 1$ for $k < 0$ and $0$ for $k \ge 0$, the sea, on which $H = 0$ and $\rho_{q} = 0$ by (i). On $\mathcal{D}$: a vector $\psi = x\Omega$ with $x$ a polynomial in modes of $[-K, K)$ is a combination of occupation vectors that agree with the sea outside $[-K, K)$. On such a vector $\rho_{q}$ acts only through terms $v_{k}w_{k + q}$ with $k \ge -K$ empty and $k + q < K$ filled, so it vanishes for $q \ge 2K$ and keeps the support in $[-K, K)$; $\rho_{q}^{*}$ acts through terms $v_{k + q}w_{k}$ with $k < K$ filled and $k + q \ge -K$ empty, so its result agrees with the sea outside $[-K - q, K + q)$. Hence on $\psi$ every operator in the display involves only modes of the window $[-3K, 3K)$ and coincides there with the window operators of (i) for $M = 3K$; $H_{\infty}\psi = H\psi$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}\psi = \mathcal{Q}\psi$ because the modes outside the window contribute $0$ to the normal-ordered sums on $\psi$. Identity (i) is an identity in the algebra of the window, so it holds in the representation of $\omega_{0}$, and gives $H_{\infty}\psi = (\tfrac12\mathcal{Q}_{\infty}^{2} + \sum_{q \ge 1}\rho_{q}^{*}\rho_{q})\psi$, the sum finite on $\psi$. The canonical relations $[\rho_{q}, \rho_{q'}^{*}] = q\delta_{qq'}$ on $\mathcal{D}$ are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi). The check computes the band means $\Delta(k + \tfrac12)$ exactly for three widths and eight bands, the band occupations of the null vacuum, and $H = 0$, $\rho_{q} = 0$ on the window sea.

\emph{(iv)} The relabelling $k \mapsto -1 - k$ of the $L$ family maps its weights $-(k + \tfrac12)$, its sea $k \ge 0$ and its density modes $\rho_{L, q}$ to the weights, sea and density modes of an $R$ family, so the results above hold for both families. Operators of different families commute (even elements on disjoint planes). For one $q \in S$ and a vector $\psi$, compute with $[\rho^{*}_{q'}\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = \rho_{q'}^{*}[\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}^{*}]$ (as $[\rho_{q'}^{*}, \rho_{q}^{*}] = 0$) and $[\rho_{q'}^{*}\rho_{q'}, \rho_{q}] = [\rho_{q'}^{*}, \rho_{q}]\rho_{q'}$:
\[
[H, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] = q\rho_{R, q}^{*} + \sum_{q' \in S}\bigl(g_{4, q'}\rho_{R, q'}^{*}[\rho_{R, q'}, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] + g_{2, q'}[\rho_{R, q'}, \rho_{R, q}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'}\bigr),
\]
\[
[H, \rho_{L, q}] = -q\rho_{L, q} - \sum_{q' \in S}\bigl(g_{4, q'}[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'} + g_{2, q'}[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{R, q'}^{*}\bigr).
\]
On $\mathcal{D}$ the brackets are $q\delta_{qq'}$ and every operator maps $\mathcal{D}$ into itself ($S$ is finite), so $[H, \rho_{R, q}^{*}] = q(1 + g_{4, q})\rho_{R, q}^{*} + qg_{2, q}\rho_{L, q}$ and $[H, \rho_{L, q}] = -q(1 + g_{4, q})\rho_{L, q} - qg_{2, q}\rho_{R, q}^{*}$. Then $[H, \beta_{q}^{*}] = q\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr)\rho_{R, q}^{*} + q\bigl(g_{2, q} - r_{q}(1 + g_{4, q})\bigr)\rho_{L, q}$, which is a multiple of $\beta_{q}^{*}$ exactly when $g_{2, q} - r_{q}(1 + g_{4, q}) = r_{q}\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr)$, the stated quadratic. Its roots are real and distinct with product $1$ when $|g_{2, q}| < 1 + g_{4, q}$; the one of modulus less than $1$ is $r_{q} = \bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - \sqrt{(1 + g_{4, q})^{2} - g_{2, q}^{2}}\bigr)/g_{2, q}$ ($r_{q} = 0$ if $g_{2, q} = 0$), and the multiple is $q\bigl((1 + g_{4, q}) - r_{q}g_{2, q}\bigr) = \omega_{q}$. Exchanging the roles of $R$ and $L$ gives $[H, \gamma_{q}^{*}] = \omega_{q}\gamma_{q}^{*}$. On a window, let $\psi$ be edge-clean at depth $\max S$ in both families (for $L$, in the relabelled order). The brackets in the displays act either on $\psi$, or on $\rho_{L, q'}\psi$ or $\rho_{R, q'}^{*}\psi$, which have the other family's occupations of $\psi$, or, for $[\rho_{L, q}, \rho_{L, q'}^{*}]\rho_{L, q'}\psi$, on $\rho_{L, q'}\psi$, which is still edge-clean in $L$ (a lowering density mode cannot fill an empty edge level of its own family or empty a filled one); so by the stored edge identities every bracket acts as $q\delta_{qq'}$ there and the computation above holds on $\psi$. The check verifies $[H, \beta^{*}]\psi = \tfrac65\beta^{*}\psi$ and $[H, \gamma^{*}]\psi = \tfrac65\gamma^{*}\psi$ for $S = \{1\}$, $g_{4} = \tfrac12$, $g_{2} = \tfrac{9}{10}$, $r = \tfrac13$, on all sixteen depth-one edge-clean vectors of two four-mode families, and that the relation fails on a vector that is not edge-clean.

synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.formal:
Fields at a point and all their derivatives generate the jet algebra: $A^{a}_{\mu}$ and $B^{a}$ even, the ghosts $c^{a}$ and antighosts $\bar c^{a}$ odd (generators of a Grassmann algebra, the Clifford algebra of a form that vanishes), the coupling $g$ and gauge parameter $\xi$ even constants; $\partial_\mu$ acts by shifting the jet index. The gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ of the minimal massive composite, Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} has basis $T_a$ with $[T_a, T_b] = f_{ab}{}^{c}T_c$. The vector potential is $A = T_a A^{a}$, $A^{a} = A^{a}_{\mu}\gamma^{\mu}$ a vector field of the spacetime algebra, $\nabla = \gamma^{\mu}\partial_\mu$, and the field strength is the bivector $F^{a} = \nabla\wedge A^{a} + \tfrac{g}{2}f_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}\wedge A^{c}$. The BRST differential $s$ is the odd derivation, acting from the left and commuting with every $\partial_\mu$, with
\[
sA^{a} = \nabla c^{a} + g f_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}c^{c}, \qquad sc^{a} = -\tfrac{g}{2}f_{bc}{}^{a}c^{b}c^{c}, \qquad s\bar c^{a} = B^{a}, \qquad sB^{a} = 0 .
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The algebra as bivectors; computed.)} The twelve bivectors $T_{1,2,3} = \tfrac12 e_{12}, \tfrac12 e_{20}, \tfrac12 e_{01}$ on $e_0, e_1, e_2$, the eight traceless bivectors of the $e_3, \dots, e_8$ block commuting with $J = e_{34} + e_{56} + e_{78}$, and $T_{12} = \tfrac12 J$, in $\Cl(9,0)$, close under the commutator into $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$: $58$ nonzero rational structure constants, $J$ spanning the centre, a derived algebra $[\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{g}]$ of dimension $11$, a positive-definite ad-invariant form $\kappa_{ab} = -\langle T_aT_b\rangle_0$, and an eight-dimensional block whose adjoint representation has one-dimensional commutant. This realisation is isomorphic to, not identical with, the realisation on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}, and it does not fix how the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ (hypercharge) acts on matter; the pure gauge differential depends only on the isomorphism class.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Nilpotency; proved.)} For any Lie algebra, $s^2 = 0$ on the whole jet algebra, for every $g$. The check confirms $s^2 = 0$ exactly on all $300$ generators $A^{a}_{\mu}$, $c^{a}$ with at most one derivative for the algebra of (i), as polynomials in $g$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What nilpotency needs; computed.)} Replacing $\tfrac{g}{2}$ by $2g$ in $sc$ leaves $s^2c = 0$ but gives $s^2A^{a}_{\mu} = 3(D_\mu Y)^{a}$ with $Y = sc$ the correct ghost variation (in general the residual is $(2h - 1)D_\mu Y$ for $sc = -hg[c, c]$); dropping the term $gf_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}c^{c}$ gives $s^2A^{a}_{\mu} = \partial_\mu(sc^{a})$, nonzero on the $44$ components of the eleven non-abelian generators; shifting one antisymmetric pair of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ structure constants (so that the Jacobi identity fails) gives $s^2 \neq 0$ on $30$ of the $60$ underived generators.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Covariance and invariance; proved.)} $sF^{a} = g f_{bc}{}^{a}F^{b}c^{c}$, so for every ad-invariant $\kappa$ the scalar and pseudoscalar densities $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_0$ and $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_4$ are $s$-invariant. The check confirms the first identity for all twelve components, the ad-invariance of $\kappa$ and its failure for a perturbed $\kappa$, and the invariance of both densities on the $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ block exactly, with a perturbed $\kappa$ breaking the scalar one.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Gauge fixing; proved.)} With $\Psi = \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}(\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{b})$,
\[
s\Psi = \kappa_{ab}\big(B^{a}\,\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{a}B^{b} - \bar c^{a}\,\nabla\cdot(Dc)^{b}\big), \qquad (Dc)^{b} = \nabla c^{b} + g f_{cd}{}^{b}A^{c}c^{d},
\]
so $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_0 + s\Psi$, the Yang-Mills density with a covariant gauge fixing and the Faddeev-Popov operator $\nabla\cdot D$, is $s$-invariant; the check confirms the expansion and $s(s\Psi) = 0$ for the full algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} The non-abelian gauge fields of $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ admit the standard covariant BRST gauge fixing at the level of local fields: the ghost's covariant derivative is forced (iii), and the differential is nilpotent for every coupling. The differential involves no imaginary unit and no inner product, so it is compatible with the unit $I_4$ and is independent of the Krein-form premise (KF); that premise and the quartet mechanism concern the state space, not the differential. Standard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(i)); transport-absent. Not addressed: the Goldstone and doublet terms of the differential, the operator charge of the interacting theory, its renormalisation, anomalies and the Gribov ambiguity, which confines the construction to perturbation theory (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv); the lattice computation \claimref{synthesis.non-abelian-gauge-fixing-has-gribov-copies-and-the-weak-rotor-lattice-with-doublets-has-a-perimeter-law}).
synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.technical:
The problem asks for the interacting BRST charge of the gluons and the W and Z, in which the ghost's covariant derivative acts on the gauge field. At the level of local fields this is a differential on the algebra generated by the fields and their derivatives. Here the gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ of the minimal massive composite is written, up to isomorphism, by bivectors of $\Cl(9,0)$: the weak factor as half the bivectors on $e_0, e_1, e_2$ (the rotor generators already used on the stored lattice), colour as the eight traceless bivectors of the $e_3, \dots, e_8$ block that commute with a complex structure $J$, and the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ as $J/2$. This is isomorphic to the stored realisation on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, not identical with it, and it does not fix the hypercharge embedding, which the pure gauge differential does not see; with matter or Goldstone fields it would matter. The structure constants are rational and exact, and the commutant test identifies the eight-dimensional block as simple, hence $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.

The vector potential is a Lie-algebra-valued vector field of the spacetime algebra and its field strength is the bivector $F = \nabla\wedge A + \tfrac{g}{2}[A\wedge A]$. The differential acts as a gauge transformation with the ghost as parameter, $sA = Dc$, and on the ghost as $sc = -\tfrac{g}{2}[c, c]$. Squaring to zero on the ghost is the Jacobi identity; on the vector potential it needs, in addition, the factor $\tfrac12$ and the covariant term, and the exact computation shows each failing when altered. Because $s$ commutes with derivatives, nilpotency on the underived fields gives it on every derivative; the check confirms it directly up to first derivatives (300 generators), as a polynomial identity in the coupling.

The field strength transforms covariantly, so both invariant densities, the Yang-Mills scalar $\langle FF\rangle_0$ and the pseudoscalar $\langle FF\rangle_4$, are BRST invariant for any ad-invariant form. A gauge-fixing fermion $\Psi$ adds the exact term $s\Psi$, which contains the covariant gauge condition, the Gaussian weight $\tfrac{\xi}{2}B^2$ and the Faddeev-Popov term $-\bar c\,\nabla\cdot Dc$; invariance of the sum is then nilpotency. All of this is standard BRST, recomputed in the series' algebra; nothing in it comes from transport. The Goldstone and doublet terms of the differential are not included, and the construction is perturbative (Gribov copies, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv)). The differential has rational coefficients, so the unit $I_4$ never enters, and it needs no inner product; positivity of the physical states is a statement about the state space (the Krein-form premise and the quartet mechanism), which this result does not touch.
synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.lay: To describe the strong and weak forces as quantum fields in a way that respects relativity, one adds fictitious ghost fields and a bookkeeping operation that must give zero when applied twice. This result writes that operation for the full set of the series' force fields (without the Higgs fields' part), with the force fields' symmetry written as plane elements of a Clifford algebra, and checks exactly that it gives zero twice, for any strength of the force. It also shows that each ingredient is needed: removing the term in which the ghost feels the force field, or changing a factor of one half, spoils it. The usual energy of the force fields and the usual way of fixing the gauge pass the test. Nothing here is new physics; it confirms that the series' algebra carries the standard construction.

synthesis.field-level-brst-of-the-two-do.formal:
In the jet algebra of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-of-the-derived-gauge-fields-is-nilpotent}, with the gauge algebra $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} realised there by bivectors ($T_{1}, T_{2}, T_{3} = \tfrac12e_{12}, \tfrac12e_{20}, \tfrac12e_{01}$ in $\Cl(3,0)$ on $e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}$, colour on $e_{3}, \dots, e_{8}$, $T_{12} = \tfrac12J$), the structure constants $f_{ab}{}^{c}$ and the invariant form $\kappa_{ab} = -\langle T_{a}T_{b}\rangle_{0}$, add the two doublets of the scalar sector: each is an even element $\phi = \phi^{0} + \phi^{1}e_{12} + \phi^{2}e_{02} + \phi^{3}e_{01}$ of $\Cl(3,0)$, with $\rho(T_{a})\phi = T_{a}\phi$ ($a = 1, 2, 3$), colour acting by $0$, and $\rho(T_{12})\phi = y\,\phi e_{12}$ for a rational $y \ne 0$ (the normalisation of hypercharge); $\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \langle\widetilde{\phi}\psi\rangle_{0}$. Write $\phi = v + h$ with $v$ constant (the vacuum) and $h = (h^{1}, \dots, h^{8})$ even jet symbols, $\rho(c) = c^{a}\rho(T_{a})$, $D_\mu\phi = \partial_\mu h + g\rho(A^{a}_{\mu}T_{a})\phi$, $W_{a} = \rho(T_{a})v$ and $\Gamma_{ab} = \langle W_{a}, W_{b}\rangle$. Extend the stored differential by
\[
sh = -g\,\rho(c)(v + h), \qquad s(h_{J}) = \partial_{J}(sh).
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The doublets; proved.)} $\rho$ is a representation of the twelve generators by maps antisymmetric for $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, for every $y$; with hypercharge acting on the left it is not.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Nilpotency; proved.)} $s^{2} = 0$ on the whole jet algebra, for every constant $v$, every $y$ and every $g$; with $sh = +g\rho(c)(v + h)$ it fails.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Invariance; proved.)} $s(D_\mu\phi) = -g\rho(c)D_\mu\phi$; $s$ annihilates $\tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle$ and every polynomial in $|\phi_{1}|^{2}$, $|\phi_{2}|^{2}$, $\langle\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}\rangle$, $\langle\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}e_{12}\rangle$, so with the stored Yang-Mills density in the canonical normalisation, $\mathcal{L} = \tfrac12\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0} + \tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle - V$ is $s$-invariant for every such $V$ ($\tfrac12\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0} = -\tfrac14F^{a}_{\mu\nu}F^{b\,\mu\nu}$).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The 't Hooft gauge; proved.)} For $\Psi_{\xi} = \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}\big(\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{b}\big) - \xi g\,\bar c^{a}\langle W_{a}, h\rangle$, with $F^{a} = \nabla\cdot A^{a} - \xi g\,\kappa^{ab}\langle W_{b}, h\rangle$,
\[
s\Psi_{\xi} = \kappa_{ab}B^{a}F^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}\kappa_{ab}B^{a}B^{b} - \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}\,\nabla\cdot(Dc)^{b} - \xi g^{2}\,\bar c^{a}\langle W_{a}, \rho(c)(v + h)\rangle, \qquad s(s\Psi_{\xi}) = 0,
\]
and after eliminating $B$ ($B^{a} = -F^{a}/\xi$, giving $-\tfrac{1}{2\xi}\kappa_{ab}F^{a}F^{b}$) the terms of $\tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle - \tfrac{1}{2\xi}\kappa_{ab}F^{a}F^{b}$ bilinear in $A$ and $h$ are exactly $g\,\partial_\mu\big(A^{a\mu}\langle W_{a}, h\rangle\big)$, a total derivative, for every $v$ and $\xi$; with the opposite sign of the 't Hooft term they are not a total derivative.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Masses; proved, computed.)} With the normalisation of (iii), the vector quadratic form at $\xi = 1$ is $-\tfrac12\kappa_{ab}\,\partial_\mu A^{a}_{\nu}\partial^{\mu}A^{b\nu}$ up to a total derivative (Feynman type; with the density $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0}$ this happens at $\xi = \tfrac12$ instead). Suppose $V = 0$, or $v$ is a stationary point of the invariant potential $V$; then $\mathrm{Hess}\,V(v)$ annihilates every $W_{a}$ (differentiate $\langle\nabla V(\phi), \rho(T_{a})\phi\rangle = 0$ at $v$), and off a stationary point there is a tadpole. Under this hypothesis the squared masses of the vectors, the ghosts and the Goldstone modes are the eigenvalues of $g^{2}\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$, $\xi g^{2}\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$ and $\xi g^{2}W\kappa^{-1}W^{\mathsf T}$ (on the eight scalars), the potential adding nothing on the Goldstone directions; the nonzero ones agree with multiplicity, so at $\xi = 1$ every massive vector, its Goldstone mode and its ghosts share one mass. For the neutral aligned vacuum $v = (v_{1}, 0, 0, 0), (v_{2}, 0, 0, 0)$ (Goldstone rank $3$, as stored), the nonzero eigenvalues of $\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$ equal to $v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2}$ (twice) and $(v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2})(1 + \tfrac43y^{2})$; computed at $v_{1} = 1$, $v_{2} = 2$, $y = \tfrac12$: $\det(t - \kappa^{-1}\Gamma) = t^{9}(t - 5)^{2}(t - \tfrac{20}{3})$ and $\det(t - W\kappa^{-1}W^{\mathsf T}) = t^{5}(t - 5)^{2}(t - \tfrac{20}{3})$, the factor $t^{5}$ counting five massless scalars only for $V = 0$ (a potential gives the five non-Goldstone scalars their own masses).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Computed.)} (i) for $y = \tfrac12, \tfrac13$; (ii) on the $40$ generators $h^{i}_{J}$ with $|J| \le 1$ and the $72$ underived gauge, ghost and antighost generators, as polynomials in $g$ and eight formal vacuum components; (iii) on all $32$ components of $D\phi$, the kinetic term and the four invariants, with two non-invariant bilinears as controls; (iv) term by term, $256$ mixing monomials at $\xi = 1, 3$; (v) from the computed Lagrangian, the Feynman form of the vector kinetic term at $\xi = 1$ by Euler derivatives (and its failure for the unhalved density, which is of Feynman type at $\xi = \tfrac12$), and for a sample invariant potential stationary at the neutral aligned vacuum the vanishing gradient and the Hessian annihilating the three Goldstone directions (a shifted potential has a tadpole).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} With the differential extended to the scalar sector (nilpotent for every vacuum, the lemma (ii)), the 't Hooft-Feynman gauge with the series' two doublets is an exact gauge fixing in which the vector-Goldstone mixing cancels and the vectors, Goldstone modes and ghosts share their masses, the gauge in which the stored quartet result treats the massive vectors. The vacuum, and hence the breaking pattern, is an input here.
synthesis.field-level-brst-of-the-two-do.technical: The stored field-level BRST differential of the derived gauge fields left out the scalars. Here the series' two hypercharge-$\tfrac12$ doublets are written as even elements of $\Cl(3,0)$, with the weak bivectors acting on the left and hypercharge by a multiple of $e_{12}$ on the right, so the gauge algebra acts by real antisymmetric maps and no imaginary unit appears. The differential $sh = -g\rho(c)(v + h)$ around any constant vacuum $v$ squares to zero on all fields, the covariant derivative transforms covariantly, and the kinetic term and the four quadratic invariants of two doublets are BRST-invariant. The 't Hooft gauge-fixing fermion, which adds $-\xi g\,\bar c^{a}\langle\rho(T_{a})v, h\rangle$ to the covariant one, is exact, and its gauge-fixing function cancels the mixing between vectors and Goldstone modes up to a total derivative for every vacuum. In the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge, with the canonical normalisation of the Yang-Mills term and a vacuum that is a stationary point of the potential, the massive vectors, their Goldstone modes and their ghosts have one common mass matrix; for the neutral aligned vacuum the Goldstone map has rank three, as stored.
synthesis.field-level-brst-of-the-two-do.lay: In the series' version of the Standard Model, the forces have a mathematical bookkeeping device, BRST symmetry, that makes their quantum theory consistent; it had been written down for the force fields alone. Here it is extended to the two Higgs-like scalar fields of the series, written in geometric algebra as four-component quantities on which the weak force acts from one side and hypercharge from the other. The extended symmetry is consistent whatever value the scalars settle at, and in the standard gauge choice due to 't Hooft the unwanted mixing between the force fields and the would-be Goldstone particles cancels, while the massive force carriers, their Goldstone partners and the bookkeeping ghost fields all share the same masses. Which way the symmetry breaks is not decided here; it is put in by hand.

\emph{Setting.} The jet algebra, the total derivatives and the odd derivation $s$ on $A^{a}_{\mu}$, $c^{a}$, $ ar c^{a}$, $B^{a}$ are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-of-the-derived-gauge-fields-is-nilpotent}, with the gauge algebra of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} realised there by bivectors of $\Cl(9,0)$; here the even symbols $h^{i}_{J}$ ($i = 1, \dots, 8$, $J$ a multi-index) are added, with $\partial_\mu h^{i}_{J} = h^{i}_{J+\mu}$, and $s$ is extended by $s h^{i} = -g ig(ho(c)(v + h) ig)^{i}$, $s(h^{i}_{J}) = \partial_{J}(sh^{i})$, the vacuum components $v^{i}$ being constants ($\partial_\mu v = 0$, $sv = 0$). The two doublets are the scalar sector of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum} (eight real components, two hypercharge-$	frac12$ doublets), as in \claimref{synthesis.quartet-homotopy-makes-gluon-and-massive-vector-physical-states-positive-at-every-number-of-quanta}(v).

For a bivector $T$, $\widetilde{T} = -T$, so $\langle(T\phi)^{\sim}\psiangle_{0} = -\langle\widetilde{\phi}T\psiangle_{0}$ and, by cyclicity of the scalar part, $\langle(\phi T)^{\sim}\psiangle_{0} = -\langle T\widetilde{\phi}\psiangle_{0} = -\langle\widetilde{\phi}\,\psi Tangle_{0}$: both actions are antisymmetric for $\langle\cdot,\cdotangle$, which is the Euclidean form on the components. The check computes the twelve $8 	imes 8$ matrices from GA products and confirms $[ho_{a}, ho_{b}] = f_{ab}{}^{c}ho_{c}$ and antisymmetry for $y = 	frac12$ and $y = 	frac13$; hypercharge acting on the left instead gives four failures of the homomorphism property (it no longer commutes with $\su(2)$).

\emph{(ii).} $s^{2} = 	frac12[s, s]$ is an even derivation commuting with $\partial_\mu$, so it vanishes once it vanishes on the underived symbols; on $A$, $c$, $ ar c$, $B$ it vanishes by the stored theorem. On $h$, with $\phi = v + h$ and $s(c^{a}X) = (sc^{a})X - c^{a}sX$ for even $X$,
\[
s^{2}h = -g\,ho(sc)\phi + g\,ho(c^{a}T_{a})\,s\phi = 	frac{g^{2}}{2}f_{bc}{}^{a}c^{b}c^{c}ho_{a}\phi - g^{2}c^{a}c^{b}ho_{a}ho_{b}\phi = 	frac{g^{2}}{2}c^{b}c^{c} ig(f_{bc}{}^{a}ho_{a} - [ho_{b}, ho_{c}] ig)\phi = 0,
\]

synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.formal:
Let a floor of the tower carry $2N$ planes, with mode operators $a_k^{*}, a_k$ ($k = -N, \dots, N - 1$) obeying the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}, read as the right-moving modes of one chirality on a circle of $2N$ momenta in units of the circle's $2\pi/L$, with $n_k = a_k^{*}a_k$, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$, $\mathcal{N} = \sum_k n_k$ and $\rho(p) = \sum_{k,\,k+p} a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ (both indices in the window).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge and continuity; proved.)} $[\mathcal{N}, H] = 0$, $[\mathcal{N}, \rho(p)] = 0$ and $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$ exactly on every floor, for $1 \le |p| \le 2N - 1$; $\rho(\pm 2N) = 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The central term is an edge operator; proved.)} For $1 \le p \le 2N$,
\[
[\rho(p), \rho(-p)] = \sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k - \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k ,
\]
whose scalar part is zero; no floor carries a nonzero scalar central term.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The continuum value below the cut-off; proved.)} On the filled sea $\Omega$ ($n_k = 1$ for $k < 0$, $0$ otherwise), $\rho(-p)\Omega = 0$, $[\rho(-p), \rho(p)]\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$, and $\rho(p)\Omega$ is an eigenvector of $H$ at energy $E_\Omega + p$ with $\rho(-p)\rho(p)\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$. So $b_p = \rho(-p)/\sqrt{p}$ satisfies $[b_p, b_p^{*}] = 1$ on $\Omega$ exactly for $p \le N$, the continuum central term $p$ and the continuum one-loop density response (all spectral weight at energy $p$, total weight $p$) are reproduced exactly up to the cut-off, and above it the weight is $2N - p$. The value depends on the state at the window's edges: with the top mode also occupied, $[\rho(-1), \rho(1)]$ acts as $0$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No boost survives the conformal-energy cut; proved.)} In $\Cl(2,4)$ the commutant of the conformal Hamiltonian $\gamma_0e_+$ (the compact combination of $P_0 = \gamma_0n_\infty$ and $K_0 = \gamma_0n_0$, up to normalisation) among the fifteen bivectors is seven-dimensional; it meets the Lorentz bivectors in the span of the three rotations and contains no nonzero translation and no nonzero special conformal generator. So, if the floors are the conformal-energy cut-offs of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, every finite floor is invariant under the spatial rotations and not under any boost.
\item[(v)] \emph{(No weighting of the floors keeps a boost; merged from Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}(vii), 2 November 2026.)} The commutant $\mathfrak{k}$ of (iv) is closed under the commutator, and $\mathfrak{k}$ together with any one of the eight basis bivectors that anticommute with $\gamma_0e_+$ (among them the dilation $e_+e_-$), or of the boosts $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, the translations $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$ and the special conformal generators $\gamma_\mu n_0$, generates all fifteen bivectors (computed); for an arbitrary element outside $\mathfrak{k}$ the same follows from the irreducibility of the eight-dimensional complement under $\mathfrak{k}$ (argued). Hence on an irreducible unitary module, such as the attachment's one-particle helicity modules of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} (irreducibility cited), a bounded weighting $f(\gamma_0e_+)$ of the modes by conformal energy that commutes with one boost commutes with the whole conformal algebra and is a multiple of the identity (Schur's lemma, cited): no weighting of the floors, sharp or smooth, keeps a boost.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} As a regulator the floors keep the global Ward identity (charge conservation and the free continuity equation) exactly at every floor. The central term that makes the one-chirality density algebra a boson algebra, and that fixes the chiral fermion's vacuum polarisation and the two-dimensional chiral anomaly, is not a scalar on any floor (by the trace argument of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower}); it is an edge operator that equals its continuum value on the filled sea for every momentum up to the cut-off, the density analogue of the quasi-spin $[b, b^{*}] = 1 - 2k/n$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}. The regulator breaks Lorentz invariance at every finite floor, keeping only the compact part of the conformal algebra, and by (v) no smoothing of the cut-off restores a boost. A sharp cut-off on conformal energy also leaves terms in the regulated zero-point energy that match no local invariant, which a cut-off vanishing with its slope at the edge removes (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}); clauses (i) to (iii) concern the sharp cut-off only.
synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.technical:
The tower's finite floors are the natural candidate for a regulator native to the series: on the twistor attachment they are energy cut-offs. Nothing specific to the tower enters clauses (i) to (iii): they hold for any finite truncation of a chiral band, and the truncated-band origin of the central term is standard (Mattis and Lieb). This result tests what such a sharp cut-off keeps, on the computed model of a one-chirality field on a circle with $2N$ momentum modes taken from $2N$ tower planes, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$ and densities $\rho(p) = \sum_k a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$.

The global Ward identity survives exactly: the charge commutes with $H$ and with every density, and $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$, the free continuity equation of a chiral current, holds on every floor. The central term of the density algebra does not survive as a scalar: $[\rho(p), \rho(-p)]$ is the number in the top $p$ modes minus the number in the bottom $p$ modes, an edge operator with zero scalar part, as the trace argument of the no-CCR theorem requires. On the filled sea it equals $\min(p, 2N - p)$, so the continuum value $p$ (the Schwinger commutator term, the boson normalisation of bosonisation, and the weight of the chiral fermion's one-loop density response, all at energy exactly $p$) is reproduced exactly for $p \le N$ and falls linearly above the cut-off. With an excitation at the window's edge the value changes, so the central term holds on states with vacuum-like edges, as the quasi-spin reaches the CCR only on states of bounded number.

Lorentz invariance is not kept: in $\Cl(2,4)$ the commutant of the conformal Hamiltonian $\gamma_0e_+$ is the seven-dimensional compact algebra, which contains the three spatial rotations and no boost, translation or special conformal generator. A conformal-energy cut therefore regulates in one conformal frame; the four-dimensional loop integrals of the standard theory with a Lorentz-invariant regulator are not what the floors give. Nor does smoothing help: the commutant together with any one boost generates the whole conformal algebra, so on an irreducible module a weighting of the modes by conformal energy that commutes with a boost commutes with everything and is a constant (Schur's lemma); no weighting of the floors, sharp or smooth, keeps a boost (merged on 2 November 2026 from the regulator-free vacuum polarisation, where it was first stated).
synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.lay: A calculation in quantum field theory with loops needs a regulator, a way of cutting off the infinitely many high-energy modes. The series has a natural candidate: its tower is built floor by floor, each floor holding finitely many fermion modes, and on the series' link to spacetime the floors are energy cut-offs. This result tests that candidate, and with it any sharp cut-off on the number of modes, on a simple model, one chirality of a fermion moving around a circle. The floor keeps electric charge exactly and keeps the charge flowing correctly. The subtle quantum term that gives the vacuum its polarisability, and that underlies the anomaly of chiral fermions, cannot exist exactly on any finite floor; instead it appears at the floor's edges, and it takes exactly the right value for every wavelength longer than the cut-off, provided the modes near the cut-off are in their vacuum state. The price is relativity: a floor is defined by one notion of energy and is unchanged by rotations but not by boosts. Smoothing the cut-off does not help: no gradual weighting of the floors by energy restores the boosts.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit} the planes of a floor give mode operators with $\{a_j, a_k^{*}\} = \delta_{jk}$, $a_j^2 = 0$; distinct planes anticommute in the algebra, so no ordering signs need inserting. Label the $2N$ planes of a floor by $k = -N, \dots, N - 1$ and read $k$ as the momentum of a right-moving mode of one chirality on a circle (in units of $2\pi/L$); this labelling is the model, not a premise. Write $n_k = a_k^{*}a_k$, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$, $\mathcal{N} = \sum_k n_k$ and $\rho(p) = \sum_k a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ over the $k$ with $k$ and $k + p$ in the window, so $\rho(p)^{*} = \rho(-p)$ and $\rho(\pm 2N) = 0$ (no pair of window indices differs by $2N$).

\emph{(i).} From the CAR, $[n_j, a_{l}^{*}a_k] = (\delta_{jl} - \delta_{jk})\,a_l^{*}a_k$. Hence $[H, a_{k+p}^{*}a_k] = ((k + p) - k)\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_k = p\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ and $[\mathcal{N}, a_{k+p}^{*}a_k] = 0$ term by term, so $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$ and $[\mathcal{N}, \rho(p)] = 0$ with no boundary correction, and $[\mathcal{N}, H] = 0$ since both are sums of commuting numbers. For $1 \le |p| \le 2N - 1$ the sum defining $\rho(p)$ is not empty, so $\rho(p) \ne 0$. The check confirms these identities as algebra elements for $N = 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(ii).} Using $[a_{k+p}^{*}a_k, a_{l-p}^{*}a_l] = \delta_{k,l-p}\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_l - \delta_{l,k+p}\,a_{l-p}^{*}a_k$ and summing over window indices, the terms with $l = k + p$ give $\sum_k (n_{k+p} - n_k)$ over the $k$ for which both $k$ and $k + p$ lie in the window, that is $k \in \{-N, \dots, N - 1 - p\}$ for $1 \le p \le 2N$. Shifting the first sum, this is $\sum_{k = -N + p}^{N - 1} n_k - \sum_{k = -N}^{N - 1 - p} n_k$, and the common terms cancel, leaving $\sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k - \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k$ (for $p > N$ the two ranges overlap and the same cancellation holds, leaving the same expression). Each $n_k$ has scalar part $\tfrac12$ in the floor's algebra and the two sums have $p$ terms each, so the scalar part is zero; this is the trace argument of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower}, which forbids any commutator on a floor from having a nonzero scalar part. The check confirms the identity and the vanishing scalar part for $N = 1, 2, 3$ and every $p \le 2N$.

\emph{(iii).} On $\Omega$ the modes $k < 0$ are filled and $k \ge 0$ empty. A term $a_{k-p}^{*}a_k$ of $\rho(-p)$ ($p \ge 1$) needs $k$ filled and $k - p$ empty, impossible when $k < 0$, so $\rho(-p)\Omega = 0$. By (ii), $[\rho(-p), \rho(p)] = \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k - \sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k$ acts on $\Omega$ as the number of filled modes among the bottom $p$ minus the number among the top $p$: for $p \le N$ these are $p$ and $0$; for $N < p \le 2N$ they are $N$ and $p - N$. In both cases the value is $\min(p, 2N - p)$. By (i), $\rho(p)\Omega$ is an eigenvector of $H$ with eigenvalue $E_\Omega + p$, and $\rho(-p)\rho(p)\Omega = [\rho(-p), \rho(p)]\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$, which is the squared norm of $\rho(p)\Omega$ for the floor's inner product. So the spectral measure of $\rho(p)$ in $\Omega$ is a single point at energy $p$ of weight $\min(p, 2N - p)$; the one-loop density response of the free field (the particle-hole bubble, exact for a free field) is determined by it. In the continuum (the CAR limit, with the sea filled below every momentum) the same computation gives weight $p$ for every $p$, the central term of the density algebra (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-schwinger-term-and-mattis-lieb-density-algebra}: Schwinger's commutator term, and the boson algebra of Tomonaga and of Mattis and Lieb). Hence the floor reproduces the continuum exactly for $p \le N$, and $b_p = \rho(-p)/\sqrt{p}$ obeys $[b_p, b_p^{*}] = 1$ on $\Omega$ there. With the top mode also occupied, (ii) at $p = 1$ gives $n_{N-1} - n_{-N} = 1 - 1 = 0$, so the value is not a property of the algebra alone but of the state at the edges; the check confirms all of (iii) for $N = 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(iv).} Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} states that on the attachment the tower's floors are energy cut-offs, the energy being the conformal energy of the palatial storey. In $\Cl(2,4)$ with $Q(e_+) = 1$, $Q(e_-) = -1$, $n_\infty = e_+ + e_-$ and $n_0 = e_+ - e_-$ (null; any normalisation), $P_0 + K_0 = \gamma_0(n_\infty + n_0) = 2\gamma_0e_+$, and $(\gamma_0e_+)^2 = -1$, so $\gamma_0e_+$ generates the compact one-parameter group whose generator is the conformal Hamiltonian. The check computes the kernel of $B \mapsto [\gamma_0e_+, B]$ on the fifteen bivectors exactly: it is seven-dimensional (the compact $\mathfrak{so}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{so}(4)$: $\gamma_0e_+$, the three $\gamma_i\gamma_j$, the three $\gamma_ie_-$), its intersection with the Lorentz bivectors $\gamma_\mu\gamma_\nu$ is the span of the three rotations, and it has zero intersection with the span of the boosts $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, of the translations $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$ and of the special conformal generators $\gamma_\mu n_0$. A generator commuting with the conformal Hamiltonian preserves each of its eigenspaces, so the spatial rotations preserve every floor. Invariance of a single spectral subspace is weaker than commutation, so the converse needs one more step. The boosts, translations and special conformal generators lie in the eight-dimensional complement of the commutant (the noncompact part of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$); in the positive-energy modules their complex combinations raise or lower the conformal energy by one, as in the oscillator model of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, and a nontrivial unitary representation of a noncompact simple group has no nonzero finite-dimensional invariant subspace (standard). A floor is the span of the finitely many lowest energies of a module whose energies are bounded below, so a nonzero noncompact generator, whose raising part moves the top energy of the floor out of it, does not preserve the floor. Hence a floor is invariant under the spatial rotations and under no boost.

\emph{(v).} This clause was first stated as clause (vii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}; it is merged here with its proof. Every basis bivector of $\Cl(2,4)$ either commutes or anticommutes with $H = \gamma_0e_+$ (a product of basis vectors); the commuting ones span the seven-dimensional $\mathfrak{k}$ of (iv), the anticommuting ones an eight-dimensional complement $\mathfrak{p}$, and $\mathfrak{k}$ is closed under the commutator (it is a centraliser). The check computes the Lie closure of $\mathfrak{k}$ together with each of the eight anticommuting basis bivectors ($\gamma_0\gamma_j$, $\gamma_0e_-$, $\gamma_je_+$, $e_+e_-$) and each of the eleven generators $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$, $\gamma_\mu n_0$ exactly, by ranks of rational vectors: each time it is all fifteen bivectors. For an arbitrary $X \notin \mathfrak{k}$, write $X = X_{\mathfrak{k}} + X_{\mathfrak{p}}$ with $X_{\mathfrak{p}} \neq 0$; the closure contains $X_{\mathfrak{p}}$ and the $\mathfrak{k}$-module it generates, which is all of $\mathfrak{p}$ when $\mathfrak{p}$, the module $\R^{2}\otimes\R^{4}$ of $\mathfrak{so}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(4)$, is irreducible, and then $[\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{p}]$ supplies the rest (argued). Let $f$ be a bounded function and $f(H)$ the weighting of the modes of an irreducible unitary module by conformal energy. Every generator in $\mathfrak{k}$ commutes with $H$, hence with $f(H)$; if $f(H)$ also commutes with one boost, it commutes with the Lie algebra they generate, the whole conformal algebra, so by Schur's lemma (cited from memory) it is a multiple of the identity on that module and regulates nothing. The attachment's one-particle modules are irreducible under the conformal algebra (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}; irreducibility cited from memory), so no weighting of the floors, sharp as in (iv) or smooth, keeps a boost.

\emph{The reading.} Nothing in (i) to (iii) uses more than a finite truncation of a chiral band, so they hold for any sharp mode cut-off; the truncated-band origin of the central term is standard (Mattis and Lieb; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-schwinger-term-and-mattis-lieb-density-algebra}(ii)). A sharp cut-off on conformal energy also leaves non-local terms in the regulated zero-point energy, which a smooth cut-off vanishing with its slope at the edge removes (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}). The first two parts concern the global charge, which a floor keeps exactly; the local Ward identity of a gauge-invariant regulator requires the central term to be the scalar $p$, which (ii) excludes on any floor and (iii) restores on the filled sea for momenta up to the cut-off. In two dimensions the chiral anomaly and the photon mass of the Schwinger model are fixed by that central term through bosonisation (standard, cited from memory); the floors therefore reproduce them for the modes below the cut-off and not above. The four-dimensional analogue (conformal-energy modules of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} in place of momenta on a circle) is argued, not computed: the trace argument again excludes a scalar central term on a floor, and (iv) shows that the regulator is not Lorentz-invariant.
