synthesis.light-ray-gauge-currents-of-a-.formal:
Let $V$ be the five-mode module of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}, with occupation states $a^{\dagger}_{S}\Omega$, $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, 5\}$ (modes $1, 2$ the slots, $3, 4, 5$ the pairs), isotypic components $V_{n,k}$ ($n$ slots, $k$ pairs), the gauge algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ acting by $\hat t = \sum_{i,j}t_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{j}$ ($t$ traceless and anti-Hermitian on the five modes) and $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$. Its numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}); on the channels below they are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J$ the kernel bivector, through $I_{4} \mapsto J$ (the other sign is the case of (ii) in which every component is reversed). A halving $V_{+}$ is a gauge-commuting CPT halving: one of $32$ sign patterns, one member of each conjugate pair $V_{n,k}$, $V_{2-n,3-k}$, with any line of the neutral block (\claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(ii)). On one null generator take a window of levels $k = 0, \dots, L - 1$ ($L$ even) and one channel $x$ per occupation state of $V_{+}$, sixteen channels (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)); each mode $(x, k)$ is a tower plane $(e_{x,k}, f_{x,k})$, $Q(e_{x,k}) = 1$, $Q(f_{x,k}) = -1$, with $a^{*}_{x,k} = \tfrac12(e_{x,k} + f_{x,k})$, $a_{x,k} = \tfrac12(e_{x,k} - f_{x,k})$ (Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). For a channel matrix $M$ let $\rho_{q}(M) = \sum_{k, k+q}\sum_{x,y}M_{xy}a^{*}_{x,k}a_{y,k+q}$ (\claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(i)); the gauge currents are $\rho_{q}(\rho_{+}(T))$, $\rho_{+}(T)$ the matrix of $\hat t$ on $V_{+}$; $H = \sum_{x,k}(k - \tfrac{L - 1}{2})n_{x,k}$ is the window energy with half-integer weights and the sea fills $k < L/2$ in every channel (\claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(i), (iii)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Pair currents and partner blocks.)} Every $\rho_{+}(T)$ preserves each component and is anti-Hermitian over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, so every gauge current is a pair current of the channels, with no pair-creation bilinear $a_{x}a_{y}$ or $a^{*}_{x}a^{*}_{y}$: $\mathfrak{g}$ acts in the $\uu(16)$ of the channel currents, not merely in $\so(32)$. On a conjugate pair, in the bases $a^{\dagger}_{S}\Omega$ of $V_{n,k}$ and $\epsilon(S)a^{\dagger}_{S^{c}}\Omega$ of $V_{2-n,3-k}$, where $a^{\dagger}_{S}a^{\dagger}_{S^{c}}\Omega = \epsilon(S)a^{\dagger}_{1}\cdots a^{\dagger}_{5}\Omega$, the matrices of $\hat t$ are $M$ and $-M^{T}$. The trace of $\rho_{+}(T)$ on a component is $0$ for $T \in \su(2) \oplus \su(3)$ and $\dim V_{n,k}\,Y_{n,k}J$ for the hypercharge generator $JY$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Particle-hole reversal.)} Let $C$ be the channels of a set of whole components of $V_{+}$, and $V_{+}^{C}$ the halving that replaces each of them by its partner, read in the partner bases of (i). The map $\varphi_{C}$ with $e_{x,k} \mapsto e_{x,L-1-k}$, $f_{x,k} \mapsto -f_{x,L-1-k}$ for $x \in C$, fixing every other generator, is the inner automorphism $\operatorname{Ad}(\prod_{x \in C}u_{x})$, $u_{x} = f_{x,0}\cdots f_{x,L-1}\prod_{k < L/2}(e_{x,k} - e_{x,L-1-k})(f_{x,k} - f_{x,L-1-k})$, and commutes with the adjoint. It sends $a^{*}_{x,k}$ to $a_{x,L-1-k}$ and $n_{x,k}$ to $1 - n_{x,L-1-k}$ on $C$, fixes $H$, the sea and the set of vectors edge-clean at each depth, and for every $T \in \mathfrak{g}$ and every $q \ge 0$, exactly,
\[
\varphi_{C}\bigl(\rho_{q}(\rho_{+}(T))\bigr) = \rho_{q}(\rho_{+}^{C}(T)) + \delta_{q0}\,L\operatorname{tr}_{C}\rho_{+}(T),
\]
the constant being zero on $\su(2) \oplus \su(3)$. It reverses the rotation weights of $C$: for the mode rotation $\exp(\theta J\sum_{x,k}w_{x}n_{x,k})$ about the generator, $\varphi_{C}$ gives the rotation with $w_{x}$ replaced by $-w_{x}$ on $C$, times the phase $\exp(\theta JL\sum_{x \in C}w_{x})$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Levels and anomalies.)} So the exact window commutators of the gauge currents, their edge terms, their values on edge-clean vectors, the energy and the sea are, up to $\varphi_{C}$ and the hypercharge constant $L\operatorname{tr}_{C}\rho_{+}(JY)$, the same for all $32$ sign patterns and any neutral line; in particular $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}(\rho_{+}(T)\rho_{+}(T')) = 4\operatorname{tr}_{5}(tt')$ for all $T, T'$ and every halving, so the traces of $T_{3}^{2}$, of a colour Cartan generator squared, and of $Y^{2}$ over $V_{+}$ are $2$, $2$, $\tfrac{10}{3}$ for all $32$. The hypercharge constant is not a normalisation: the sea of $V_{+}$ has hypercharge $\tfrac{L}{2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y\,J$ (that is, $\rho_{0}(\rho_{+}(JY))$ acts on it by this number), and $\varphi_{C}$, which maps sea to sea, changes it by $L\operatorname{tr}_{C}Y\,J$; on edge-clean vectors the mixed central term of $\rho_{q}(\rho_{+}(JY))$ with the number current $\rho_{q}(1)$ in $\uu(16)$ is $q\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y\,J$. Both are the mixed gravitational (linear) anomaly coefficient $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y$, which takes the values $0, \pm 2, \pm 4, \pm 6$ and vanishes for exactly $8$ of the $32$ sign patterns. The four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, with the colour cubic, hold for exactly two of the $32$ sign patterns, both among those $8$: the complementary pair $\pm(-1)^{n+k}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4). On the $8$ patterns with $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y = 0$ the constant vanishes and $\varphi_{C}$ is an exact isomorphism of the gauge currents, the energy and the sea, so six anomalous patterns are not distinguished from the two anomaly-free ones. Hence the linear anomaly condition is visible along one generator (the sea's hypercharge, the $Y$-$N$ mixed level) and the cubic conditions are not; no trace quadratic in $\mathfrak{g}$ sees either. With the rotation weights the cubic ones are visible too: if the sixteen channels of $V_{+}$ carry one weight $w_{0}$, each anomaly coefficient is a weighted trace, linear for the mixed gravitational condition and cubic for the others, such as $\sum_{x}(w_{x}/w_{0})Y_{x}$ and $\sum_{x}(w_{x}/w_{0})Y_{x}^{3}$, which $\varphi_{C}$ preserves, while every trace quadratic in $\mathfrak{g}$ (every level) is blind to the weights.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The abelian normalisation.)} With the stored $Y$, $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}T_{3}^{2} = 2$, $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$, $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Q^{2} = \tfrac{16}{3}$ for $Q = T_{3} + Y$; relative to the trace form of the five modes the level of every factor, the abelian one included, is $4$; for the integral charges $6Y$ (greatest common divisor $1$) the abelian trace is $120$, and for $3Q$ it is $48$. A rescaling $Y \mapsto \lambda Y$ multiplies the abelian level by $\lambda^{2}$: it is a number only after a normalisation is chosen, while the ratios $\operatorname{tr}T_{3}^{2} : \operatorname{tr}Y^{2} : \operatorname{tr}Q^{2} = 3 : 5 : 8$, so $\operatorname{tr}T_{3}^{2}/\operatorname{tr}Q^{2} = \tfrac38$, are fixed.
\end{enumerate}
All clauses are proved. \emph{Reading (argued).} The statement that the Standard Model gauge algebra acts inside exact $\uu(16)$ level-one channel currents per light ray and generation holds as far as it goes: the channels are complex with the unit $J$, the gauge currents are pair currents, and no gauge generator connects the two chirality arrays of a light ray, because $\mathfrak{g}$ acts on the internal index while the chirality and the rotation about the generator act on the spinor values (\claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iii), (iv)); reading the conjugate components in the other array is $\varphi_{C}$. Its exactness is that of the stored window identity: exact as an operator identity with edge terms, the central term exact on edge-clean vectors. What it carries of the anomaly content is only the linear part: four-dimensional anomaly cancellation has one linear condition, seen along a generator as the sea's hypercharge and the $Y$-$N$ central term, and cubic conditions that need the channel weights; on the eight sign patterns with $\operatorname{tr}Y = 0$ the gauge currents with energy and sea are the same for anomalous and anomaly-free halvings. The abelian level is a convention, and the trace form is positive on $\mathfrak{g}$, so along one generator the central term of no gauge current vanishes.
synthesis.light-ray-gauge-currents-of-a-.technical: The sixteen Weyl components of a generation give sixteen complex channels on a light ray, and the stored window identity makes their pair currents a level-one $\uu(16)$ current algebra, exact up to edge terms. The gauge algebra $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ of the slot module acts on a halving $V_{+}$ by matrices that are anti-Hermitian over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ and preserve each isotypic component, so its currents are pair currents in $\uu(16)$, never pair-creation terms of $\so(32)$; and since it acts on the internal index while chirality acts on the spinor values, no gauge generator mixes the two chirality arrays. On a conjugate pair of components the matrices are $M$ and $-M^{T}$ in dual bases. The particle-hole reversal of the channels of some components, $a^{*}_{x,k} \mapsto a_{x,L-1-k}$, is an inner automorphism of the window algebra (a product of vectors); it fixes the energy with half-integer weights, the sea and the edge-clean vectors, maps the gauge currents of one halving exactly to those of the halving with those components conjugated, up to a constant in the hypercharge zero mode, and reverses the channels' rotation weights. So all $32$ gauge-commuting CPT halvings have the same trace form $4\operatorname{tr}_{5}$ (traces $2$, $2$, $\tfrac{10}{3}$ of $T_{3}^{2}$, a colour Cartan generator squared, $Y^{2}$), and the same gauge currents, energy and sea up to the hypercharge constant. That constant is not harmless: it is the change of the sea's hypercharge, $\tfrac{L}{2}\operatorname{tr}Y$, and $\operatorname{tr}Y$ is also the mixed central term of the hypercharge and number currents in $\uu(16)$, the mixed gravitational anomaly coefficient, nonzero for $24$ of the $32$ patterns. Among the $8$ with $\operatorname{tr}Y = 0$ the structures are isomorphic, and only $2$ are anomaly-free. So the linear anomaly condition is seen along a generator and the cubic ones are not; no level of $\mathfrak{g}$ sees either, and the cubic coefficients are cubic traces weighted by the rotation weights. The abelian level depends on the normalisation of $Y$ ($\tfrac{10}{3}$ with the stored $Y$, $4$ relative to the five modes, $120$ for integral charges $6Y$); the ratios $3 : 5 : 8$ of the traces of $T_{3}^{2}$, $Y^{2}$, $Q^{2}$ are fixed.
synthesis.light-ray-gauge-currents-of-a-.lay: Along a single light ray on a horizon, the sixteen kinds of particle in one generation of matter behave like sixteen independent lanes of traffic, and the forces of the Standard Model rotate the lanes into one another. One can ask whether this one-dimensional picture knows the most delicate consistency condition of the Standard Model, that the quantum anomalies cancel within each generation. It knows only the simplest part of it. Swapping particles and holes on some of the lanes, an exact symmetry of the one-dimensional picture apart from a shift in the total hypercharge of the filled lanes, turns a consistent generation into one of thirty-two arrangements of which thirty are inconsistent. The picture sees that shift, which is the simplest of the consistency conditions, but it cannot tell apart the eight arrangements whose total hypercharge is zero, six of them inconsistent. The remaining conditions become visible only when one also keeps track of how each lane turns about the light ray. The strength of the abelian force in this picture is also not a fixed number: it depends on a choice of units, and only ratios between forces are fixed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} the modes $a^{*}_{x,k} = \tfrac12(e_{x,k} + f_{x,k})$, $a_{x,k} = \tfrac12(e_{x,k} - f_{x,k})$ satisfy $\{a_{x,k}, a^{*}_{y,l}\} = \delta_{xy}\delta_{kl}$, $\{a_{x,k}, a_{y,l}\} = 0$, and the adjoint $*$ (the antiautomorphism fixing the generators of square $+1$ and negating those of square $-1$) has $(a_{x,k})^{*} = a^{*}_{x,k}$. The kernel bivector $J$ commutes with every mode, $J^{2} = -1$, $J^{*} = -J$, so $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ is a field of scalars for the mode algebra, as in \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}; for a matrix $A$ on the one-particle index set, $\hat A = \sum A_{(x,k)(y,l)}a^{*}_{x,k}a_{y,l}$ satisfies $[\hat A, \hat B] = \widehat{[A, B]}$, and $\rho_{q}(M) = \widehat{S_{q} \otimes M}$ with $S_{q}$ the partial shift of the window (the proof of (i) there). The five-mode module and its halvings are those of \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}, and a halving's sixteen occupation states label the sixteen channels of a light ray, its Weyl components (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)); on it the same bilinear rule gives $[\hat t, \hat s] = \widehat{[t, s]}$.

\emph{(i).} The operator $\hat t$ conserves the number of slots and the number of pairs when $t$ is block diagonal on slots and pairs, which every element of $\mathfrak{g}$ is; so $\hat t$ preserves each $V_{n,k}$, hence each component of a halving, and $\rho_{+}(T)$ is block diagonal on the components of $V_{+}$. It is anti-Hermitian since $\hat t^{*} = \widehat{t^{*}} = -\hat t$ for the positive Hermitian form in which the occupation states are orthonormal. A gauge current is $\rho_{q}(\rho_{+}(T)) = \sum M_{xy}a^{*}_{x,k}a_{y,k+q}$: only creator-annihilator products occur, so it is a pair current, and the real Lie algebra of the $\rho_{0}(M)$ with $M$ anti-Hermitian over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ is $\uu(16)$; the bilinears $a_{x}a_{y}$, $a^{*}_{x}a^{*}_{y}$, which together with the pair currents span $\so(32)$, do not occur. For the partner blocks, the exterior product pairs $V_{n,k}$ with $V_{2-n,3-k}$ into the top degree: $P(\alpha, \beta)a^{\dagger}_{1}\cdots a^{\dagger}_{5}\Omega = \alpha\wedge\beta$. The bases $a^{\dagger}_{S}\Omega$ and $b_{R} = \epsilon(R)a^{\dagger}_{R^{c}}\Omega$ are dual for $P$: $a^{\dagger}_{S}a^{\dagger}_{R^{c}}\Omega = 0$ unless $S = R$, and $a^{\dagger}_{S}\epsilon(S)a^{\dagger}_{S^{c}}\Omega = \epsilon(S)^{2}a^{\dagger}_{1}\cdots a^{\dagger}_{5}\Omega$. The operator $\hat t$ is the derivation of the exterior algebra induced by $t$, so $\hat t(\alpha\wedge\beta) = \hat t\alpha\wedge\beta + \alpha\wedge\hat t\beta$, and on the top degree $\hat t$ is multiplication by $\operatorname{tr}t = 0$. Hence $P(\hat t\alpha, \beta) + P(\alpha, \hat t\beta) = 0$, and in dual bases the matrix of $\hat t$ on $V_{2-n,3-k}$ is $-M^{T}$. On an irreducible component the trace of a semisimple generator vanishes ($\su(2) \oplus \su(3)$ is its own derived algebra), and the hypercharge generator acts on $V_{n,k}$ as the scalar $Y_{n,k}J$.

\emph{(ii).} The images of the generators under $\varphi_{C}$ are, up to sign, a permutation of the generators, with the same squares, so they anticommute pairwise and $\varphi_{C}$ extends to an automorphism of the window Clifford algebra (its universal property). A vector $u$ with $Q(u) \ne 0$ acts by the reflection $z \mapsto -uzu^{-1}$, which maps $f_{x,k}$ to $-f_{x,k}$ for $u = f_{x,k}$, exchanges $e_{x,k}$ and $e_{x,L-1-k}$ for $u = e_{x,k} - e_{x,L-1-k}$ ($Q(u) = 2$, $z - 2(z\cdot u)u/Q(u)$), exchanges $f_{x,k}$ and $f_{x,L-1-k}$ for $u = f_{x,k} - f_{x,L-1-k}$ ($Q(u) = -2$), and fixes every generator orthogonal to $u$. The product $u_{x}$ has $2L$ factors, an even number, so the signs cancel and $\operatorname{Ad}(u_{x})$ is the composition of these reflections, which is $\varphi_{\{x\}}$ on the generators; $u_{x}\tilde u_{x} = \prod Q = (-1)^{L}2^{L/2}(-2)^{L/2}$ is a nonzero scalar. For distinct channels the $u_{x}$ involve disjoint generators, so $\varphi_{C} = \operatorname{Ad}(\prod_{x \in C}u_{x})$. It commutes with $*$ because it maps generators of square $+1$ to generators of square $+1$ and generators of square $-1$ to $\pm$ generators of square $-1$. Then $\varphi_{C}(a^{*}_{x,k}) = \tfrac12(e_{x,L-1-k} - f_{x,L-1-k}) = a_{x,L-1-k}$ and $\varphi_{C}(a_{x,k}) = a^{*}_{x,L-1-k}$, so $\varphi_{C}(n_{x,k}) = a_{x,L-1-k}a^{*}_{x,L-1-k} = 1 - n_{x,L-1-k}$. With $c = (L - 1)/2$,
\[
\varphi_{C}\Bigl(\sum_{k}(k - c)n_{x,k}\Bigr) = \sum_{k}(k - c) - \sum_{k}(k - c)n_{x,L-1-k} = 0 + \sum_{j}(j - c)n_{x,j},
\]
since $L - 1 - j - c = c - j$: $H$, the window energy with the half-integer weights of \claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(i), (iii) (shifted by the constant $M^{2}/2$ there, $L = 2M$), is fixed. A vector with $n_{x,k} = 1$ for $k < d$ and $n_{x,k} = 0$ for $k \ge L - d$ goes to one with the same property, so the edge-clean vectors at each depth, and for $d = L/2$ the sea, are preserved. For the currents, $M = \rho_{+}(T)$ is block diagonal on components and $C$ is a union of components, so $M_{xy} = 0$ when exactly one of $x, y$ lies in $C$. For $x, y \in C$,
\[
\varphi_{C}(a^{*}_{x,k}a_{y,k+q}) = a_{x,L-1-k}a^{*}_{y,L-1-k-q} = -a^{*}_{y,k'}a_{x,k'+q} + \delta_{xy}\delta_{q0}, \qquad k' = L - 1 - k - q,
\]
and $k, k + q$ run over the window exactly when $k', k' + q$ do. Summing with $M_{xy}$ gives $\rho_{q}$ of the matrix $-M^{T}$ on $C$ plus $\delta_{q0}L\operatorname{tr}_{C}M$; by (i), $-M^{T}$ on $C$ is the matrix of $\hat t$ on the partner components in the partner bases, that is $\rho_{+}^{C}(T)$ there, and outside $C$ nothing changes. The constant vanishes on $\su(2) \oplus \su(3)$ by (i). Finally $\varphi_{C}(\sum_{k}w_{x}n_{x,k}) = w_{x}(L - \sum_{k}n_{x,k})$ for $x \in C$, which gives the reversed weights and the phase.

\emph{(iii).} $\varphi_{C}$ is an automorphism, so it carries every identity among the currents (the exact window commutators of \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(i) with their edge terms, the values on the edge-clean vectors it preserves) to the corresponding identity for $V_{+}^{C}$, and it fixes $H$ and the sea. Every gauge-commuting halving is obtained from the halving $(-1)^{n+k}$ by reversing a set of whole charged components (a sign pattern) and choosing a line of the neutral block, whose channel carries the zero matrix; so all $32$ sign patterns, with any neutral line, are related by some $\varphi_{C}$. The trace form: $\operatorname{tr}(MM')$ is unchanged when a block $M$, $M'$ is replaced by $-M^{T}$, $-M'^{T}$, so it is the same for all halvings, and on the halving $(-1)^{n+k}$ it equals $4\operatorname{tr}_{5}(tt')$ for each of the twelve basis generators and their pairs (computed). The anomaly coefficients are sums over the weights of $V_{+}$: $\sum Y$, $\sum Y^{3}$, $\sum YT_{3}^{2}$, $\sum YH_{3}^{2}$ (the four conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, the second and third weighted by the multiplicity of the other factor through the sum over weights) and the colour cubic $\sum H_{8}^{3}$, $H_{8} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, -2)$ on the pairs; each is odd under replacing a component by its partner, whose weights are the negatives. Over the $32$ sign patterns exactly two give zero for all five, and they are complementary; they are the parity halvings $\pm(-1)^{n+k}$ on the charged components, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(4) states (computed). The hypercharge constant: the sea fills $L/2$ levels of every channel, so $\rho_{0}(\rho_{+}(JY)) = \sum_{x,k}Y_{x}J\,n_{x,k}$ acts on it as $\tfrac{L}{2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y\,J$; since $\varphi_{C}$ maps the sea of $V_{+}$ to the sea of $V_{+}^{C}$ and $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}^{C}}Y = \operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y - 2\operatorname{tr}_{C}Y$, the constant $L\operatorname{tr}_{C}Y\,J$ of (ii) is the difference of the two seas' hypercharges. By \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(i) with $M = \rho_{+}(JY)$ and $M' = 1$ (the number current, in $\uu(16)$ but not in $\mathfrak{g}$), $[\rho_{q}(M), \rho_{q}(1)^{*}]$ acts on edge-clean vectors as $q\operatorname{tr}(M) + \rho_{0}([M, 1]) = q\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y\,J$. Both are the mixed gravitational coefficient $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y = \pm 1 \pm 1 \pm 1 \pm 1 \pm 2$ (the contributions $\dim V_{n,k}Y_{n,k}$ of $V_{1,0}$, $V_{2,0}$, $V_{0,1}$, $V_{1,1}$, $V_{2,1}$ are $1, 1, -1, 1, 2$, each sign reversed with the component), which is zero exactly when the sign of the $2$ is opposite to three of the four $\pm1$: $8$ of the $32$ patterns (computed); it does not vanish on the other $24$, so these are distinguished from the anomaly-free ones by the sea's hypercharge. Two halvings with $\operatorname{tr}Y = 0$ differ by a $C$ with $\operatorname{tr}_{C}Y = 0$, so there $\varphi_{C}$ maps currents, energy and sea exactly, and the $8$ contain the $2$ anomaly-free patterns and $6$ anomalous ones. If the channels of $V_{+}$ carry one weight $w_{0}$, then after $\varphi_{C}$ the channels of $C$ carry $-w_{0}$ and the opposite charges, so the weighted traces $\sum_{x}(w_{x}/w_{0})Y_{x}$ (linear) and $\sum_{x}(w_{x}/w_{0})Y_{x}^{3}$ and the other cubic ones are unchanged, while every unweighted trace quadratic in $\mathfrak{g}$ is the same for all halvings, as shown.

\emph{(iv).} On the halving $(-1)^{n+k}$ (one generation: $Q$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $L$, $e^{c}$ and the neutral singlet), $\operatorname{tr}T_{3}^{2} = 4\cdot 2\cdot\tfrac14 = 2$ (four doublets), $\operatorname{tr}Y^{2} = 6\cdot\tfrac{1}{36} + 3\cdot\tfrac49 + 3\cdot\tfrac19 + 2\cdot\tfrac14 + 1 + 0 = \tfrac{10}{3}$, $\operatorname{tr}T_{3}Y = 0$ (each doublet has one $Y$), so $\operatorname{tr}Q^{2} = 2 + \tfrac{10}{3} = \tfrac{16}{3}$. On the five modes $\operatorname{tr}_{5}T_{3}^{2} = \tfrac12$ and $\operatorname{tr}_{5}Y^{2} = 2\cdot\tfrac14 + 3\cdot\tfrac19 = \tfrac56$, ratios $4$ and $4$, as (iii) gives for every generator. The charges $6Y$ are the integers $0, -4, 1, -3, 6, 2$ with multiplicities $1, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3$, greatest common divisor $1$ and squares summing to $120$; the charges $3Q$ are integers with squares summing to $9\cdot\tfrac{16}{3} = 48$. Rescaling multiplies a quadratic trace by $\lambda^{2}$, and the ratios $2 : \tfrac{10}{3} : \tfrac{16}{3} = 3 : 5 : 8$ do not change when $Y$ is fixed by $Q = T_{3} + Y$.

\emph{Checks.} The exact check verifies (i) for the twelve basis generators on all five conjugate pairs (the partner blocks, anti-Hermiticity, block diagonality on all $32$ states, the traces on components); (ii) on a window $L = 4$ with five channels (the components $V_{1,0}$ and $V_{0,1}$) for three choices of $C$: the images square correctly, $\operatorname{Ad}(u_{x})$ equals $\varphi_{C}$ on the generators of a channel and fixes another, $u_{x}\tilde u_{x} = 16$, the number operators and $H$, and the identity for all twelve generators and $q = 0, \dots, 3$; (iii) the $12 \times 12$ trace form $4\operatorname{tr}_{5}$ on all $32$ sign patterns, the traces $2$, $2$, $\tfrac{10}{3}$, four doublets, and exactly two anomaly-free patterns, complementary, of uniform parity, with zero colour cubic; and, separately, $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}Y$ over the $32$ patterns (values $0, \pm2, \pm4, \pm6$, zero for $8$, the $2$ anomaly-free among them), the constant $L\operatorname{tr}_{C}Y\,J$ as the difference of the seas' hypercharges $\tfrac{L}{2}\operatorname{tr}Y$ for every pair of patterns differing on one component, and on a window $L = 2$ with the three channels of $V_{1,0}$ and $V_{2,0}$ ($\operatorname{tr}Y = 2$) the sea's hypercharge and the $Y$-$N$ central term on the sea, both $\operatorname{tr}Y\,J$ (times $L/2 = 1$); (iv) the numbers $2$, $\tfrac{10}{3}$, $\tfrac{16}{3}$, the ratios, $120$, $48$, the greatest common divisor and the scaling.

synthesis.light-ray-recurrence-test-verd.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator of a horizon in the scope of Premise (N$_{+}$), a \emph{complex array} is an array of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3, weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, and a \emph{real array} the modes of one real chiral boson at integer weights $\kappa k$, which carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering ($\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$, as each complex array does, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(ii)). For a content with $f$ complex and $b$ real arrays per generator put $c = f + b$, and call the \emph{one-window test} the condition $24 \mid c$ and the \emph{two-window test} the condition $12 \mid c$. They are the conditions for $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = 1$ and $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = 1$ ($J$ the unit of the boundary-mode arrays; on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$ and the conditions are the same), that is, for a window evolution of the form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$, with $P$ the grading normalised to $+1$ on the sea, to be $P$, respectively to be $\pm P$, equivalently the evolution over two windows to be $1$. That form is the reading under which the tests are posed; nothing below uses it. Call the \emph{additive reading} the reading in which the light-ray sea contains, besides the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation and in addition to them, one real array per real component of the null data of the gauge vectors, of the scalar doublets and, if $\epsilon = 1$, of the graviton. It lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading, and it is not the reading of Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), which identifies every channel of each four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, a current of the arrays. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Null data of each field, under the additive reading.)} On a null plane $N_{k}$ of $\Cl(1,3)$, $k = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, $m = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, $Q(k) = Q(m) = 0$, $\ip{k}{m} = 2$: every Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i)); every abelian gauge vector gives two real fields per generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii)), at integer boost weight (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(vi)), and the same count for each component of a non-abelian vector is argued, not proved; and every real scalar component gives one real field per generator for every potential $V$: for linearised solutions $\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}$ of $\nabla^{2}\phi + V'(\phi) = 0$ the current $\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla\phi_{1}$ has $\nabla\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla^{2}\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla^{2}\phi_{1} = 0$, its flux through $N_{k}$ is $k\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$, which contains neither $V$ nor a transverse derivative, and $\nabla^{2} = (k\cdot\nabla)(m\cdot\nabla) - \partial_{1}^{2} - \partial_{2}^{2}$, so the field equation fixes $(m\cdot\nabla)\phi$ on $N_{k}$ from $\phi$ there and one boundary value per generator (that these data carry integer weight, so form a real array, is argued). Hence, under the additive reading, a content of $n_{g}$ generations of the slot module (sixteen Weyl components each, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)), $n_{V}$ gauge vectors, $n_{s}$ real scalar components and, if a graviton's two helicities are counted, $\epsilon = 1$ ($\epsilon = 0$ otherwise) has
\[
c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon ,
\]
for every mass matrix and every scalar potential.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The gauge vectors drop out, additive reading.)} With the connection-forced algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), $n_{V} = 12$ and the vectors contribute $24$, so they change neither test. A gauge algebra of dimension $d$ drops out of the one-window test if and only if $12 \mid d$, and of the two-window test if and only if $6 \mid d$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The verdict on generations, additive reading.)} With $n_{V} = 12$ and $n_{s} = 4n_{h}$ ($n_{h}$ doublets), the one-window test holds if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, and the two-window test if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. So: with no scalar counted both hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$; with one doublet the one-window test fails for every $n_{g}$ and the two-window test holds exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ ($c = 60$ at $n_{g} = 2$, where the window evolution is $-P$); with the eight real components of the linear rung field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), $n_{h} = 2$, both hold exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, so $n_{g} = 1$ and $4$ pass and $n_{g} = 3$ fails ($c = 80$); with $\epsilon = 1$ (the graviton counted additively, as J3's species, every massless field, would include it) neither holds for any $n_{g}$, $n_{h}$ ($c \equiv 2 \pmod 4$). The content $n_{h} = 1$, $\epsilon = 1$ gives $c = 78$ at $n_{g} = 3$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The per-generation count.)} With $f$ Weyl components per generation and nothing else, the one-window test holds if and only if $24/\gcd(24, f)$ divides $n_{g}$ (the two-window test likewise with $12$), and the one-window modulus is $3$ exactly when $f \equiv 8$ or $16 \pmod{24}$. Fifteen components per generation (no neutral singlet, not a CPT halving of the slot module) give $8 \mid n_{g}$ and $4 \mid n_{g}$; sixteen components and the count of eight Majorana-Weyl units per generation give the same modulus $3$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Boson-fermion balance, additive reading.)} If $b = 2f$, the balance of on-shell degrees of freedom at which the quartic coefficient $2N_{V} + N_{S} - 2N_{W}$ of the attachment's Sakharov sum vanishes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}(iv), here with $\epsilon = 0$), then $c = 3f = 48n_{g}$ and both tests hold for every $n_{g}$; at $n_{g} = 3$, $N_{V} = 12$ this is that theorem's $N_{S} = 72$, with $c = 144$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(J3's reading.)} If the integer-weight channels are read as J3 reads them, currents of the arrays, they add no array, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$.
\end{enumerate}
So the scalar and graviton content set the verdict only under the additive reading: there the tests single out $n_{g} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ only with no graviton and a number of doublets divisible by $6$ (one window) or $3$ (two windows), and with the graviton counted no content passes; under J3's reading the verdict is $3 \mid n_{g}$. Which reading holds, and so which fields form the sea, is not decided here, and neither test distinguishes three generations from six or nine.
synthesis.light-ray-recurrence-test-verd.technical: The recorded recurrence test asks that the evolution of the light-ray sea over one window of Killing time be exactly the fermion grading, which needs the light-ray central charge $c$ to be a multiple of $24$; the weaker requirement, the grading up to sign or two windows giving the identity, needs a multiple of $12$. This result reads off both verdicts under two readings of the bosons. In the additive reading the null data of the vectors, the scalars and possibly the graviton are counted as real arrays of their own on top of the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation; this reading lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading and is not that of the stored channel postulate J3, which reads every massless field's channels as currents of the arrays. Null data are mass-blind: a Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix and an abelian vector two real fields (both stored), and a real scalar one real field for every potential, since the symplectic flux through the null plane is $\phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$ and the potential enters only the constraint; the non-abelian vector count and the integer weight of scalar data are argued. So $c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon$. The twelve gauge vectors give exactly $24$ and drop out; the recorded failure at $78$ comes from the doublet's $4$ and the graviton's $2$. With $n_{h}$ doublets, one window needs $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$ and two windows $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$; a graviton, which J3's species list includes, makes both fail always. On the two doublets of the store's linear rung field the test passes at one and four generations and fails at three; with one doublet the two-window test passes at two. At the boson-fermion balance where the stored quartic Sakharov coefficient vanishes, $c = 48n_{g}$ and the test does not see $n_{g}$. Under J3's own reading the bosons add nothing, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests give $3 \mid n_{g}$; the modulus $3$ comes from $24 = 8 \cdot 3$ against the power of two $16$, and the Majorana-Weyl count $8$ of the literature gives the same.
synthesis.light-ray-recurrence-test-verd.lay: An earlier argument suggested that a timing condition on the sea of particles running along a black hole's horizon (after one cycle the sea should return to itself exactly, up to the sign that distinguishes fermions) would require the number of particle generations to be a multiple of three, provided only the matter particles form that sea. Whether the force carriers, the Higgs field and the graviton add to that sea depends on a reading the series has not settled: its own rule for these fields treats them as built from the matter sea, in which case they add nothing and the multiple-of-three answer stands. If instead they are counted as extra members of the sea, the force carriers add exactly a harmless amount, while the Higgs field and a graviton shift the answer: with one Higgs doublet the strict condition can never be met and a slightly weaker form picks two generations; with the series' two Higgs doublets it picks one or four and rules out three; with a graviton it can never be met. In no reading can the condition tell three generations from six.

proofs.main:
\emph{The tests.} Let $J$ be the unit of the boundary-mode arrays, $J^{2} = -1$, central among the modes (on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$, and everything below holds with $I_{4}$ for $J$). For $c \in \Z$, $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \cos	frac{2\pi c}{24} + J\sin	frac{2\pi c}{24} = 1$ exactly when $c/24 \in \Z$; likewise $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = (e^{2\pi Jc/24})^{2} = 1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$, and $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \pm1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$. An operator implementing the grading is fixed only up to sign; normalising it by $P = +1$ on the sea, the one-window test says that $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is $P$, the two-window test that it is $\pm P$, equivalently that its square, the evolution over two windows, is $1$ ($P^{2} = 1$, $P$ commuting with the central unit). The form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is the reading under which the tests are posed: each complex array carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the null ordering (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(i), (ii)), and a real array at integer weights carries, in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering, $	frac12\sum_{n \ge 1}\kappa n = 	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$ (the zero mode carrying nothing), with excitation energies in $\kappa\Z$, so its one-window phase on excitations is $1$. \emph{Computed:} the finite part at $\varepsilon = 0$ of $\sum_{n \ge 0}(n + a)e^{-\varepsilon(n + a)}$ is $-	frac12B_{2}(a)$, by exact series inversion, so $\zeta(-1) = -	frac12B_{2}(1) = -	frac1{12}$ and a real array carries $-\kappa/24$; a real array at the half offset would carry $	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1, 	frac12) = +\kappa/48$, not the null-ordered window value. That the boson's zero point equals the null-ordered window value of the continuum, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric} shows for the CAR arrays, is part of the additive reading, not derived. None of this is used in (i) to (vi), which are statements about $c$.

\emph{The two readings.} Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), in the past cone of the null-ordering result, identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel of every four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, which is a current of the arrays; read so, the integer-weight channels add no array and only the CAR count enters $c$. The additive reading instead counts their null data as further real arrays. Premise (N$_{+}$) and the window reading (\claimref{synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-energy}) are stated for CAR arrays (the arrays of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3), so neither places vector, scalar or graviton data in the sea; the additive reading is an extension of both. Clauses (i) to (v) are statements under the additive reading and (vi) under J3's.

(i) \emph{Fermions and vectors} are the cited clauses: Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i) shows that every Lorentz-covariant mass term, Dirac or Majorana, acts from the right and enters only the equation fixing $\Lambda(k)\psi$ from the free data $\Lambda(m)\psi$, one complex channel per Weyl component; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii) shows that the flux of the Maxwell symplectic current through $N_{k}$ in the gauge $k\cdot A = 0$ contains the two transverse components alone, so an abelian gauge vector gives two real fields on each generator. \emph{Argued, not proved:} for the factors of a non-abelian algebra the count is that of the free field, component by component in the adjoint, the interaction entering, as the mass terms do for the spinor, only through the equations off the plane (light-front gauge); no stored clause covers it. Both carry integer or half-integer boost weight as recorded in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(ii), (vi): spinor data weight $	frac12$ (the complex arrays), vector and bivector data integer weight (the real arrays); clause (vi) of that theorem does not cover scalars.

The cases: $n_{h} = 0$ gives $3 \mid n_{g}$ in both; $n_{h} = 1$ is odd while $2n_{g}$ is even, so the one-window test never holds, and $n_{g} \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ for the other; $n_{h} = 2$ gives $2 \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, i.e. $n_{g} \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, and $n_{g} + 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, the same. At $n_{g} = 2$, $n_{h} = 1$: $c = 60$, $c/24 = 	frac52$ and $e^{2\pi J\cdot 5/2} = J^{10} = -1$ (the window evolution is $-P$); at $n_{g} = 3$, $n_{h} = 2$: $c = 80$, $80/12$ is not an integer; at $n_{g} = 3$, $n_{h} = 1$, $\epsilon = 1$: $c = 48 + 24 + 4 + 2 = 78$. The linear rung field has eight real components (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}, its four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum), so $n_{s} = 8$, $n_{h} = 2$. \emph{Computed:} both equivalences on a full period ($n_{g}  mod 3$, $n_{h}  mod 6$, $\epsilon$) with two lifts, and the one-window rule on $0 \le n_{g}, n_{h} < 40$; the pass lists for $1 \le n_{g} \le 9$ at $n_{h} = 0, 1, 2$; the values $J^{10} = -1$, $J^{20} = 1$ with $J = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$ of $\Cl(1,3)$ standing for the unit.

(iv) Let $g = \gcd(24, f)$. Then $24 \mid fn_{g}$ if and only if $(24/g) \mid (f/g)n_{g}$, and since $24/g$ and $f/g$ are coprime, if and only if $(24/g) \mid n_{g}$; the same with $12$. $24/g = 3$ exactly when $g = 8$, that is $8 \mid f$ and $3

synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.formal:
In the setting of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}: the complexified rung summand $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ with $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$, $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, $\mathsf{N} = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$, $m = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})$, the slot mixing $U(2)$ with generators $T_{j}$ and $Y$, the rung boost $e^{tK}$, the D-term potential $V_{D}$ at level $\xi = 2\zeta$, the null-lift locus $L = \{Q = -H^{2}\}$, its cone $L_{0} = \{Q = 0\}$ (the limit $H \to 0$) and the physical family point $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$ of $L_{0}$, with $\mathsf{N}^{*} = \tfrac12\lambda^{2}$, $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{*}$, $M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac12(g^{2} + g'^{2})\mathsf{N}^{*}$, $v^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}^{*}$. Take the field theory's unit to be $I_{4}$ (\claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}). The \emph{linear rung field} is the field with values in all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, eight real components, with a real $U(2)$-invariant polynomial potential; the \emph{constrained field} is its restriction to $L$ or $L_{0}$. Masses are eigenvalues of the Hessian divided by the kinetic coefficient of the stored Hermitian term. Write $r = \sqrt{k_{8}^{2} + k_{9}^{2}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The unit.)} In $\Cl(3,5)$, spacetime with the two rung planes, $I_{4}^{2} = -1$ and $I_{4}$ commutes with every $v_{a}$, $w_{a}$; so $\mathcal{R}_{\C} = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}\otimes(H_{4} \oplus H_{5})$ inside the algebra, $c^{2} = Q(c)$ is $I_{4}$-bilinear, and the field has four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum. With $b = \sum_{a}v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{tb})$ is the rung boost $e^{tK}$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{\phi I_{4}b})$ multiplies each $v_{a}$ by $e^{\phi I_{4}}$ and each $w_{a}$ by $e^{-\phi I_{4}}$, which is $e^{2\phi Y}$: on the rung summand the hypercharge rotation is the rung boost at $I_{4}$-imaginary rapidity, the reading \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes} gives on the modes. Since $I_{4}b$ anticommutes with every spacetime vector, $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{\phi I_{4}b})$ does not fix the spacetime vectors (it moves $\gamma_{0}$ for $\cos\phi = -\tfrac{7}{25}$), so the identification holds on rung values, not on spacetime points.
\item \emph{(Spectrum of the linear field.)} Let $V = V_{D} + W(\mathsf{N}) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$, with the level fixed by the stored vacuum condition so that the family point is critical. Its eight masses there are $0$ three times (the gauge orbit), $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 2\mathsf{N}^{*}W''$ and $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$ twice, as on $L$, and the \emph{normal pair}, spanned by the two directions of $\alpha_{1}$, the only directions that change $Q$ at first order, with
\[
m_{H}^{2},\ m_{A}^{2} = 2W'(\mathsf{N}^{*}) + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}(k_{10} \pm r) = m_{\pm}^{2} - M_{W}^{2} + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}(k_{10} \pm r),
\]
not mixed with the other modes. For the pure D-term the normal pair is massless. With $k_{8} = k_{9} = 0$ and the term $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2}$, the vacuum lies at $Q = -H^{2}(1 - 2W'/m_{H}^{2})$ to first order in $H^{2}$: the constrained field is the limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ of the linear one, at fixed $m_{h}$ and $m_{\pm}$.
\item \emph{(Scale-free linear field.)} Let $V$ be a quartic over the ten stored invariants on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $V = k_{1}|\alpha|^{4} + k_{2}|\beta|^{4} + k_{3}|\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2} + |\alpha|^{2}(k_{4}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{5}\operatorname{Im}Q) + |\beta|^{2}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}Q) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$, with the flat condition $a + b - e = 0$ and the admissibility $e \ge 0$, $2a \ge e$ of \claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(3). The physical ray $\alpha = 0$ is a critical point exactly when $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$. There the masses are $0$ four times (three gauge directions and the scalon), $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$ twice, and $m_{H}^{2}, m_{A}^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N} + 4\mathsf{N}(k_{10} \pm r)$, all proportional to $\mathsf{N}$. If $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$ and $k_{10} \ge r$, then $V \ge 0$ on $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ and $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$; if $k_{10} + r < -(2a - e)/2$ the normal pair is tachyonic.
\item \emph{(The scalon sum.)} Under the hypotheses (GW) and (D) of \claimref{synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev}, applied to the scale-free linear field of (3) (real scalars with a quartic polynomial potential, the setting of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}), the real scalars other than the scalon and the gauge directions are the charged pair and the normal pair, and
\[
8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4} + 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} - 12m_{t}^{4} - \ell, \qquad \ell = 12m_{b}^{4} + 12m_{c}^{4} + 4m_{\tau}^{4}.
\]
With the stored input box of that result ($m_{h} \in [125, 125.4]$, $v \in [246, 247]$, $m_{t} \in [162, 173]$ GeV, the stored $M_{W}$, $M_{Z}$, $m_{b}$, $m_{c}$, $m_{\tau}$), $2 \cdot 450^{4} < 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} < 2 \cdot 456^{4}$ GeV$^{4}$. Hence $m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV and $m_{H}, m_{A} < 542$ GeV; when $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$ (as under $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$, $k_{10} \ge r$), $m_{\pm} < 383$ GeV. The stored bracket $450 < m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV is the case $m_{H} = m_{A} = 0$. The displayed relation is the standard Gildener-Weinberg sum rule of the scale-invariant two-doublet model; what is new is that the linear rung field is that model.
\item \emph{(Diphoton rate.)} Under the same hypotheses, with the loop functions of the stored result, the normal pair is neutral and does not enter $h \to \gamma\gamma$ at one loop, the charged pair enters with unit weight, and its loop function $A_{0}(\tau) = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 2}4^{n}\tau^{n - 2}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, $\tau = m_{h}^{2}/4m_{\pm}^{2}$, increases as $m_{\pm}$ decreases; so $\mu_{\gamma\gamma}$ decreases with $m_{\pm}$ and $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ for every $m_{\pm} \in (m_{h}/2, 456]$ GeV.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the transmutation branch excluded, 2 November 2026).} Under the decided coupling reading, the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion $Yc + \tilde{Y}c^{*}$ with complex symmetric family matrices (the rung $10$), the scale-free (transmutation) branch of clauses (3) to (5) is recorded as excluded, by three independent strikes: (a) $h \to \gamma\gamma$: the bound $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ of (5) lies $3.3$ standard deviations below the Particle Data Group 2026 average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ (pdglive node S126SGG, read on 2 November 2026; inputs ATLAS 2023 $1.04^{+0.10}_{-0.09}$, CMS 2022 $1.13 \pm 0.09$, ATLAS and CMS Run 1 $1.14^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$); (b) $B$-meson mixing: with the normal pair below $542$ GeV, as (4) requires, its tree-level exchange exceeds the measured $B_{s}$ and $B_{d}$ mass differences more than $50$ times for every splitting of $m_{H}$ and $m_{A}$ (more than $52$ and $50$), with quark mixing from tree-level determinations and three-family unitarity (\claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch}); (c) strong coupling: on the surface of (4) the quartic couplings reach $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV at one loop (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch}). Clauses (1) to (5) and their mathematics are unchanged: (1) and (2) hold for the linear field on every branch, and (3) to (5) stand as statements about the scale-free linear field under (GW) and (D); what is excluded is that branch as the origin of the weak scale under that coupling reading. The branch with a level, on which the normal pair and the charged pair are heavy (about $2.5$ to $3.5$ TeV), is the working branch.
synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.technical:
Take the field theory's unit to be $I_{4}$. In the algebra of spacetime and the two rung planes, $I_{4}$ commutes with the rung vectors, so the rung field's complex coefficients are $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$-valued inside the algebra, $c^{2} = Q(c)$ is bilinear over them, and the field carries four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum; on the rung summand the hypercharge rotation is the rung boost $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{tb})$, $b = \sum_{a}v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$, taken at imaginary rapidity $t = \phi I_{4}$. The continued rotor moves the spacetime vectors ($I_{4}b$ anticommutes with them), so this holds on rung values, not on spacetime points.

A polynomial (elementary) quantum field is linear: it takes values in all eight real components, not on the quadric $Q = -H^{2}$. For $V = V_{D} + W(\mathsf{N}) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$ at the stored family point on the cone, the stored masses $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 2\mathsf{N}^{*}W''$ and $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$ survive, and a neutral normal pair appears, the two directions that change $Q$, with $m_{H,A}^{2} = 2W' + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}(k_{10} \pm r)$, $r = \sqrt{k_{8}^{2} + k_{9}^{2}}$; it is massless for the pure D-term, and the constrained field is the limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ (the linear vacuum sits at $Q = -H^{2}(1 - 2W'/m_{H}^{2})$ to first order in $H^{2}$).

For the scale-free linear field with the flat physical ray ($k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$ is needed for the ray to be critical), the masses are $0$, $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$ and $m_{H,A}^{2} = m_{\pm}^{2} + 4\mathsf{N}(k_{10} \pm r)$, all proportional to $\mathsf{N}$, so under the Gildener-Weinberg formula and decoupling the normal pair enters the scalon sum, the standard sum rule of the scale-invariant two-doublet model: $2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$ lies between $2 \cdot 450^{4}$ and $2 \cdot 456^{4}$ GeV$^{4}$ over the stored inputs. The charged pair lies below $456$ GeV (below $383$ GeV when the normal pair is the heavier, as for $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$, $k_{10} \ge r$), the normal pair below $542$ GeV; the stored $450$ to $456$ GeV is the edge with a massless normal pair. That edge is itself excluded (argued): the normal pair is the neutral part of a doublet, so a massless pair would add about half a neutrino species to the invisible width of the $Z$, which the measured width rules out. The normal pair is neutral, and the charged pair's loop function grows as it gets lighter, so $h \to \gamma\gamma$ stays below $0.900$ of the Standard Model rate for every charged mass between $m_{h}/2$ and $456$ GeV. (Note, 2 November 2026: under the series' coupling reading with symmetric family matrices the transmutation branch is excluded, by the diphoton rate, whose Particle Data Group 2026 average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ lies $3.3$ standard deviations above the bound $0.900$, by tree-level $B$-meson mixing from the light normal pair more than fifty times the measured rate, and by quartic couplings that reach $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV; the spectrum of the linear field stands on every branch, and the branch with a level, with the second doublet at a few TeV, is the working branch.)
synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.lay: To treat the series' Higgs candidate, the rung field, as a quantum field one has to say what its quantum values are. The series' own imaginary unit, the spacetime volume element, works for it, and with that unit the hypercharge symmetry turns out to be the series' frame boost taken at imaginary speed. A quantum field of the ordinary, well-behaved kind cannot be confined to the curved surface on which the rung field was defined; it has to range over all its directions, and two extra neutral particles appear, the directions off the surface. If the weak scale arises from quantum corrections alone, as an earlier result explored, these two particles must be counted: the charged scalar that result predicted near 450 GeV is then lighter, the new neutral pair lies below about 540 GeV, and the predicted shortfall in the Higgs boson's decays to two photons, about ten per cent, remains for every allowed charged mass. (Since 2 November 2026 that quantum-corrections route is recorded as ruled out under the series' reading of how the Higgs field couples to quarks: the measured two-photon rate lies well above the predicted shortfall, the new neutral pair would make bottom mesons turn into their antiparticles far faster than is observed, and the forces among these particles would grow too strong within a few TeV. The working alternative has the second set of particles at a few TeV.)

proofs.main:
\emph{(1).} Take generators $\gamma_{0}, \ldots, \gamma_{3}$ of spacetime and, for each rung plane $a = 4, 5$, $e_{a}$, $f_{a}$ with $e_{a}^{2} = 1$, $f_{a}^{2} = -1$, all mutually orthogonal, and $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} + f_{a})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} - f_{a})$; then $v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$ and $\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \delta_{ab}$, the stored null pairs. A vector orthogonal to the four $\gamma_{\mu}$ anticommutes with each of them, so it commutes with their product $I_{4}$ (four sign changes); $I_{4}^{2} = -1$. This is the stored property that $I_{4}$ commutes with every mode (\claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}), here for the rung modes. Hence $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ acts on $H_{4} \oplus H_{5}$ as a complex structure inside the algebra, and for $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ with $\alpha_{a}, \beta_{a} \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, $c^{2} = \sum_{a,b}\alpha_{a}\beta_{b}\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = Q(c)$, bilinear over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$: the stored complex-bilinear form, its unit read as $I_{4}$. (In the full algebra $I_{4}$ is not central: it anticommutes with the spacetime vectors, as the field theory uses; on the rung summand it commutes.) Four $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ coefficients give four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum, each realised by the polynomial representation of \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(1) with variables indexed by the rung field's modes.

Let $b_{a} = v_{a}w_{a} - \tfrac12 = v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$ and $b = b_{4} + b_{5}$. From $w_{a}v_{a} = 1 - v_{a}w_{a}$ and $v_{a}^{2} = 0$: $v_{a}w_{a}v_{a} = v_{a}$, so $[b, v_{a}] = v_{a}$, and likewise $[b, w_{a}] = -w_{a}$; $b_{4}$ and $b_{5}$ commute (disjoint planes), $b_{a}^{2} = v_{a}w_{a}v_{a}w_{a} - v_{a}w_{a} + \tfrac14 = \tfrac14$, and $(I_{4}b_{a})^{2} = -\tfrac14$. So $e^{tb_{a}} = \cosh\tfrac t2 + 2b_{a}\sinh\tfrac t2$, $e^{\phi I_{4}b_{a}} = \cos\tfrac\phi2 + 2I_{4}b_{a}\sin\tfrac\phi2$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{zb}) = e^{z\,\mathrm{ad}_{b}}$ multiplies $v_{a}$ by $e^{z}$ and $w_{a}$ by $e^{-z}$, for $z = t$ real (the stored $e^{tK}$, $Kv_{a} = v_{a}$, $Kw_{a} = -w_{a}$, \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(4)) and for $z = \phi I_{4}$. On coefficients the latter is $\alpha \mapsto e^{\phi I_{4}}\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto e^{-\phi I_{4}}\beta$, which is $e^{2\phi Y}$ for $Y = \tfrac{1}{2}I_{4}\mathbf{1}$ acting by $\alpha \mapsto Y\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{Y}\beta$. So $Y = \tfrac12 I_{4}K$ on the rung field: the unitary hypercharge flow is the rung boost at $I_{4}$-imaginary rapidity, which is the reading \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes} gives for any plane's modes (real rapidity scales, imaginary rapidity is the unitary phase). The identification is on rung values only: each $\gamma_{\mu}$ anticommutes with $I_{4}$ and commutes with $b$, so it anticommutes with $I_{4}b$, and $e^{\phi I_{4}b}\gamma_{\mu}e^{-\phi I_{4}b} = e^{2\phi I_{4}b}\gamma_{\mu} \ne \gamma_{\mu}$ for $\phi \notin \pi\mathbb{Z}$: the automorphism moves every spacetime vector and does not commute with the Lorentz rotors, so it is not a spacetime-point transformation, while on the rung summand it is the hypercharge phase. The check verifies all of this in $\Cl(3,5)$ at $e^{t} = 4$ and $(\cos\phi, \sin\phi) = (-\tfrac{7}{25}, \tfrac{24}{25})$, including that $\gamma_{0}$ anticommutes with $v_{a}$ and with $I_{4}b$ and that its image is not $\gamma_{0}$.

\emph{(2).} By \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(1), on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $\sum_{j}\mu_{j}^{2} = \tfrac14(\mathsf{N}^{2} - |Q|^{2})$ and $\mu_{Y} = \tfrac12 m$, so $V = F(\mathsf{N}, m) + (k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})|Q|^{2} + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2}$ with $F = \tfrac18 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{2} + \tfrac12 g'^{2}(\tfrac12 m - \zeta)^{2} + W(\mathsf{N})$. Write $A = |\alpha|^{2}$, $B = |\beta|^{2}$, $\mathsf{N} = \tfrac12(A + B)$, $m = \tfrac12(A - B)$. At $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$: $\partial_{B}V = \tfrac12(F_{\mathsf{N}} - F_{m})$, which vanishes by the stored vacuum condition (on the cone it reads $(g^{2} + g'^{2})\lambda^{2} + 4g'^{2}\zeta + 8W' = 0$), so $F_{m} = F_{\mathsf{N}} = \tfrac14 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{*} + W'$. The $\alpha$ directions enter $V$ through $A$ (quadratically in $\alpha$) and through $Q = -\lambda\alpha_{1}$ (linearly in $\alpha_{1}$); hence the first derivatives in $\alpha$ vanish, the $\alpha$-$\beta$ second derivatives vanish, $\alpha_{2}$ does not mix with $\alpha_{1}$, and in real coordinates the Hessian on $\alpha_{2}$ is $2\partial_{A}V = F_{\mathsf{N}} + F_{m} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}^{*} + 2W' = M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$, the stored charged mass, while on $\alpha_{1}$ it is $M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$ plus the Hessian of $\lambda^{2}\bigl((k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})|\alpha_{1}|^{2} + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}\alpha_{1}^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{1}^{2}\bigr)$, the matrix $2\lambda^{2}\bigl((k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})\mathbf{1} + \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}k_{8} & k_{9}\\ k_{9} & -k_{8}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\bigr)$, with eigenvalues $4\mathsf{N}^{*}(k_{10} \pm r) - M_{W}^{2}$. The sum is $2W' + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}(k_{10} \pm r)$. The kinetic coefficient of each real coordinate is one ($2\mathsf{N}(e) = 1$). The $\beta$ block is the stored one: three directions of the gauge orbit (rank three, the generator $Y - T_{3}$ fixing the point) are massless by invariance, and the radial direction has $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 2\mathsf{N}^{*}W''$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(4) at $m^{*} = -\mathsf{N}^{*}$, $H = 0$). Since $Q = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$ has differential $\beta^{\mathsf T}d\alpha + \alpha^{\mathsf T}d\beta = -\lambda\,d\alpha_{1}$ at the point, the normal pair is exactly the pair of directions transverse to $L_{0}$. For the pure D-term ($W = 0$, $k = 0$) its mass vanishes: these are D-flat directions.

\emph{The level.} With $k_{8} = k_{9} = 0$ and the term $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2}$, restrict to $\alpha = (a, 0)$, $\beta = (-\lambda', 0)$ with $a, \lambda'$ real. Since $V$ depends on $a$ only through $a^{2}$ and through $Q = -a\lambda'$, the mixed second derivative in $(a, \lambda')$ vanishes at $a = 0$, so the shift of $\lambda'$ at first order in $H^{2}$ does not enter the $a$-equation at that order. Along real $\alpha_{1} = a$ the part of $V$ without the $k_{10}$ term is quadratic in $a$ at first order, with coefficient half the normal Hessian of (2) at $k_{10} = 0$, that is $W'$; so the $a$-derivative is $2W'a - 2\lambda k_{10}(H^{2} - a\lambda) + O(H^{4})$, which vanishes for $a(2W' + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}k_{10}) = 2\lambda k_{10}H^{2}$, that is $a = \rho H^{2}/\lambda$ with $\rho = 1 - 2W'/m_{H}^{2}$, $m_{H}^{2} = 2W' + 4\mathsf{N}^{*}k_{10}$, and $Q = -\rho H^{2}$. The check verifies this as the vanishing of the constant and linear coefficients in $H^{2}$ of the exact $\alpha_{1}$-gradient, and that $\rho = 1$ fails when $W' \ne 0$. As $k_{10} \to \infty$ with $m_{h}$, $m_{\pm}$ fixed, $\rho \to 1$ and the normal pair decouples: the constrained field is that limit. For $H \ne 0$ the off-diagonal Hessian entries between the normal and neutral directions are of relative order $H^{2}/\mathsf{N}^{*}$ (computed symbolically), about $10^{-88}$ at the weak scale.

\emph{(3).} On the ray $\alpha = 0$, $V = k_{2}|\beta|^{4}$, so the ray is flat exactly when $k_{2} = 0$, which is $a + b - e = 2k_{2} = 0$ in the stored coordinates $a = k_{1} + k_{2} + k_{3}$, $b = k_{1} + k_{2} - k_{3}$, $e = 2(k_{1} - k_{2})$; then $e = 2k_{1}$ and $2a - e = 2k_{3}$. The only term linear in $\alpha$ is $|\beta|^{2}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}Q) = -\lambda^{3}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}\alpha_{1} + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{1})$, a tadpole unless $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$; the $k_{4}, k_{5}$ terms are cubic in $\alpha$ and do not enter the Hessian. As in (2), $\partial_{A}V = k_{3}\lambda^{2}$ gives $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2k_{3}\lambda^{2} = 2(2a - e)\mathsf{N}$ on $\alpha_{2}$, and $\alpha_{1}$ adds $4\mathsf{N}(k_{10} \pm r)$; the radial direction is the flat one (the scalon) and the gauge orbit has rank three. Every term is homogeneous of degree four, so each mass squared is proportional to $\mathsf{N}$. For $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$: $k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} \ge -r|Q|^{2}$, so $V \ge V_{4}(\mathsf{N}, m) + (k_{10} - r)|Q|^{2}$ with $V_{4} = a\mathsf{N}^{2} + bm^{2} + e\mathsf{N}m$; on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $\mathsf{N}^{2} \ge |Q|^{2} + m^{2} \ge m^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), and $V_{4} \ge 0$ for $|m| \le \mathsf{N}$ under the admissibility conditions (\claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(3)); so $V \ge 0$ when $k_{10} \ge r$, the ray is a minimum of $V$ on the unit sphere as the imported Fact requires, and $m_{H,A}^{2} \ge m_{\pm}^{2}$. If $k_{10} + r < -(2a - e)/2$ one normal mass squared is negative (the check exhibits $V = -\tfrac{1}{200}$ next to the ray for $k_{3} = \tfrac12$, $k_{10} = -1$).

\emph{(4).} Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass} applies to real scalars with a scale-free quartic polynomial potential and a flat direction at a minimum on the unit sphere; the linear field of (3) is such a theory (eight real scalars), and the cone $L_{0}$ is not a linear space, so the constrained field is outside the Fact's hypotheses except as a limit. Counting real scalars with masses at $\varphi = v$: the three gauge directions are massless in Landau gauge and the scalon is the flat direction, leaving the charged pair (two) and the normal pair (two); vectors and fermions are as in \claimref{synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev}(i), under the same hypothesis (D). This gives the displayed relation, the standard sum rule of the scale-invariant two-doublet model: J. S. Lee and A. Pilaftsis, Phys. Rev. D 86 (2012) 035004 (arXiv:1201.4891), and K. Lane and W. Shepherd, arXiv:1808.07927, Eq. (10), $(\sum M^{4})^{1/4} = 540$ GeV over the heavy states (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(i); their fermion couplings differ from the series' readings, which the sum rule does not use). Solving for $X = 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$, the right side is $8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} - 6M_{W}^{4} - 3M_{Z}^{4} + 12m_{t}^{4} + \ell$, the expression the stored result calls $2m_{\pm}^{4}$; it increases in $\pi$, $v$, $m_{h}$, $m_{t}$, and the stored check's corner evaluation, repeated here with $\pi \in [\tfrac{333}{106}, \tfrac{355}{113}]$, gives $2 \cdot 450^{4} < X < 2 \cdot 456^{4}$. Then $2m_{\pm}^{4} \le X$ gives $m_{\pm} < 456$; $m_{H}^{4} \le X$ and $X < 542^{4}$ give $m_{H}, m_{A} < 542$ (computed: $X^{1/4}$ lies between $535.8$ and $541.6$ GeV over the box); and $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$ give $4m_{\pm}^{4} \le X < 4 \cdot 383^{4}$. Equality $X = 2m_{\pm}^{4}$, the stored bracket, holds only for $m_{H} = m_{A} = 0$. The normal pair is the neutral component of the doublet $\alpha$, so the $Z$ couples to it with doublet strength and $Z \to HA$ is open when $m_{H} + m_{A} < M_{Z}$; a massless pair would add about half a neutrino species to the $Z$'s invisible width, which the measured $N_{\nu} = 2.9840 \pm 0.0082$ excludes (argued; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(ii)); this does not change the bounds above appreciably, since $M_{Z}^{4}/8 \ll X$.

\emph{Reading.} In the scale-free case the bound $m_{H}^{2} < 542^{2}$ GeV$^{2}$ gives $4\mathsf{N}(k_{10} + r) + m_{\pm}^{2} < 542^{2}$ GeV$^{2}$, so $k_{10} + r < 542^{2}/(2v^{2}) \approx 2.4$ (computed): the null-lift constraint is not imposed by a large coupling, and the elementary rung field under transmutation is two complete doublets with a neutral pair below $542$ GeV. With a level ($\xi \ne 0$, not scale free) $k_{10}$ is free and the constrained field is a limit of the linear one, but $k_{10} \gg 4\pi$ would put the normal pair's quartic beyond perturbation theory (argued). Transport-convenient throughout: the field, the locus, the unit and the boost are the series'; the spectrum and the scalon sum are standard two-doublet and Gildener-Weinberg computations.

\emph{(5).} With $f(\tau) = \arcsin^{2}\sqrt{\tau} = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 1}(4\tau)^{n}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, whose $n = 1$ term is $\tau$, $A_{0} = (f - \tau)/\tau^{2} = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 2}4^{n}\tau^{n - 2}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, a series with positive coefficients and leading term $\tfrac13$, increasing on $0 < \tau < 1$. On the flat ray $m_{\pm}^{2} \propto \varphi^{2}$, so the charged pair's term has unit weight, as in the stored result; the normal pair carries no electric charge. The Standard Model amplitude $A_{\mathrm{SM}} = A_{1}(\tau_{W}) + \tfrac43 A_{1/2}(\tau_{t})$ is negative with $|A_{\mathrm{SM}}| > 1 > A_{0}$ (the check brackets it below $-6.4$), so $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} = ((A_{\mathrm{SM}} + A_{0})/A_{\mathrm{SM}})^{2}$ decreases as $A_{0}$ grows, that is as $m_{\pm}$ decreases. At $m_{\pm} = 456$ GeV, with the stored $m_{h}$, $M_{W}$ and pole $m_{t}$, exact interval arithmetic gives $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$; so the bound holds for every $m_{\pm} \in (m_{h}/2, 456]$ GeV. The check also brackets the rate below $0.900$ and decreasing at $400$, $300$, $200$, $100$ and $70$ GeV (computed: about $0.899$, $0.898$, $0.895$, $0.873$, $0.806$; the heavy limit $A_{0} = \tfrac13$ gives $0.900$). Against the Particle Data Group average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ quoted in the stored result, the deficit is about three standard deviations for every charged mass, so freeing the charged mass through the normal pair does not relieve it.

synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-.technical:
Given the massless two-point function, equal at spacelike separation to $-1/(4\pi^{2}Q(\xi))$ and even (standard), Pauli's free-field argument runs on the series' own polarisation sums. The sums of the stored fields have degree $d = 2s$: $1$ for a scalar, $k\gamma_{0} = 2k_{0}\Lambda(k)$ for the spinor, and the photon's bivector sum, a quadratic in $k$ on the null cone. With weights $1$ and $c$ on particle and antiparticle parts and bracket sign $\eta$, the bracket at spacelike $\xi$ is a nonzero multiple of $(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)(1/Q)$, and $P(\partial)(1/Q) \neq 0$; so in a positive-norm space ($c > 0$) the field is local exactly when $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{2s}$.

The tower's CAR has $\eta = +1$ and the palatial CCR $\eta = -1$, so with positive norm the tower carries local spinor fields and the palatial storey local scalar and photon fields, and an elementary local rung scalar of positive norm is palatial. The positive norm is needed: with an indefinite (Krein) form, $c = -1$, the condition becomes $\eta = (-1)^{2s}$ and a CAR scalar is local, as the Faddeev-Popov ghosts of covariant gauge fixing are. For these free fields the result can stand in for the Jost-point import, traded for locality with positive norm; modular covariance is an alternative premise for the same sign.
synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-.lay: Particles that make up matter obey an exclusion rule, while particles of force and the Higgs do not, and which rule a particle obeys is tied to its spin. Here that tie is derived for the series' simplest fields from one requirement, together with the usual rule that quantum states have positive probabilities: measurements at points too far apart for light to connect must not disturb each other. The series stores exclusion-rule modes in one part of its algebra and the other kind in another; the requirement allows half-integer spin only in the first and whole-number spin only in the second, so an elementary Higgs field would have to be built in the second. Without positive probabilities the rule fails, which is why the bookkeeping fields used to fix gauges can break it.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting and the imported input.} Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ and $Q(\xi) = \xi_{0}^{2} - \xi_{1}^{2} - \xi_{2}^{2} - \xi_{3}^{2}$. The one input from outside the store is the massless two-point function $D_{+}(\xi) = \int d\mu(k)\, e^{-I_{4}k\cdot\xi}$ over the forward null cone with the invariant measure (numbers, the field theory's phases among them, read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$); it is the boundary value $-1/(4\pi^{2}(Q(\xi) - I_{4}0\,\xi_{0}))$, the infinitesimal shift written in scalar form in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, so on the open spacelike set $\{Q < 0\}$ it is the real function $-1/(4\pi^{2}Q(\xi))$, even under $\xi \to -\xi$ (standard; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(i); e.g. the free-field chapters of Streater and Wightman or Birrell and Davies). Only $f = 1/Q$ and its evenness enter the argument and the checks; the constant $-1/(4\pi^{2})$ and the powers of $I_{4}$ are overall nonzero factors and are kept symbolic. The method is Pauli's free-field argument (Pauli 1940, standard; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(ii)); the new content is that the series' own polarisation sums and storeys reproduce it.

\emph{The bracket of a free field.} Let a free field have particle part $\int d\mu\, u(k)a(k)e^{-I_{4}k\cdot x}$ and antiparticle part $\int d\mu\, v(k)b^{*}(k)e^{I_{4}k\cdot x}$, with $[a(k), a^{*}(k')]_{\eta} = [b(k), b^{*}(k')]_{\eta} = \delta$ (the bracket $[x, y]_{\eta} = xy + \eta yx$, $\eta = +1$ for the CAR, $-1$ for the CCR), and suppose the antiparticle sum $\sum vv^{*}$ is $c$ times the particle sum $P(k) = \sum uu^{*}$, $c \neq 0$ real, with $c > 0$ when the Fock space has a positive norm, as for the stored spinor field (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2): the anticommutator is $\sum_{j} 2\alpha_{j}\cos(k_{j}\cdot\xi)\Lambda(k_{j})\chi$, the same $\Lambda(k)$ on both exponentials) and the Hermitian photon (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(4)); for a scalar $P = 1$ and positivity of $\langle bb^{*}\rangle$ forces $c > 0$. On an indefinite (Krein) space $\langle bb^{*}\rangle$ may be negative, and then $c < 0$ is allowed. Then the bracket of the field with its adjoint is the c-number
\[
\int d\mu\,P(k)e^{-I_{4}k\cdot\xi} + \eta c\int d\mu\,P(k)e^{I_{4}k\cdot\xi} = P(I_{4}\partial)D_{+}(\xi) + \eta c\,P(-I_{4}\partial)\bigl[D_{+}(-\,\cdot\,)\bigr](\xi),
\]
$\xi = x - y$, where $P$ is any polynomial agreeing with the sum on the cone (two such differ by $Q(k)R(k)$, and $R(I_{4}\partial)\Box D_{+} = 0$ off the cone since $\Box(1/Q) = 0$ there, checked). For $P$ homogeneous of degree $d$, $P(-I_{4}\partial) = (-1)^{d}P(I_{4}\partial)$, and on the spacelike set $D_{+}(-\xi) = D_{+}(\xi)$, so there the bracket is $-\tfrac{I_{4}^{d}}{4\pi^{2}}(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)f$. The script evaluates the two terms separately, the second from the derivatives of $1/Q$ at $-\xi$ with the chain-rule signs, so the parity is computed, not assumed.

\emph{(1).} Scalar: $P = 1$, $d = 0$. Spinor: by Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1) the one-particle projector is $\Lambda(k) = k\gamma_{0}/(2k_{0})$, the factor $1/(2k_{0})$ belonging to the invariant measure, so $P(k) = k\gamma_{0}$, linear: $P(-k) = -P(k)$. The script checks $\Lambda^{2} = \Lambda$, $k\Lambda = 0$, $P(-k) = -P(k)$ and $P(2k) = 2P(k)$ at five rational null $k$. Photon: by Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(2) the modes at null $k$ are the bivectors $f$ with $kf = 0$; for $\epsilon$ orthogonal to $k$, $k(k \wedge \epsilon) = Q(k)\epsilon - (k\cdot\epsilon)k = 0$, so the modes are $k \wedge \epsilon$ with $\epsilon$ transverse (the script checks two independent transverse $\epsilon$ at each $k$). The polarisation sum on test bivectors is $\sum_{ij}(\delta_{ij} - k_{i}k_{j}/|\mathbf{k}|^{2})\langle A(k \wedge \gamma_{i})\rangle_{0}\langle B(k \wedge \gamma_{j})\rangle_{0}$; the terms of $-\gamma^{\mu}\cdot\gamma^{\nu}$ beyond the transverse projector are proportional to $k^{\mu}$ or $k^{\nu}$ and vanish under $k \wedge$, so on the cone it equals the quadratic polynomial of (1). The script verifies the equality for all $36$ pairs of basis bivectors at five null $k$, and $P(-k) = P(k)$, $P(2k) = 4P(k)$. So $d = 0, 1, 2 = 2s$ for the three fields.

\emph{(2).} $\partial_{\mu}f = -2\xi_{\mu}/Q^{2}$ and $\partial_{\mu}\partial_{\nu}f = -2\gamma_{\mu}\cdot\gamma_{\nu}/Q^{2} + 8\xi_{\mu}\xi_{\nu}/Q^{3}$, exact at rational points. For the spinor $P(\partial)f = \partial^{\mu}f\,\gamma_{\mu}\gamma_{0} = -2\xi\gamma_{0}/Q^{2} \neq 0$. For the photon the script computes the coefficients of the quadratic $P(k)[A, B]$ by polarisation and evaluates $P(\partial)f$ for $A = B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$, nonzero; for the scalar $f \neq 0$. At four rational spacelike points and for $\eta = \pm 1$, $c \in \{1, 2, \tfrac12\}$, the computed bracket vanishes exactly when $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{d}$, and with $c = -1$ added to the sample exactly when $\eta = (-1)^{d}$. Since the bracket is $-\tfrac{I_{4}^{d}}{4\pi^{2}}(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)f$ on the whole spacelike set and $P(\partial)f$ is a nonzero rational function there, the field is local (its bracket vanishes at every spacelike separation, the locality of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2)) if and only if $1 + \eta c(-1)^{d} = 0$, that is, for $c > 0$, $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{d}$, and for $c = -1$, $\eta = (-1)^{d}$. The second case needs a negative-norm antiparticle term: a local anticommuting scalar ($d = 0$, $\eta = +1$, $c = -1$) is the Faddeev-Popov ghost of covariant gauge fixing, which lives on a Krein space (\claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}); so every statement below about which storey carries a local field holds in a positive-norm space. With $\eta = +1$ and $d = 1$ this is the stored anticommutator $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_{0}$, a derivative of the Pauli-Jordan function.

\emph{(3).} A tower plane is realised in $\Cl(1,1)$ by $v = \tfrac12(e + f)$, $w = \tfrac12(e - f)$, $e^{2} = 1$, $f^{2} = -1$: $Q(v) = Q(w) = 0$ and $vw + wv = 1$ (the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), while $vw - wv \neq 1$. The palatial pair on polynomials (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra}), $a = d/dz$, $a^{*} = z$, has $[a, a^{*}]z^{n} = z^{n}$ and $\{a, a^{*}\}z^{n} = (2n + 1)z^{n}$, checked for $n \le 5$. So tower modes give $\eta = +1$, palatial modes $\eta = -1$, and by (2), with positive norm, a tower lift is local only for $d$ odd (the spinor) and a palatial lift only for $d$ even (the scalar and the photon). This is the twistor attachment's sentence (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}) that a CAR lift is local exactly when $2s$ is odd, now for these attached free fields from locality with positive norm and the sums, the Jost-point theorem being traded for those premises (it stays the input for interacting fields). By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower} no floor and no bounded element of the CAR limit carries the CCR, so a local elementary scalar of positive norm, in particular a quantised rung field read as elementary, is a palatial field; the tower's rung vectors are odd CAR elements and as the modes of a local scalar field would violate (2). Bosons made of tower fermions are not excluded by this (they are even composites, with the CCR reached only in the limit of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}).

\emph{Scope.} The result covers the free massless scalar, spinor and Maxwell fields with the stated structure of particle and antiparticle sums; it assumes locality, positive energy and a positive norm, and does not cover interacting fields or the general Wightman setting. For a massive field the same argument needs only that the massive two-point function is real, even and nonzero at spacelike separation (standard; its Bessel-function form is cited from memory and not used). The sign $(-1)^{2s}$ is also the factor by which the boost rotor continued over one modular period ($2\pi$ in imaginary rapidity, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}(iv)) acts on values; that coincidence is not used here, and a derivation from modular covariance rests on a different premise (\claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}). Transport-convenient: the sums and storeys are the series' objects; the locality argument itself is standard.
