proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} Rotors, the bivectors $B_{k}$, the Haar measure and its moments $\int u^{\alpha}dU = \prod_{k}(\alpha_{k} - 1)!!/\prod_{j=0}^{|\alpha|/2 - 1}(4 + 2j)$ (zero unless every $\alpha_{k}$ is even) are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weak-factor-rotor-lattice-strong-coupling-area-law}(i), (ii); the check multiplies rotors by a four-component product compared first with \texttt{GA.mul} on all sixteen basis pairs. Lattice weights, Haar measure and reflection positivity are those of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wilson-lattice-gauge-theory-and-strong-coupling-confinement}.

\emph{Step 1 (the continuum copy; proved).} Write $q = P/D$ with $P = (1 - r^{2}) + 2\sum_{k}x_{k}B_{k}$ and $D = 1 + r^{2}$. Then $P\widetilde P = (1 - r^{2})^{2} + 4r^{2} = D^{2}$, so $q\widetilde q = 1$. The gauge transform of $A = 0$ by $q$ is $A_{i} = \widetilde q\,\partial_{i}q = \widetilde P(D\,\partial_{i}P - P\,\partial_{i}D)/D^{3}$, a bivector-valued rational field; at the origin $A_{1} = 2B_{1} \neq 0$. For the line element $\Omega^{2}$ times the flat one in three dimensions, the divergence of a covector field $A$ is $\Omega^{-3}\sum_{i}\partial_{i}(\Omega A_{i})$ (in index form, $\sqrt{g}\,g^{ij} = \Omega\,\delta_{ij}$, a parenthetical reading), so the Coulomb condition of the round three-sphere is $\sum_{i}\partial_{i}(\Omega A_{i}) = 0$. With $N_{i} = \widetilde P(D\,\partial_{i}P - P\,\partial_{i}D)$, $\Omega A_{i} = 2N_{i}/D^{4}$ and $D^{5}\sum_{i}\partial_{i}(N_{i}/D^{4}) = \sum_{i}(D\,\partial_{i}N_{i} - 4N_{i}\,\partial_{i}D)$, a polynomial valued in the even subalgebra of $\Cl(3,0)$; the check expands it with exact coefficients and finds it zero, while the flat analogue $\sum_{i}(D\,\partial_{i}N_{i} - 3N_{i}\,\partial_{i}D)$ is not zero. (Standard reading: $q$ is the identity map of the three-sphere onto the unit rotors, and $\widetilde q\,dq$ is its left-invariant Maurer-Cartan form, whose components are dual to Killing fields of the round metric and hence co-closed.) For an abelian field the copies of $A = 0$ are $A = d\theta$; the condition gives $\Delta_{S^{3}}\theta = 0$, and on a compact connected manifold $\int\theta\,\Delta\theta = -\int|d\theta|^{2}$ forces $d\theta = 0$. This is (i).

\emph{Step 2 (the lattice copy; computed).} Stationary points of $g \mapsto F_{U}(g)$ at $g = 1$ are the configurations whose lattice divergence $\sum_{\mu}(\langle U_{x,\mu}\rangle_{2} - \langle U_{x - \mu,\mu}\rangle_{2})$ of bivector parts vanishes at every site (first variation of $\langle(1 + \epsilon w_{x})U(1 - \epsilon w_{y})\rangle_{0}$), the lattice Landau gauge. Since $B_{3}^{4} = 1$, $g_{(x,y)} = B_{3}^{x}$ is periodic on four sites; the transformed links are $B_{3}^{x}B_{3}^{-(x+1)} = -B_{3}$ along the first axis and $1$ along the second. Both configurations have constant links and hence zero divergence. The second variation along $g_{x} = 1 + \epsilon w_{x} + \tfrac12\epsilon^{2}w_{x}^{2}$ is $\epsilon^{2}\sum_{\ell}\langle\tfrac12w_{x}^{2}U_{\ell} + \tfrac12U_{\ell}w_{y}^{2} - w_{x}U_{\ell}w_{y}\rangle_{0}$; the check builds its $24 \times 24$ matrix on the three bivector components at the eight sites by polarisation and computes the signature of the Faddeev-Popov form, minus twice that coefficient, by exact congruence: $(21, 0, 3)$ at $U = 1$, where it is the lattice Laplacian with the three global modes as kernel, and $(14, 2, 8)$ at the copy. A configuration whose Faddeev-Popov form has a negative mode is a saddle of $F$ on its orbit and lies outside the Gribov region. The gauge function uses only $B_{3}$, so the copy has a compact $U(1)$ analogue (links $-B_{3}$ in the group $a + bB_{3}$), where the Faddeev-Popov form at the copy is semi-definite; the negative modes come from the off-diagonal terms $\langle B_{a}B_{3}B_{b}\rangle_{0}$, $a, b \in \{1, 2\}$, which couple neighbouring sites and exist only for the non-abelian group. This is (ii).

\emph{Step 3 (the signed count; computed).} With the first rotor fixed and $g$ at the second site, $F(g) = \langle U_{1}\widetilde g\rangle_{0} + \langle gU_{2}\rangle_{0} = \langle g\widetilde{U_{1}}\rangle_{0} + \langle gU_{2}\rangle_{0} = \langle gM\rangle_{0}$, using $\langle X\rangle_{0} = \langle\widetilde X\rangle_{0}$. Along $g\exp(w)$ the first variation is $\langle gwM\rangle_{0} = \langle wMg\rangle_{0}$, zero for all bivectors $w$ exactly when $Mg$ is a scalar, that is $g = \lambda\widetilde M$ with $\lambda$ real; unit length gives $\lambda = \pm(M\widetilde M)^{-1/2} = \pm\tfrac58$. So there are exactly two stationary points. The second variation is $\langle g\,\tfrac12(w_{a}w_{b} + w_{b}w_{a})\,M\rangle_{0} = -\delta_{ab}\langle gM\rangle_{0} = \mp\tfrac85\,\delta_{ab}$, so the Faddeev-Popov forms are $\pm\tfrac85$ times the identity, of determinant signs $+1$ and $-1$; the check computes both matrices and their signatures. Their sum is $0 = \chi(S^{3})$, as the Poincar\'e-Hopf theorem requires for a Morse function on the three-sphere. Neuberger's theorem \cite{Neuberger1987}, as read through \cite{KalloniatisVonSmekalWilliams2005} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-singer-gauge-slice-neuberger-lattice-brst-and-fradkin-shenker-complementarity}(ii)), is the same count for the gauge-fixing functional on any lattice and any compact group: the integral of a BRST-invariant observable over the gauge orbit with the Faddeev-Popov determinant (with sign) is a topological invariant proportional to the Euler characteristic of the gauge group, which vanishes for $SU(2)$ and for $U(1)$; so the gauge-fixed partition function is zero and gauge-fixed expectation values are $0/0$. This general statement is cited, not proved. This is (iii).

\emph{Step 4 (perimeter law at $\beta = 0$; proved).} The weight is $\prod_{\ell}\exp(\kappa\langle\widetilde{\varphi_{x}}U_{\ell}\varphi_{y}\rangle_{0})$ with Haar measure on links and on the unit rotors $\varphi$. The change of variables $U_{\ell} \mapsto \varphi_{x}U_{\ell}\widetilde{\varphi_{y}}$ preserves the Haar measure and $\langle U_{C}\rangle_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weak-factor-rotor-lattice-strong-coupling-area-law}(iv), a gauge transformation by $g = \varphi$), and turns the weight into $\prod_{\ell}\exp(\kappa\langle U_{\ell}\rangle_{0})$ (unitary gauge; the check tests this by integrating over the site rotors with the Haar moments: the hopping term has the moments of $u_{0}$ up to the fourth, and the two-link loop $0 \to 1 \to 0$, integrated over both sites and both links without gauge fixing, has the expansion $\tfrac{\kappa^{2}}{16} - \tfrac{\kappa^{4}}{192} + O(\kappa^{6})$, which is $c(\kappa)^{2}$ to that order); the $\varphi$ integrals then factor out. The links are now independent, each with the conjugation-invariant weight $e^{\kappa u_{0}}$. Its mean $\bar U$ commutes with every rotor, so $\bar U = c(\kappa)$ is a scalar, and $\overline{\widetilde U} = c(\kappa)$ as well. For $C$ using $P$ distinct links once each, independence gives $\langle U_{C}\rangle = c(\kappa)^{P}$ and $\langle\langle U_{C}\rangle_{0}\rangle = c(\kappa)^{P}$, exactly. Expanding, $c = (\kappa m_{2} + \tfrac{\kappa^{3}}{6}m_{4} + \dots)/(1 + \tfrac{\kappa^{2}}{2}m_{2} + \dots)$ with $m_{2} = \int u_{0}^{2}dU = \tfrac14$ and $m_{4} = \tfrac18$, so $c = \tfrac{\kappa}{4} + (\tfrac{1}{48} - \tfrac{1}{32})\kappa^{3} + O(\kappa^{5}) = \tfrac{\kappa}{4} - \tfrac{\kappa^{3}}{96} + O(\kappa^{5})$. The check computes the moments, the gluing value $\int U u_{0}\,dU = \tfrac14$ and $\int U\,dU = 0$ exactly, using the 24 Hurwitz units after checking that they reproduce every Haar moment of degree at most three, and the leading coefficients $4^{-4}$ and $4^{-6}$ of the $1 \times 1$ and $1 \times 2$ loops. Since the Haar measure is symmetric under $u_{0} \mapsto -u_{0}$, the numerator of $c$ is $\int_{u_{0} > 0}u_{0}(e^{\kappa u_{0}} - e^{-\kappa u_{0}})\,dU > 0$, so $c(\kappa) > 0$ for $\kappa > 0$, the loop decays as $e^{-P\ln(1/c)}$, a perimeter law. This is (iv).

\emph{Step 5 (reading; argued).} (a) At small $\beta > 0$ and small $\kappa > 0$ the leading terms of a large $R \times T$ loop are $(\kappa/4)^{2(R + T)}$ and $(\beta/4)^{RT}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weak-factor-rotor-lattice-strong-coupling-area-law}(v)); the first dominates as the loop grows, so the area law of the pure gauge field does not survive the doublet. The full statement, that no phase boundary separates the Higgs and confinement regions for a fundamental Higgs field, is \cite{FradkinShenker1979} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-singer-gauge-slice-neuberger-lattice-brst-and-fradkin-shenker-complementarity}(iii)). The series' Higgs is recorded as two fundamental doublets (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}); that pattern is input here, not derived, and the frozen-length model is the standard proxy. The stored area-law theorem already says its area law is not evidence of confinement; the perimeter law is what is added. (b) The Krein premise is used by the BRST quantisation at the free level and in loops; Steps 1 to 3 show that its gauge fixing is not global beyond perturbation theory, and Gribov's ambiguity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv)) and Singer's theorem \cite{Singer1978} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-singer-gauge-slice-neuberger-lattice-brst-and-fradkin-shenker-complementarity}(i)) are the general statements. Neither refutes the premise (its refutation conditions concern the physical space and gauge dependence of amplitudes), but positivity under (K4) beyond perturbation theory cannot be had from a lattice BRST construction as it stands. (c) As a reading, not adopted by any stored result: the gauge-invariant rotor lattice is a non-perturbative definition available for the weak factor (no colour lattice is stored); it has a positive transfer matrix by reflection positivity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wilson-lattice-gauge-theory-and-strong-coupling-confinement}(ii)) without gauge fixing, ghosts or an indefinite form. (d) Continuum confinement of pure colour, with the asymptotic freedom of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}, is the open mass-gap question; nothing here bears on it.

\emph{Status.} (i) and (iv) proved; (ii) and (iii) computed exactly on the stated lattices, with the general signed count cited; the reading argued. All standard; recomputed in the rotors of the weak factor. Transport-absent.

synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the.formal:
Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$, a null plane $N$ whose generators run along $n = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, the second null direction $\bar n = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, transverse vectors in the span of $\gamma_{1}, \gamma_{2}$, and the transverse bivector $J_{\perp} = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$ ($J_{\perp} = -I_{4}B$, $B = \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}$, the bivector written $J$ in \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}). Separately, $J$ denotes the tower's kernel bivector, $J^{2} = -1$, $J^{*} = -J$, commuting with every tower mode (the unit of \claimref{synthesis.kernel-bivector-is-the-unit-of-hermitian-boson-fields-on-the-tower}); $J_{\perp}$ acts on spacetime multivectors, $J$ on the operators, and the two are not identified. For a vector potential $A$ put $F = \nabla\wedge A$, $F\cdot A = \langle FA\rangle_{1}$, $T(a) = -\tfrac12 FaF$, $\partial_{n} = n\cdot\nabla$, and write $A = \mu\,n + \nu\,\bar n + A_{\perp}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The symplectic current; proved.)} For any two potentials, $\omega = F_{1}\cdot A_{2} - F_{2}\cdot A_{1}$ satisfies $\nabla\cdot\omega = (\nabla\cdot F_{1})\cdot A_{2} - (\nabla\cdot F_{2})\cdot A_{1}$ identically; so $\omega$ is conserved on solutions of the free Maxwell equation $\nabla F = 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Null data; proved, with the quantisation rule a hypothesis.)} $n\cdot(n\cdot F) = 0$, so $n\cdot F = \kappa n + E_{\perp}$ with $E_{\perp}$ transverse; $E_{\perp}$ is gauge invariant and $n\cdot T(n) = -Q(E_{\perp}) > 0$ for $E_{\perp} \ne 0$: the null energy flux through $N$ is positive definite on $E_{\perp}$ and depends on nothing else. In the gauge $n\cdot A = 0$ ($\nu = 0$), $n\cdot F = \partial_{n}A$ and
\[
n\cdot\omega = \partial_{n}A_{1\perp}\cdot A_{2\perp} - \partial_{n}A_{2\perp}\cdot A_{1\perp}
\]
identically: the flux of $\omega$ through $N$ contains the two transverse components alone, with no longitudinal coefficient and no transverse derivative. Taking, as in light-front quantisation, this flux (zero modes dropped) as the symplectic form of the free field, its canonical data on $N$ are $E_{\perp} = \partial_{n}A_{\perp}$, two real fields on each generator, data on distinct generators are independent, and no indefinite form enters. On a generator closed to period $2\pi$ (affine parameter $\lambda$; the discretised light-cone setting) with transverse cell of area $s$, $A_{\perp} = \sum_{i = 1,2}\sum_{k \ge 1}(a_{ik}\cos k\lambda + b_{ik}\sin k\lambda)\gamma_{i}$ (the zero mode carries no $E_{\perp}$), the flux of $\omega$ is $2\pi s\sum k(a_{ik}b_{ik}' - b_{ik}a_{ik}')$ and the null energy $P = \pi s\sum k^{2}(a_{ik}^{2} + b_{ik}^{2})$ generates the future null translations for the bracket $\{a_{ik}, b_{jl}\} = \delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}/(2\pi sk)$. Under the quantisation hypothesis $[\,,\,] = J\{\,,\,\}$ (Dirac's rule, with the tower's unit $J$, chosen because (v) realises these modes on tower pairs; with the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ of the unit principle the algebra is the same), the modes $\alpha_{ik} = (\pi s)^{1/2}k(a_{ik} + Jb_{ik})$ satisfy $[\alpha_{ik}, \alpha_{jl}^{*}] = k\,\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}$, $[\alpha_{ik}, \alpha_{jl}] = 0$, $[P, \alpha_{ik}] = -k\alpha_{ik}$: on each generator, two commuting chiral current algebras ($\alpha_{i,-k} = \alpha_{ik}^{*}$). The orientation of the unit cancels between the quantisation rule and the modes, so the sign $+k$ is fixed by positive null energy alone.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The field theory's unit on the null data and the two helicities; proved.)} For transverse $u$, $I_{4}(\bar n\wedge u) = J_{\perp}(\bar n\wedge u) = -(\bar n\wedge u)J_{\perp}$, while $I_{4}(n\wedge u) = (n\wedge u)J_{\perp}$. The null data sit in the $\bar n\wedge E_{\perp}$ part of $F$ ($E_{\perp}(n\wedge u) = 0$), and $E_{\perp}(I_{4}F) = J_{\perp}E_{\perp} = -E_{\perp}J_{\perp}$: on the null data the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ is the transverse quarter turn, right multiplication by $-J_{\perp}$. With $\varepsilon = \gamma_{1}E_{\perp} \in \mathrm{span}\{1, J_{\perp}\}$, $\varepsilon(I_{4}F) = -J_{\perp}\varepsilon(F)$, so the null data of a field of positive frequency relative to $I_{4}$, $e^{-I_{4}k\lambda}$, have $\varepsilon \propto e^{+J_{\perp}k\lambda}$, while the rotation $E_{\perp} \mapsto RE_{\perp}\tilde R$ about the generator, $R = e^{-J_{\perp}\phi/2}$, is $\varepsilon \mapsto \varepsilon e^{J_{\perp}\phi}$: every null datum of positive frequency relative to $I_{4}$ rotates in the same sense as it translates, one helicity, as in \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(ii), (iii) (null bivectors are $I_{4}$-stable, and with the unit $I_{4}$ positive frequency is helicity $+1$); the negative-frequency data rotate in the opposite sense. On the quantised modes of (ii), the rotation acts on the components and multiplies $\alpha_{\pm,k} = 2^{-1/2}(\alpha_{1k} \mp J\alpha_{2k})$ by $e^{\pm J\phi}$, while the null translation by $t$ multiplies both by $e^{-Jkt}$: the two helicities are the two relative orientations of the transverse rotation and the null translation.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Pair currents of the generators; proved.)} Divide the transverse plane into cells of area $s$, one generator $g$ per cell (the cell form of the transverse delta function of the generator CAR, \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(i)). On each generator let $c_{ga,k}$, $a \in \{+, -\}$ the two chirality channels of the canonical part, $k = 1, \dots, L$ the levels of a window, be tower modes ($c^{*} = v$, $c = w$ of distinct planes, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), and put $j^{xy}_{m} = \sum_{k}c_{x,k}^{*}c_{y,k+m}$ (sum over $k, k + m$ in the window) for labels $x, y$ (generator and channel). The window identity (\claimref{synthesis.density-modes-bosonise-only-along-one-null-direction}(i), here for unequal shifts $m$, $l$) reads, exactly,
\[
[j^{xy}_{m}, j^{zu}_{l}] = \delta_{yz}\!\!\sum_{k,\,k+m,\,k+m+l}\!\! c_{x,k}^{*}c_{u,k+m+l} \;-\; \delta_{xu}\!\!\sum_{k,\,k+l,\,k+l+m}\!\! c_{z,k}^{*}c_{y,k+l+m},
\]
which on vectors edge-clean at the depth of the indices is $\delta_{yz}j^{xu}_{m+l} - \delta_{xu}j^{zy}_{m+l} + m\,\delta_{xu}\delta_{yz}\delta_{m+l,0}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} is the case $x = y = z = u$). By definition, the rotation about a generator acts on the tower modes of channel $\pm$ with weight $\pm\tfrac12$ and the unit $J$: $U(\phi) = \prod_{a,k}(1 + (z_{a} - 1)n_{a,k})$, $z_{\pm} = e^{\pm J\phi/2}$, the mode rotation of \claimref{synthesis.ladder-bosons-inherit-spin-statistics-from-the-single-modes}(i) with these weights, unitary for the CAR adjoint; the weights are matched to those of \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iv), which are stated with Hestenes' unit, not derived from them. The densities $j^{g\pm,g\pm}_{m}$ are invariant (helicity $0$) and the flip currents $j^{g+,h-}_{m}$, $j^{g-,h+}_{m}$ are multiplied by $e^{J\phi}$, $e^{-J\phi}$ (helicity $\pm 1$), the transformation of $\alpha_{\pm,k}$ in (iii).
\item[(v)] \emph{(The photon's relations are collective; proved, with the limit argued.)} For a matrix $M$ over the generators with entries in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ let $\varepsilon_{m} = \sum_{g,h}M_{gh}j^{g+,h-}_{m}$, of helicity $+1$, and let $\Omega$ be the bottom-filled window in every channel of every generator, the band restriction of the null vacuum (\claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii), \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi)). Then $[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{l}] = 0$, $\varepsilon_{m}\Omega = 0$ for $m \ge 1$, the value of $[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{m}^{*}]$ on $\Omega$ is $m\operatorname{tr}MM^{*}$ exactly (no fluctuation), and for $m < l$ the defect $D = [\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{l}^{*}]$ has
\[
\|D\Omega\|^{2} = 2(l - m)\,\|MM^{*}\|_{F}^{2} \;\ge\; \frac{2(l - m)\,(\operatorname{tr}MM^{*})^{2}}{N}
\]
on $N$ generators, with equality exactly when $MM^{*}$ is scalar. Normalised to the photon's central term ($\operatorname{tr}MM^{*} = 1$), the defect is at least $2(l - m)/N$: on one generator ($N = 1$) it is $2(l - m)$, so the flip currents of a single generator never carry the photon's relations, and no smearing over finitely many generators removes it (the finite number of quanta such a mode holds is the quasi-spin capacity of \claimref{synthesis.helicity-one-pair-modes-on-a-null-generator-are-quasi-spins}(iv), of which this is the mean-square side). For a transversally smeared field, $M = \mathrm{diag}(s^{1/2}f(y_{g}))$ with $s\sum_{g}|f(y_{g})|^{2} = 1$, the defect is $2(l - m)\,s\cdot s\sum_{g}|f(y_{g})|^{4}$, which tends to $0$ as $s \to 0$ on the continuum of generators of the null plane (argued, by Riemann sums). So the helicity-covariant relations of (ii) and (iii), $[\alpha_{\pm,k}, \alpha_{\pm,l}^{*}] = k\delta_{kl}$, are carried by transversally smeared flip currents in mean square on the null vacuum in that limit, while the densities carry exact canonical pairs of helicity $0$ on every generator. For the window level operator $H = \sum_{x,k}k\,n_{x,k}$, $[H, j^{xy}_{m}] = -mj^{xy}_{m}$: the flip currents have the linear dispersion of (ii) for the second quantisation of the compression of the null translation generator to the band modes, up to the shift $\tfrac12$ and the band scale (\claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(ii), (iii)), not for the generator itself.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Free Maxwell theory in the spacetime algebra gives, on a null plane, the kinematics of photon quantisation (classical, transverse, as in light-front quantisation): two transverse chiral fields per generator with positive null energy and no indefinite form, the sign of their relations fixed by positive null energy whatever the orientation of the unit, and on the data the unit $I_{4}$ is right multiplication by $-J_{\perp}$. The ladder's fermions add exact canonical pairs of helicity $0$ (density waves, not photons) and the photon's helicity $\pm 1$ relations only collectively, as transversally smeared spin-flip pairs, in mean square on the null vacuum in the continuum of generators, with an exact defect of order $1/N$ and a normalisation that vanishes with the cell size, so that the composite is free. It does not give the transverse dynamics, the coupling to charges, convergence of states, null rotations, or other gauge bosons. So the photon stays elementary (\claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}) and the Krein form a premise (\claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}): the exact composite bosons of the null vacuum have helicity $0$ and live on one generator each.
synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the.technical:
Free Maxwell theory in the spacetime algebra gives the photon's kinematics on a null plane with no indefinite metric. The symplectic current $\omega = F_{1}\cdot A_{2} - F_{2}\cdot A_{1}$ is conserved on free fields, and in the gauge $n\cdot A = 0$ its flux through the plane is $\partial_{n}A_{1\perp}\cdot A_{2\perp} - \partial_{n}A_{2\perp}\cdot A_{1\perp}$: only the two transverse components, with no transverse derivative. The gauge-invariant null data $E_{\perp}$ (the transverse part of $n\cdot F$) carry the positive null energy $-Q(E_{\perp})$, and under Dirac's quantisation rule with a central unit each generator carries two commuting chiral current algebras $[\alpha_{ik}, \alpha_{jl}^{*}] = k\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}$, whose sign does not depend on the orientation of the unit. On the null data $I_{4}$ is right multiplication by $-J_{\perp}$ ($J_{\perp} = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$), so data of positive frequency relative to $I_{4}$ rotate about the generator in the sense in which they translate, one helicity, as in the stored photon modes; the two helicities are the two relative orientations of the rotation and translation phases.

The ladder adds the following. The fermions of the generators supply two chirality channels per generator, whose pair currents obey the level-one current algebra exactly on edge-clean window vectors. With the tower's kernel unit $J$ and channel weights $\pm\tfrac12$, densities have helicity $0$ and spin-flip currents helicity $\pm 1$. For a flip current $\varepsilon_{m} = \sum M_{gh}j^{g+,h-}_{m}$ over $N$ generators, the value of $[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{m}^{*}]$ on the null vacuum is $m\operatorname{tr}MM^{*}$ and the defect $[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{l}^{*}]$, $m < l$, has norm squared $2(l - m)\|MM^{*}\|_{F}^{2} \ge 2(l - m)(\operatorname{tr}MM^{*})^{2}/N$, with equality for uniform smearing. One generator never carries the photon's relations; transversally smeared flip currents do, in mean square on the null vacuum, in the limit of the continuum of generators. Not given: the transverse dynamics, the coupling to charges, or other gauge bosons.
synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the.lay: On a light front the electromagnetic field has a simple set of free data: two numbers per light ray, its two transverse components, with positive energy and no unphysical modes; this much is ordinary electromagnetism written in geometric algebra. The horizon's fermions, two kinds per light ray, can be paired up into wave-like modes. Pairs that keep the fermion's kind give exact boson waves, but they do not turn under rotations about the light ray as light does, so they are not photons. Pairs that flip the kind turn like light's two helicities, but on a single light ray they are not exact bosons; averaged over many neighbouring light rays the error shrinks like one over their number, so they reproduce the photon's commutation relations on the vacuum, on average, in the limit of infinitely many light rays. The dynamics across rays, the coupling to charges and the other force carriers are not given.

\emph{(v)} The span of the pair currents of one generator over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ decomposes under $U(\phi)$ into the phases $1$ (densities), $z_{+}^{2}$ ($j^{+-}_{m}$) and $z_{-}^{2}$ ($j^{-+}_{m}$), so its helicity $+1$ part is spanned by the $j^{+-}_{m}$. By (iv), $[j^{+-}_{m}, j^{+-}_{l}] = 0$ ($\delta_{bc} = \delta_{ad} = 0$) and on edge-clean vectors $[j^{+-}_{m}, j^{-+}_{l}] = j^{++}_{m+l} - j^{--}_{m+l} + m\,\delta_{m+l,0} = 2j^{3}_{m+l} + m\,\delta_{m+l,0}$. Let $\Omega$ be the bottom-filled window (each channel filled up to a level $h$ with the depth conditions); by \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi) this is the restriction to band modes of the null vacuum of \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii), the filled sea of negative null momentum on every generator. For $q < 0$, $j^{aa}_{q}\Omega = \sum_{k}c_{a,k}^{*}c_{a,k+q}\Omega$ is a sum of $|q|$ orthogonal unit vectors (a particle at $k > h$ and a hole at $k + q \le h$), so $\|j^{aa}_{q}\Omega\|^{2} = |q|$, and the two channels give orthogonal vectors: $\|2j^{3}_{q}\Omega\|^{2} = 2|q|$. (Checked: $2$ for $(m, l) = (0, -1)$ at $L = 3$ and $(1, -2)$ at $L = 4$, and $4$ for $(0, -2)$ and $(-1, -1)$ at $L = 4$.)

\emph{Many generators.} With $g, h$ labelling generators, $\varepsilon_{m}^{*}$ has coefficients $ ar M$ and the roles of the channels exchanged, and the CAR identity gives, on vectors edge-clean in every generator,
\[
[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{l}^{*}] = \sum_{g,g'}(MM^{*})_{gg'}j^{g+,g'+}_{m-l} - \sum_{h,h'}(M^{*}M)_{h'h}j^{h-,h'-}_{m-l} + m\,\delta_{ml}\operatorname{tr}MM^{*},
\]
with $j^{x,y}_{q} = \sum_{k}c_{x,k}^{*}c_{y,k+q}$ across generators. For $m = l$ the operator part has expectation $\sum_{g}(MM^{*})_{gg}h - \sum_{h}(M^{*}M)_{hh}h = 0$ on $\Omega$, so the central value is $m\operatorname{tr}MM^{*}$. For $m < l$, $q = m - l < 0$, the vectors $j^{x,y}_{q}\Omega$ for distinct pairs $(x, y)$ are orthogonal (distinct occupation patterns) and each has norm squared $|q|$, as in the one-generator case (for $x 
e y$ the particle and the hole sit in different channels, with the same count of positions). So $\|D\Omega\|^{2} = |q|(\|MM^{*}\|_{F}^{2} + \|M^{*}M\|_{F}^{2}) = 2|q|\,\|MM^{*}\|_{F}^{2}$, since $\|M^{*}M\|_{F}^{2} = \operatorname{tr}(M^{*}MM^{*}M) = \operatorname{tr}(MM^{*}MM^{*})$. For the self-adjoint $H = MM^{*}$ on $N$ generators, Cauchy and Schwarz give $(\operatorname{tr}H)^{2} \le N\operatorname{tr}H^{2} = N\|H\|_{F}^{2}$, with equality exactly when $H$ is scalar. (Checked on two generators for $M = 1$, $ egin{pmatrix}1&1\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $ egin{pmatrix}2&0\1&1\end{pmatrix}$: norms $4$, $14$, $56$, central values $2$, $3$, $6$, equality only for $M = 1$; on three generators with $M = 1$: norm $6$, central value $3$.) For $M = \mathrm{diag}(s^{1/2}f(y_{g}))$, $\operatorname{tr}MM^{*} = s\sum_{g}|f(y_{g})|^{2}$ and $\|MM^{*}\|_{F}^{2} = s^{2}\sum_{g}|f(y_{g})|^{4}$, a Riemann sum for $s\int|f|^{4}d^{2}y$, which tends to $0$ as $s 	o 0$ for bounded $f$ of compact support (argued). The same bound applied to $\varepsilon_{\pm}$ built from $j^{+-}$ and $j^{-+}$ gives the relations stated, the commutator $[\alpha_{+,k}, \alpha_{-,l}^{*}]$ corresponding to $[j^{+-}_{k}, j^{+-}_{-l}] = 0$ exactly and $[\alpha_{+,k}, \alpha_{-,l}]$ to $2j^{3}_{k+l}$, which annihilates $\Omega$ for $k, l \ge 1$.

\emph{(v), the diagonal value and the dispersion.} For $m = l$ the operator part is a combination of $j^{xy}_{0}$, and $j^{xy}_{0}\Omega = \delta_{xy}h\Omega$, so $[\varepsilon_{m}, \varepsilon_{m}^{*}]\Omega = m\operatorname{tr}MM^{*}\,\Omega$ exactly, with no fluctuation; the defect lives only in the off-diagonal commutators. The identity $[H, j^{xy}_{m}] = -mj^{xy}_{m}$ (proved in (iv)) concerns the window level operator $H = \sum k\,n_{x,k}$; on the full generator the band modes are not eigenvectors of the null translation generator, and its compression to them is diagonal with weights proportional to $k + 	frac12$ (\claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(ii), (iii)), so the linear dispersion holds for the second quantisation of that compression, up to the shift and the band scale, and not for the generator itself.

synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gaug.formal:
In the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}: $\mathcal{R}_{\C} = (H_{4} \oplus H_{5}) \otimes \C$ (the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ commutes with the rung vectors, and numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, which is the $\C$ of this statement) with $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$, $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, $\mathsf{N}(c) = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$, $m(c) = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})$, the slot mixing $U(2)$ acting by $\alpha \mapsto X\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{X}\beta$ (generators $T_{j} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}$, $Y = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\mathbf{1}$), $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, the null-lift locus $L = \{Q(c) = -H^{2}\}$, the lift family $c_{\lambda} = -\lambda w_{4} + \tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda}v_{4}$ and the rung unit $u_{\lambda} = dc_{\lambda}/d\lambda$. Call a \emph{one-doublet subspace} a $U(2)$-invariant real subspace of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ of real dimension four, and a one-doublet field a field valued in one.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Classification.)} The real-linear $U(2)$-equivariant maps from the doublet $\C^{2}$ (generators $T_{j}$, $Y$) to $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ are $\gamma \mapsto (p\gamma, q\bar{\gamma})$, $p, q \in \C$, a real four-dimensional space, and each nonzero one is injective. The one-doublet subspaces are $D_{0} = \{\beta = 0\}$, $D_{\infty} = \{\alpha = 0\}$ and the graphs $G_{a} = \{\beta = a\bar{\alpha}\}$, $a \in \C \setminus \{0\}$.
\item \emph{(One orbit, one frame.)} $Q$ vanishes on $D_{0}$ and $D_{\infty}$, which miss $L$. On $G_{a}$, $Q(\alpha, a\bar{\alpha}) = a|\alpha|^{2}$ and $m/\mathsf{N} = (1 - |a|^{2})/(1 + |a|^{2})$; so $G_{a}$ meets $L$ only when $a = -r$, $r > 0$, and then $G_{-r} \cap L = \{|\alpha|^{2} = H^{2}/r\}$ is one $U(2)$-orbit, a three-sphere, which contains $c_{\lambda}$ exactly when $\lambda^{2} = rH^{2}$. The frame of a vacuum on $G_{-r} \cap L$ is fixed by $r$.
\item \emph{(Pure gauge on the locus.)} At $c_{\lambda}$ the tangent spaces of $G_{-r}$ and of $L$ meet in the tangent space of the gauge orbit, of dimension three. So the rung unit $u_{\lambda}$ and the charged plane of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(3) lie in no one-doublet subspace through $c_{\lambda}$, and the smallest $U(2)$-invariant real subspace containing $c_{\lambda}$ and $u_{\lambda}$ is $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$.
\item \emph{(The one physical mode leaves the locus.)} In $G_{-r}$ the complement of the gauge orbit at $c_{\lambda}$ for $\operatorname{Re}(x^{*}\cdot y)$ is the line of $c_{\lambda}$, along which $dQ = 2Q(c_{\lambda}) = -2H^{2} \neq 0$: a direction normal to $L$, while $Q(c_{\lambda}, u_{\lambda}) = 0$.
\item \emph{(Size of the distinction; computed.)} The one-doublet subspace through $c_{\lambda}$ is $G_{-r}$ with $r = \lambda^{2}/H^{2}$; its radial direction $c_{\lambda}/\lambda = (\tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}e_{4}, -e_{4})$ and the rung unit $u_{\lambda} = (-\tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}e_{4}, -e_{4})$ differ by $\tfrac{2H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}e_{4}$ in the $\alpha$-coefficient, a relative angle of order $H^{2}/\lambda^{2}$ (of order $H^{2}/v^{2}$ at the stored vacuum, where $\lambda^{2}$ is of the order of the weak scale squared); and along the radial direction the term $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2}$ of the linear field adds a mass squared of order $k_{10}H^{4}/\lambda^{2}$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence a field whose restriction to $L$ carries the rung unit and the charged pair of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(3) takes values in all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$. The count of two doublets follows if the null-lift constraint is imposed exactly (the limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ of the linear field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), the neutral physical scalar is exactly the rung unit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(3)) and the field is linear; it does not follow at finite $k_{10}$, where by (5) a one-doublet field reproduces the rung-unit direction to relative order $H^{2}/\lambda^{2}$. The representation $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, one doublet and its conjugate, is fixed by the ten (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}); it does not by itself choose between a field in a real form (one doublet; the tower's conjugation fixes $G_{1}$, which misses $L$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(5)) and a field in all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ (two).
synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gaug.technical:
The rung field takes values in the complexified rung summand: eight real components that carry one weak doublet of hypercharge one half and its conjugate, which as a complex field are two hypercharge-one-half doublets. The four-dimensional pieces a single doublet could occupy are classified exactly. They are the two complex doublets, on which the null-lift form $Q$ vanishes, and the graphs $\beta = a\bar{\alpha}$, on which $Q = a|\alpha|^{2}$ and the ratio of the hypercharge moment map to the norm is constant. A graph reaches the null-lift locus only for real negative $a$, and then in a single gauge orbit at a single frame set by $a$. On the exact locus, therefore, a one-doublet field is pure gauge. The rung unit, the frame boost that the stored theory identifies with the neutral physical scalar, is not tangent to any one-doublet piece through the vacuum, and neither is the charged pair. The smallest invariant space containing the vacuum and the rung unit is the whole summand. The single physical mode a one-doublet field has is its radial direction, which changes $Q$.

The count of two doublets is a consequence of three readings, each taken exactly: the null-lift constraint imposed as a hard constraint, the Higgs identified exactly with the rung unit, and a linear field. At any finite constraint coupling the distinction is tiny. The radial direction of the one-doublet piece through the vacuum differs from the rung unit by a relative angle of order $H^{2}/v^{2}$, about $10^{-88}$ at the stored frame. The constraint term shifts its mass squared only by an amount of order $k_{10}H^{4}/v^{2}$. The hard limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ is not a perturbative decoupling. The rung quartics run to strong coupling within a few TeV on the transmutation branch (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch}). The decoupling that flavour allows, through the level, makes the whole second doublet heavy and leaves one light doublet at low energy (\claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch}). In two-doublet language the rung unit is the standard direction that changes the ratio of the two vacuum values, which a single doublet lacks. The ten fixes the representation but not the count: the tower's conjugation selects a one-doublet real form that misses the locus.
synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gaug.lay: In this framework the Higgs field lives in an eight-dimensional space whose directions come from the geometry that transport adds. The Standard Model uses one Higgs doublet, which has four real directions. This result asks whether four of the eight directions could be enough here. If the framework's vacuum condition is imposed exactly, they are not. Any four-direction slice that respects the weak and hypercharge symmetries either never meets that condition or meets it only along directions that are pure gauge, which the massive W and Z bosons absorb. The particle the framework identifies with the observed Higgs boson, a change of the frame in which the vacuum is read, points out of every such slice. If the condition is only approximate, as it is in a field theory with finite couplings, one doublet can imitate that particle to about one part in $10^{88}$. So the need for a second doublet rests on taking the condition and the identification exactly, not on anything measurable at present.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} As in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}: $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ has complex coordinates $(\alpha, \beta) \in \C^{2} \times \C^{2}$, with $\C = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (the field theory's unit $I_{4}$), $U(2)$ acts by $\alpha \mapsto X\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{X}\beta$, and by Proposition \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are} the $v$-coefficients carry a weak doublet of hypercharge $\tfrac12$ and the $w$-coefficients its conjugate. The Hermitian form is $\operatorname{Re}(c^{*}\cdot d)$ with $c^{*} = \theta(\bar{c})$, so $(\alpha, \beta)^{*} = (\bar{\beta}, \bar{\alpha})$ and $\mathsf{N}(c) = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$. Let $D = \C^{2}$ with the same generators $T_{j} = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}$, $Y = \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\mathbf{1}$, viewed as a real representation of dimension four.

\emph{(1).} $D$ is irreducible as a real representation: $SU(2)$ acts transitively on the unit sphere of $D$, so a nonzero invariant real subspace contains a sphere's worth of directions and is all of $D$. Its real-linear equivariant endomorphisms commute with the central generator $Y$, which acts as $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}$, so they are complex-linear, and by Schur's lemma they are the complex scalars. The map $\beta \mapsto \bar{\beta}$ carries $(\C^{2}, \bar{X})$ to $(\C^{2}, X)$ equivariantly, so as a real representation $\mathcal{R}_{\C} \cong D \oplus D$, and the real-linear equivariant maps $D \to \mathcal{R}_{\C}$ are $\gamma \mapsto (p\gamma, q\bar{\gamma})$ with $p, q \in \C$, a real four-dimensional space; a nonzero one is injective because its kernel is an invariant subspace of the irreducible $D$. The script solves the intertwining equations for an unknown real $8 \times 4$ matrix against the four generators, by exact elimination, finds a solution space of real dimension four, and checks that it equals the span of the four maps $(p, q) = (1, 0), (I_{4}, 0), (0, 1), (0, I_{4})$, while the inequivariant map $\gamma \mapsto (\bar{\gamma}, 0)$ fails the equations. By complete reducibility for the compact group $U(2)$, an invariant real subspace of dimension four is isomorphic to $D$, so it is the image of such a map: $D_{0}$ for $q = 0$, $D_{\infty}$ for $p = 0$, and otherwise $\{(p\gamma, q\bar{\gamma})\} = \{\beta = a\bar{\alpha}\}$ with $a = q/\bar{p}$.

\emph{(2).} On $D_{0}$ and $D_{\infty}$ one of $\alpha$, $\beta$ vanishes, so $Q = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = 0 \neq -H^{2}$. On $G_{a}$, $Q = \alpha^{\mathsf T}a\bar{\alpha} = a|\alpha|^{2}$, $\mathsf{N} = \tfrac12(1 + |a|^{2})|\alpha|^{2}$ and $m = \tfrac12(1 - |a|^{2})|\alpha|^{2}$. So $Q = -H^{2}$ forces $a|\alpha|^{2} = -H^{2}$, that is $a = -r$ with $r > 0$ and $|\alpha|^{2} = H^{2}/r$; $U(2)$ preserves $G_{-r}$ and acts on $\alpha$ by $X$, and $SU(2)$ is transitive on the three-sphere $|\alpha|^{2} = H^{2}/r$, so $G_{-r} \cap L$ is one orbit. The lift point $c_{\lambda}$ has $\alpha = \tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda}e_{4}$, $\beta = -\lambda e_{4}$, so it lies in $G_{a}$ exactly for $a = -\lambda^{2}/H^{2}$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(4) the frame of a charge-preserving point is fixed by $m$, here by $m/\mathsf{N} = (1 - r^{2})/(1 + r^{2})$, a constant of the subspace. The script checks these identities exactly for five values of $a$ (real and complex) and three $\alpha$ each, and the membership of $c_{\lambda}$ for fifteen pairs $(H^{2}, \lambda)$.

\emph{(3).} $G_{-r}$ is a linear subspace, so its tangent space at $c_{\lambda}$ is $G_{-r}$ itself; the tangent space of $L$ is $\ker dQ$, $dQ(c)[x] = 2Q(c, x)$ (two real conditions). Since $G_{-r} \cap L$ is one orbit of dimension three (the stabiliser of $c_{\lambda}$ is a circle, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(1)), and the gauge tangent vectors $T_{j}c_{\lambda}$, $Yc_{\lambda}$ lie in both $G_{-r}$ and $\ker dQ$, the intersection is the gauge tangent provided it has dimension three, which follows directly: for $x = (\delta\alpha, -r\overline{\delta\alpha})$, $Q(c_{\lambda}, x) = \tfrac12(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\delta\beta + \beta^{\mathsf T}\delta\alpha) = -\tfrac{\lambda}{2}(\overline{\delta\alpha_{4}} + \delta\alpha_{4})$, using $rH^{2}/\lambda = \lambda$, which vanishes exactly when $\operatorname{Re}\delta\alpha_{4} = 0$, a real three-dimensional space. The rung unit $u_{\lambda} = (-\tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}e_{4}, -e_{4})$ is not in $G_{-r}$: there $\delta\beta = -r\overline{\delta\alpha} = +e_{4}$. The physical directions of $L$ at $c_{\lambda}$, the neutral line of $u_{\lambda}$ and the charged plane (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(3)), are by definition complementary to the gauge tangent inside $T_{c_{\lambda}}L$, so none lies in $G_{-r} \cap T_{c_{\lambda}}L$; and $c_{\lambda}$ lies in no other one-doublet subspace by (2). An invariant real subspace containing $c_{\lambda}$ contains its $U(2)$-span, which is $G_{-r}$ (four-dimensional, by (1) and (2)); adding $u_{\lambda} \notin G_{-r}$ gives a subspace of dimension greater than four, which by complete reducibility and $\mathcal{R}_{\C} \cong D \oplus D$ is $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$. The script computes, for fifteen pairs $(H^{2}, \lambda)$ by exact rank: $G_{-r} \cap \ker dQ$ of dimension three equal to the gauge tangent, $u_{\lambda}$ and the two charged directions (solved as the kernel of $dQ$, the gauge tangents and $u_{\lambda}$ for the Hermitian form) outside $G_{-r}$, the generated span of $\{c_{\lambda}, u_{\lambda}\}$ of real rank eight and that of $c_{\lambda}$ equal to $G_{-r}$.

\emph{(4).} Inside $G_{-r}$ the gauge tangent has dimension three, so its complement for $\operatorname{Re}(x^{*}\cdot y)$ is a line; $c_{\lambda}$ is orthogonal to the gauge tangent, since $\operatorname{Re}(c^{*}\cdot Tc) = 0$ for every anti-Hermitian generator $T$, and so spans it. Along it $dQ(c_{\lambda})[c_{\lambda}] = 2Q(c_{\lambda}) = -2H^{2}$, so it changes $Q$; by contrast $Q(c_{\lambda}, u_{\lambda}) = \tfrac12(\tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda}\cdot(-1) + (-\lambda)(-\tfrac{H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}})) = 0$. The script finds the complement by exact elimination and checks both values. In the linear field the directions changing $Q$ are the neutral normal pair, of mass squared $2W' + 4\mathsf{N}(k_{10} \pm r)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}; there $r$ denotes a coupling, not the graph parameter), which grows without bound as $k_{10} \to \infty$.

\emph{(5).} The radial line of $G_{-r}$ at $c_{\lambda}$ is that of $c_{\lambda}$, and $c_{\lambda}/\lambda - u_{\lambda} = (\tfrac{2H^{2}}{\lambda^{2}}e_{4}, 0)$ exactly (checked), while both have $\beta$-component $-e_{4}$; so the angle between the two directions is of order $H^{2}/\lambda^{2}$. Along $c = (1 + t)c_{\lambda}$, $Q(c) = (1 + t)^{2}Q(c_{\lambda})$, so $Q + H^{2} = -2H^{2}t + O(t^{2})$ and $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2} = 4k_{10}H^{4}t^{2} + O(t^{3})$; with the kinetic coefficient $\mathsf{N}(c_{\lambda}) = \tfrac12(\lambda^{2} + H^{4}/\lambda^{2})$ for $t$ the added mass squared is of order $8k_{10}H^{4}/\lambda^{2}$ (computed, up to the normalisation convention of the kinetic term). At the stored frame $\lambda^{2}/H^{2} = e^{2\eta}$ is of order $10^{88}$, so both are negligible at any finite $k_{10}$.

\emph{Conclusion.} On the exact locus a one-doublet field is pure gauge, and its one physical direction is normal to the locus. The stored theory's neutral physical scalar is the rung unit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(3)) and it carries a charged pair; by (3) a field whose restriction to $L$ carries both takes values in a subspace containing $c_{\lambda}$ and $u_{\lambda}$, which is all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$. This gives two doublets under three readings taken exactly: the null-lift constraint as a hard constraint, the Higgs exactly the rung unit, and a linear field. By (5) it does not follow at finite $k_{10}$, where a one-doublet field reproduces the rung-unit direction to relative order $H^{2}/\lambda^{2}$; and the hard limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ is a nonlinear limit, not a perturbative decoupling. The representation $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ is that of the ten; it admits the one-doublet real forms $G_{a}$, among them $G_{1}$, fixed by the tower's conjugation ($\beta = \bar{\alpha}$, where $Q = |\alpha|^{2} > 0$), and $G_{-1}$, which meets $L$ only at the balanced frame (as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-is-frame-boost}(5)); so the representation alone does not fix the count. Standard content: in two-doublet language $u_{\lambda}$ changes the ratio $|\alpha|/|\beta|$ of the two vacuum values at fixed $\alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, a direction a single doublet lacks. The result is transport-convenient: the summand, the locus and the frame are transport's, the argument is linear algebra.

synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-.technical:
In a covariant gauge, under the indefinite-form (Krein) premise for the gauge field (\claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}; the covariant photon propagator inside loops is imported, \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}), with the Dirac matrices as the spacetime algebra's product, propagator numerators $k + m$, the vertex $\gamma^{\mu}$, the units of the Feynman rules and the Wick rotation written as the right unit $I_{4}$, outside the Clifford product, and imported Pauli-Villars regulators of positive and negative weight ($\sum c_{i} = \sum c_{i}M_{i}^{2} = 0$; fermions on the fermion loop, a photon on the photon line), one-loop electrodynamics reproduces the standard results with exact rational coefficients. The trace is four times the scalar part, and the chiral traces are $2\proj$ read with the pseudoscalar sent to $\mp$ the unit $I_{4}$.

The vacuum-polarisation numerator after the shift is $a \mapsto -2Q(\ell)a + 8x(1-x)(Q(q)a - (a\cdot q)q) + 4\Delta a$; the part proportional to $a$ has radial integral $L - \Delta + \Delta^{2}/(L+\Delta)$ and cancels under the regulators, leaving a transverse polarisation whose logarithm has coefficient $e^{2}/(12\pi^{2})$ per Dirac fermion ($\int_{0}^{1}x(1-x)\,dx = 1/6$). For a massless chiral fermion the numerator's $I_{4}$ part vanishes after the shift and symmetric integration and its scalar part is half; this is a statement about the numerator, since the regulators carry Dirac masses.

In the vertex the four-dimensional contraction identities and the on-shell projectors leave a magnetic coefficient $b = 2mz(1-z)$, the Gordon identity carries the real bivector $\gamma^{\mu} \wedge q$, and the exact parameter integral gives $F_{2}(0) = \alpha/(2\pi)$. The resolvent identity $S(k+h) - S(k) = -S(k+h)hS(k)$ gives the Ward-Takahashi identity integrand by integrand, so $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$.

Placing the unit as $I_{4}$ inside the product at each propagator instead flips the mass term: harmless on massless chiral lines, but on a massive loop it leaves a non-transverse remainder proportional to $\sum c_{i}M_{i}^{2}\ln\Delta_{i}$, so on massive lines the unit stands outside the product.
synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-.lay: The standard first quantum corrections of electrodynamics, the screening of charge by virtual pairs, the electron's extra magnetic moment and the identity that keeps charge the same at every order, come out of the series' algebra of spacetime with the usual numbers. Two standard ingredients are taken from the literature: the usual covariant description of the photon inside loops, and the usual way of taming the infinities with heavy auxiliary particles, some of which enter with negative weight; both rest on a premise the series adopts, that the photon's states carry the standard indefinite measure in which some unphysical states have negative length. The charge screening has the textbook strength, the magnetic correction is the fine-structure constant over two pi, and the magnetic structure is a plain plane element of spacetime with no imaginary number in it. One point is specific to the series: its imaginary unit, the spacetime volume element, may sit inside the algebraic products only on massless lines; on massive lines it must stay outside, or charge conservation fails.

synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-.formal:
Work in a covariant gauge (the background Feynman gauge with Faddeev-Popov ghosts), under the indefinite-form (Krein) premise for the gauge field, Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}. Let $F = \sum_{\mu<\nu}F^{\mu\nu}\gamma_{\mu}\gamma_{\nu}$ be a field-strength bivector of $\Cl(1,3)$ and $X = F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$, so that $\langle F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -X/2$. Let $M(F)$ be its Lorentz generator in a field's spin representation: $a \mapsto a\cdot F$ on vectors, $\psi \mapsto \tfrac12F\psi$ on the minimal left ideal $\Cl^{+}(1,3)P$, $P = \tfrac12(1 + \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0})$, which is $I_{4}$-stable and so, with the unit $I_{4}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}, a two-dimensional complex space (one Weyl spinor). Define the spin weight $s = 4\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\,M(F)^{2}/X$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $s = 0$ for a scalar, $-1$ for the Weyl ideal, $-2$ for the whole even algebra (a Dirac field of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}, two ideals of one chirality with the unit $I_{4}$) and $-4$ for a vector; on the Weyl ideal the $I_{4}$-complex trace of the squared spin coupling $E = 2M(F)$ is $2F^{2} \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, whose $I_{4}$ part is the parity-odd $F \wedge F$.
\item With the heat-kernel coefficient $\tfrac{1}{12}\Omega_{\mu\nu}\Omega^{\mu\nu} + \tfrac12E^{2}$ of a Laplace-type operator on a flat background (imported, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-heat-kernel-coefficients-and-background-field-gauge}; $a_{2}$ in DeWitt's numbering, $a_{4}$ in Vassilevich's), a field with $n$ components, statistics $\sigma$ and determinant weight $w$ contributes $b = \tfrac13\sigma w(n + 6s)$ per unit index: $\tfrac13$ for a complex scalar, $\tfrac23$ for a Weyl spinor, $\tfrac43$ for a Dirac spinor, $-\tfrac{10}{3}$ for the gauge vector in the background Feynman gauge and $-\tfrac13$ for its Faddeev-Popov ghosts, so $-\tfrac{11}{3}$ for the gauge field, split as $+\tfrac13$ orbital and $-4$ spin.
\item For the derived algebra $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} acting on $\C^{2}$ and on $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$: $T = \tfrac12$ on $\C^{2}$, $\C^{3}$ and $\Lambda^{2}\C^{3}$, $T = 0$ on $\Lambda^{0}$ and $\Lambda^{3}$, and $C_{2} = 2$, $3$ for the adjoints; for $\su(2)$ as the bivectors of $\Cl(3,0)$ acting on the even algebra (a doublet with the central unit $e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$) and on the bivectors, $C_{2}/T = 4$.
\item Under (S), with $n_{g}$ copies of the content of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency} and $n_{h}$ complex doublets of hypercharge $\tfrac12$, both counts inputs, in the normalisation $a_{1} = \tfrac35\alpha_{Y}^{-1}$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-one-loop-running-trace-ratio},
\[
(b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}) = \Bigl(\tfrac{4n_{g}}{3} + \tfrac{n_{h}}{10},\; -\tfrac{22}{3} + \tfrac{4n_{g}}{3} + \tfrac{n_{h}}{6},\; -11 + \tfrac{4n_{g}}{3}\Bigr),
\]
which is $(\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$ at $(n_{g}, n_{h}) = (3, 1)$, the imported values, and $(\tfrac{21}{5}, -3, -7)$ at $(3, 2)$. The $\su(3)$ factor is asymptotically free exactly when $n_{g} \leq 8$ and the $\su(2)$ factor exactly when $8n_{g} + n_{h} < 44$; at $n_{g} = 3$ both are, for every $n_{h} \leq 19$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-.technical:
In a covariant gauge, under the indefinite-form (Krein) premise for the gauge field (\claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), the spin coupling of every one-loop operator in a background gauge field is twice the Lorentz generator of the field-strength bivector $F$ in the field's spin representation, and its trace is a Clifford computation: on vectors ($a \mapsto a\cdot F$) the spin weight $s = 4\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\,M(F)^{2}/X$ is $-4$; on a minimal left ideal of the even algebra, which with the unit $I_{4}$ is one Weyl spinor, it is $-1$, the $I_{4}$-complex trace of the squared coupling being $2F^{2}$ with $I_{4}$ part $F \wedge F$; on the whole even algebra it is $-2$; on a scalar $0$.

With the imported heat-kernel coefficient $\tfrac{1}{12}\Omega^{2} + \tfrac12E^{2}$ and the background-field bookkeeping (\claimref{synthesis.imported-heat-kernel-coefficients-and-background-field-gauge}) with Faddeev-Popov ghosts, each field contributes $\tfrac13\sigma w(n + 6s)$ per unit index: $\tfrac13$ (complex scalar), $\tfrac23$ (Weyl), $-\tfrac{11}{3}$ (gauge field and ghosts). With the indices of the derived algebra computed on $\C^{2}$ and $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and, under (S), the derived content with $n_{g}$ generations and $n_{h}$ doublets taken as inputs, $b = (\tfrac{4n_{g}}{3} + \tfrac{n_{h}}{10}, -\tfrac{22}{3} + \tfrac{4n_{g}}{3} + \tfrac{n_{h}}{6}, -11 + \tfrac{4n_{g}}{3})$: $(\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$ at three generations and one doublet, $(\tfrac{21}{5}, -3, -7)$ at two doublets. Colour is asymptotically free for $n_{g} \leq 8$ and the weak factor for $8n_{g} + n_{h} < 44$, so at three generations both are for every $n_{h} \leq 19$.
synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-.lay: How fast the strengths of the forces change with energy is fixed, at the first quantum correction, by a sum over the particles, each weighted by a number that depends on its spin. Those weights come out of the series' algebra of spacetime as traces of how a field's spin responds to a force field, once a standard heat-kernel formula and the standard covariant treatment of the force fields are taken from the literature. The number of generations and of Higgs doublets are inputs, since the store has not settled either. Applied to the particle content the series derives under its slot hypothesis, three generations with one doublet give the standard values and two doublets give slightly different ones; with three generations the strong and weak forces weaken at high energy for any number of doublets up to nineteen. The gluons and the weak bosons are not yet built as quantum states here.

Units $\hbar = c = 1$; the Euclidean section of the flat field, as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants} (the Feynman distributions follow by the standard Wick rotation), under the imported extension theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products}(ii)). Vectors are those of $\Cl(4,0)$ with orthonormal basis $\gamma_{1},\dots,\gamma_{4}$; $\nabla = \sum_{a}\gamma_{a}\partial_{a}$. For the Dirac field of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation} of mass $m \ge 0$ let $S$ be its Euclidean propagator, the vector-plus-scalar valued kernel with $(\nabla + m)S = \delta = S(\overleftarrow{\nabla} + m)$ that tends to zero at infinity; for $m = 0$, $S(w) = w/(2\pi^{2}Q(w)^{2})$. The photon propagator in the covariant gauge with parameter $\xi$ ($\xi = 1$ Feynman, $\xi = 0$ Landau) is the bilinear form $D_{w}(a,b) = \frac{1}{4\pi^{2}Q(w)}\big(\tfrac{1+\xi}{2}\,a\cdot b + (1-\xi)\frac{(a\cdot w)(b\cdot w)}{Q(w)}\big)$. The use of this covariant photon propagator inside a loop is under the Krein-form premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, as for the self-energy and vertex parts of clause (iii) of the cited theorem; the identities below are identities of the kernels and need no premise. With the vertex and coupling $e$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.coupled-system-tree-level}, the one-loop kernels are, with $x$, $y$ the ends of the electron line, $z$ the photon vertex, $u = x - z$, $v = z - y$, $w = u + v$ and $n$ the vector at the photon vertex,
\[
\Sigma(w) = e^{2}\sum_{a,b}\gamma_{a}S(w)\gamma_{b}\,D_{w}(\gamma_{a},\gamma_{b}), \qquad \Lambda(n;u,v) = e^{2}\sum_{a,b}\gamma_{a}S(u)\,n\,S(v)\gamma_{b}\,D_{u+v}(\gamma_{a},\gamma_{b}),
\]
defined for $w \neq 0$ and for $(u,v) \neq (0,0)$ (overall signs and units are conventions and are not fixed here). Write $\operatorname{div}\Lambda = \sum_{a}(\partial_{v_{a}} - \partial_{u_{a}})\Lambda(\gamma_{a};u,v)$, the divergence in $z$. For a length $\ell > 0$ define, on test functions $g$ on $\R^{4}$ and $f$ on $\R^{8}$,
\[
\langle\bar\Sigma^{\ell},g\rangle = \int\Sigma(w)\big(g(w) - \theta(\ell^{2} - Q(w))(g(0) + w\cdot\nabla g(0))\big)d^{4}w, \qquad \langle\bar\Lambda^{\ell}(n),f\rangle = \int\Lambda(n;u,v)\big(f(u,v) - \theta(\ell^{2} - Q(u+v))f(0,0)\big)d^{4}u\,d^{4}v,
\]
$\theta$ the unit step. The method and all values are standard; the statement records them in the series' algebra.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Kernels and degrees; computed.)} $\sum_{a,b}\gamma_{a}w\gamma_{b}D_{w}(\gamma_{a},\gamma_{b}) = -2\xi w/(4\pi^{2}Q(w))$ and $\sum_{a,b}\gamma_{a}\gamma_{b}D_{w}(\gamma_{a},\gamma_{b}) = (3+\xi)/(4\pi^{2}Q(w))$, so $\Sigma(w) = -\frac{\xi e^{2}}{4\pi^{4}}\frac{w}{Q(w)^{3}} + \frac{(3+\xi)e^{2}m}{16\pi^{4}}\frac{1}{Q(w)^{2}} + (\text{scaling degree at most } 3)$: scaling degree $5$ in $\R^{4}$, degree of divergence $1$, as stored. $\Lambda$ is locally integrable on $\R^{8}\setminus\{0\}$ (its factors have scaling degrees $3$, $3$, $2$ on the partial diagonals) and has scaling degree $8$ at the origin, degree of divergence $0$, as stored. For $m = 0$ in the Landau gauge $\Sigma$ vanishes identically off the origin.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Off the coincident point; proved.)} On $\R^{8}\setminus\{0\}$, $\operatorname{div}\Lambda = \delta(v)\Sigma(u) - \delta(u)\Sigma(v)$. For $w \neq 0$ the integral of $\Lambda$ over the photon vertex converges absolutely and
\[
\int\Lambda\big(n;\tfrac{w}{2}+t,\tfrac{w}{2}-t\big)\,d^{4}t = (n\cdot w)\,\Sigma(w),
\]
which follows from $\int S(x-z)\,n\,S(z-y)\,d^{4}z = (n\cdot(x-y))\,S(x-y)$. Both hold for every $m \ge 0$ (for $m > 0$ given the standard properties of the massive Euclidean propagator: fundamental solution on both sides, exponential decay, local integrability, the stored expansion; not derived in the store) and for any photon kernel that depends on $w$ alone.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The Ward identity on the extended kernels; proved.)} $\bar\Sigma^{\ell}$ and $\bar\Lambda^{\ell}$ are extensions of $\Sigma$ and $\Lambda$ with the same scaling degrees, covariant under rotations and reflections of $\Cl(4,0)$, and for every $\ell > 0$, every $\xi$ and every $m \ge 0$ (for $m > 0$ given the standard properties of the massive Euclidean propagator: fundamental solution on both sides, exponential decay, local integrability, the stored expansion; not derived in the store)
\[
\operatorname{div}\bar\Lambda^{\ell} = \delta(v)\,\bar\Sigma^{\ell}(u) - \delta(u)\,\bar\Sigma^{\ell}(v) \qquad\text{on } \R^{8}.
\]
The identity is built in by the choice of the two subtraction regions, the cylinder $Q(u+v) < \ell^{2}$ for the vertex and the ball $Q(w) < \ell^{2}$ of the same length for the self-energy; in terms of the stored constants this choice is $c_{V} = -c_{2}$. The cylinder has no counterpart in signature $(1,3)$, and the statement is one on the Euclidean section only.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Different lengths, $m = 0$; computed.)} With $\mu = 1/\ell$, $\mu\,\partial_{\mu}\bar\Sigma^{\ell} = \frac{\xi e^{2}}{8\pi^{2}}\nabla\delta$ and $\mu\,\partial_{\mu}\bar\Lambda^{\ell}(n) = -\frac{\xi e^{2}}{8\pi^{2}}\,n\,\delta(u)\delta(v)$: the coefficient $\xi e^{2}/(16\pi^{2})$ of $\ln\mu^{2}$ in the self-energy is the textbook one, and the two derivatives are opposite, the stored relation $c_{V} = -c_{2}$. With the vertex cut at length $\ell_{V}$ and the self-energy at $\ell_{\Sigma}$ the identity of (iii) fails by the local term $\frac{\xi e^{2}}{8\pi^{2}}\ln(\ell_{V}/\ell_{\Sigma})\sum_{a}(\partial_{v_{a}} - \partial_{u_{a}})\gamma_{a}\delta(u)\delta(v)$, zero only for $\ell_{V} = \ell_{\Sigma}$ unless $\xi = 0$. For $m > 0$ the mass term of $\bar\Sigma^{\ell}$ has $\mu\,\partial_{\mu}$ equal to $\frac{(3+\xi)e^{2}m}{8\pi^{2}}\delta$ at leading order in $m\ell$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(In the logarithmic form of the stored result, $m = 0$; computed.)} With $s = Q(w)$: the cut-off extension of $1/s^{2}$ with the value subtracted on the ball of radius $\ell$ is $-\frac14\nabla^{2}(\ln(M^{2}s)/s)$ with $\ln(M^{2}\ell^{2}) = 1$; that of $w/s^{3}$ with the first-order Taylor polynomial subtracted is $\frac{1}{16}\nabla\nabla^{2}(\ln(M^{2}s)/s)$ with $\ln(M^{2}\ell^{2}) = \frac32$. So $\bar\Sigma^{\ell} = -\frac{\xi e^{2}}{64\pi^{4}}\nabla\nabla^{2}(\ln(M_{\Sigma}^{2}s)/s)$, and the zero-transfer vertex $\int\bar\Lambda^{\ell}(n)\,d^{4}t$ is $-\frac{\xi e^{2}}{4\pi^{4}}$ times the sum of the homogeneous distribution $\frac18\big((n\cdot\nabla)\nabla - \frac14 n\nabla^{2}\big)(1/s)$, which carries no scale, and $-\frac{1}{16}n\,\nabla^{2}(\ln(M_{V}^{2}s)/s)$; the identity of (iii) holds exactly when
\[
\ln\big(M_{\Sigma}^{2}/M_{V}^{2}\big) = \tfrac12 ,
\]
the value $\ln(M_{\Sigma}/M_{V}) = \frac14$ of differential renormalisation (Haagensen and Latorre 1993, as quoted in eq. (36) of arXiv:hep-th/9709067, checked; Freedman, Johnson and Latorre from memory; that the scale $M_{V}$ here is theirs is not shown).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(The freedom on the Euclidean section; the stored count, carried to the Euclidean section.)} Clause (iii) of the stored theorem counts, in $\Cl(1,3)$ and in the momenta, the covariant local differences obeying the identity and the reflection: $\delta m$ and $Z_{2} = Z_{1}$ only. Carried to position-space kernels in $\Cl(4,0)$ under rotations and reflections (the covariant local terms are the same; the relation $c_{V} = -c_{2}$ is rederived in the proof), and with the pair of (iii) here, the Ward-preserving pairs of extensions of the one-loop self-energy and vertex on the Euclidean section are exactly $\bar\Sigma^{\ell} + c_{m}\delta + c_{2}\nabla\delta$, $\bar\Lambda^{\ell}(n) - c_{2}\,n\,\delta(u)\delta(v)$ with two real constants $c_{m}$, $c_{2}$ (a change of $\ell$ being a change of $c_{2}$ at $m = 0$). On the Euclidean section, for these two kernels at one loop, a pair obeying the identity is exhibited; for the time-ordered products in signature $(1,3)$ the existence remains the imported one (Scharf) unless the Wick rotation of the vertex kernel is supplied, which the store does not hold, and at higher orders and for the four-photon and three-current kernels it remains imported in any case. This result does not discharge that import; it supports it at one loop on the Euclidean section. As there, the kernels contain the covariant photon propagator and are read under the Krein-form premise.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.one-loop-self-energy-and-verte.technical: The stored regulator-free result extends the one-loop vacuum polarisation explicitly and, for the electron self-energy and the vertex, counts how two Ward-preserving extensions can differ while importing that one exists. Here one is written down on the Euclidean section; the import, which concerns the time-ordered products in signature $(1,3)$, is supported by it and not discharged, since the cylinder used has no counterpart there and no Wick rotation of the vertex kernel is stored. On the Euclidean section the self-energy kernel is the product of the electron and photon propagators, $-\xi e^{2}w/(4\pi^{4}Q(w)^{3})$ plus a mass term with coefficient $3 + \xi$, with $\xi$ the gauge parameter; the vertex kernel is a product of two electron propagators and the photon propagator of the line joining the electron's ends. Away from the point where all three positions coincide, the divergence of the vertex in the position of the photon vertex is the difference of two self-energies (the Ward-Takahashi identity), and the integral of the vertex over that position is the self-energy times the separation of the ends (its zero-transfer form); both follow from the propagator being a fundamental solution, for any mass and any gauge parameter. Extend the self-energy by subtracting the test function's first-order Taylor polynomial inside a ball of radius $\ell$, and the vertex by subtracting the test function's value at the origin whenever the electron's ends are closer than $\ell$, wherever the photon vertex is. Then the Ward-Takahashi identity holds for the extended kernels exactly, as an identity of absolutely convergent integrals: it is built in by the choice of the two subtraction regions (cylinder and ball of one length), which in terms of the stored constants is the choice $c_{V} = -c_{2}$. If the two lengths differ, it fails by a local term proportional to $\xi\ln(\ell_{V}/\ell_{\Sigma})$. Rewritten in the logarithmic form used by the stored result, the two cut-off extensions carry scales with $\ln(M^{2}\ell^{2}) = 3/2$ and $1$, so the identity ties the scales by $\ln(M_{\Sigma}^{2}/M_{V}^{2}) = 1/2$, the known relation of differential renormalisation. With the stored count carried to the Euclidean section this gives all Ward-preserving pairs there at one loop: the pair above plus the two constants $\delta m$ and $Z_{2} = Z_{1}$. For $m > 0$ the argument uses standard properties of the massive Euclidean propagator that are not derived in the store. All of it is textbook physics under the imported extension theorem and, for the photon line, the Krein-form premise; no infrared regulator enters, and the on-shell conditions and the form factor $F_{2}(0)$ are not treated.
synthesis.one-loop-self-energy-and-verte.lay: A charged particle's own field feeds back on it, and the calculation of this effect is singular where the points involved coincide. The series already treated one such quantity, the screening of charge, by a method that needs no artificial regulator, and for two others, the electron's self-interaction and its coupling to light, it relied on the literature for the statement that the method can be made to respect charge conservation. Under the same standard theorem on extending singular quantities, and assuming the series' premise on how the photon's states are measured, this result carries out those two cases at the lowest order, in the Euclidean (imaginary-time) form of the theory: if the two quantities are cut off in two matched regions of one common length, charge conservation holds exactly, because that choice of regions builds it in, and what remains free is two constants, the electron's mass and the normalisation of its field, as the series had counted. For a massive electron the argument uses standard properties of its propagator that are not checked here, and the electron's magnetic moment and the normalisation of the field on the mass shell are not treated. The numbers obtained are the known ones. This is a recovery of standard physics in the series' algebra, at the lowest order and in the Euclidean form only; the statement in real time, and higher orders, still rely on the literature.

Euclidean section only: the imported existence for the time-ordered products in signature (1,3) is supported, not discharged; no Wick rotation of the vertex kernel is stored
the identification of the vertex scale of clause (v) with the scale of the differential-renormalisation literature is not shown

the massive propagator is used through its standard properties (fundamental solution, exponential decay, local integrability, scaling degree 3), which are not checked; the checks are on the massless kernels and the order-m coefficient

synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-e.technical:
The stored one-loop electrodynamics uses Pauli-Villars fields, some of negative weight, so its regulator rests on the same indefinite form as the covariant gauge; the floors of the tower keep the Ward identity but no boost, which excludes them as a covariant regulator, not as a cut-off whose limit is shown to be covariant. A standard alternative (Epstein and Glaser; in this computational form, Freedman, Johnson and Latorre) needs no regulator: the one-loop kernels are well defined away from coincident points, and extending them across is the only step that needs a choice, governed by the scaling degree, the calculus of the stored Hadamard scaling results. Carried out in the spacetime algebra on the Euclidean section, the vacuum polarisation away from the origin, including the order-$m^{2}$ term from the Klein-Gordon recursion, is $(e^{2}/(12\pi^{4}))T(s^{-2})$ minus $(e^{2}m^{2}/(8\pi^{4}))T(s^{-1})$ plus a part of low scaling degree, $T$ the transverse operator $a \mapsto (a\cdot

abla^{2}$. Writing $s^{-2}$ as a Laplacian of the locally integrable $\ln(\mu^{2}s)/s$ gives an extension that is transverse and covariant by construction; its dependence on the scale $\mu$ is a multiple of $T(\delta)$, whose coefficient $e^{2}/(6\pi^{2})$ is twice the magnitude $e^{2}/(12\pi^{2})$ of the stored log coefficient. No regulator field and no photon line, so no Krein form, enters. For the other one-loop kernels the result is narrower: exact rank computations in $\Cl(1,3)$ show how covariant extensions obeying the Ward identities and the reflection can differ (exactly by $Z_{3}$, $\delta m$ and $Z_{2} = Z_{1}$, not at all for the three- and four-photon kernels, and at most one vector-conserving three-current extension, so one axial divergence), while their existence is the imported part (Scharf's Ward-preserving time-ordered products; for the self-energy and vertex at one loop a pair is exhibited on the Euclidean section in a later stored result, which supports the import without discharging it); the self-energy and vertex kernels carry the covariant photon propagator and so hold under the Krein-form premise. On a gravitational field the Hadamard scaling theorem gives every Dirac two-point function the flat scaling degree, so the same counting carries over with terms in the field strength added (argued); for the vacuum polarisation on a torsion-free field later stored results show that, given the imported local covariance, two transverse local covariant extensions differ by $Z_{3}$ alone, the existence of a transverse one being not proved. A separate statement is recorded with it: the scalar bubble gives the standard quartic coefficient $3/(16\pi^{2})$. The statement that no smooth weighting of the floors keeps a boost, once a clause here, is now clause (v) of the floor-regulator result.
synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-e.lay: Calculations with quantum loops produce infinities that are usually tamed by a regulator, an artificial modification at very high energies removed at the end. The series had used borrowed regulators, one of which needs fictitious particles with negative probabilities, and its own natural cut-off, the floors of its tower, singles out one observer and so breaks relativity. A known method, extending the loop quantities across the points where they are singular, is here carried out in the series' algebra. For the screening of electric charge by the vacuum it needs no regulator and no fictitious particles, stays relativistic, keeps charge conservation, and gives the standard strength of screening. For the other one-loop quantities the calculation shows that the only freedom left by relativity and charge conservation is the three constants physicists already adjust (the electron's mass, the normalisation of its field and the strength of the charge); that a version keeping charge conservation exists there is taken from the literature (a later result of the collection exhibits one at the first order of approximation in the imaginary-time form of the theory, which supports the literature's statement and does not replace it), and for the electron's own corrections the photon's states are assumed to carry the standard indefinite measure of the series' premise. The whole calculation assumes the standard theorem on extending such quantities, also taken from the literature. A related statement, that no smoothing of the tower's floors can restore relativity, is recorded with the result on the floors.
