synthesis.quartet-homotopy-makes-gluon-a.formal:
Units and signature of the store. A one-particle space is a real space $V$ with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ grading (bosonic polarisation and Goldstone modes even, ghosts odd), an orthonormal basis for a positive form and a fundamental symmetry $J$ (a signed permutation of that basis), with Krein form $\langle x, y\rangle_K = \langle x, Jy\rangle$. Its Fock space $S(V)$ is the graded-symmetric algebra (bosons: the palatial polynomials of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra}, with the positive form $\langle z^n, z^m\rangle = n!\,\delta_{nm}$ of the setting of \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}; ghosts: the tower floors of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), with Krein form $\langle x, \Gamma(J)y\rangle$; $d\Gamma(X)$ is the graded derivation extending a one-particle operator $X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The homotopy lemma; proved.)} Let $Q_1$ be odd with $Q_1^2 = 0$ and Krein-self-adjoint, $V = V_{\mathrm{ph}} \oplus V_{q}$ a Krein-orthogonal sum with $Q_1V_{\mathrm{ph}} = 0$, and $R_1$ odd with $Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1 = P_{q}$, the projection onto $V_{q}$ along $V_{\mathrm{ph}}$. Then $Q_{B} = d\Gamma(Q_1)$ is nilpotent and Krein-self-adjoint, $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = N_{q}$ for $R = d\Gamma(R_1)$ and $N_{q} = d\Gamma(P_{q})$ the number of quanta in $V_{q}$, $\ker Q_{B} = S(V_{\mathrm{ph}}) \oplus \operatorname{im}Q_{B}$, and the cohomology of $Q_{B}$ is $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$, in every number of quanta and at ghost number zero only. If $V_{\mathrm{ph}}$ is Krein-positive, the Krein form on $\ker Q_{B}$ is positive semi-definite with radical $\operatorname{im}Q_{B}$, and positive definite on the cohomology.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Gluons; proved.)} For each colour and each null momentum $k$, with polarisation modes carrying the Gupta-Bleuler form $-u\cdot w$ and a ghost pair with $\langle c, \bar c\rangle_K = 1$, the free charge of \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}, $Q_1u = -(k\cdot u)c$, $Q_1\bar c = k$, has the homotopy $R_1k = \bar c$, $R_1c = -\bar k$, zero on $\bar k$ and on the transverse plane, where $\bar k$ is null with $k\cdot\bar k = 1$; $V_{q} = \mathrm{span}\{k, \bar k, c, \bar c\}$ and $V_{\mathrm{ph}} = \{k, \bar k\}^{\perp}$, which is Krein-positive. So by (i) the physical space at every number of quanta, for any number of colours and any finite set of null momenta, is the Fock space of the transverse polarisations, positive.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Massive vectors in the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge; proved.)} For a vector of momentum $p$, with the Goldstone and ghost modes at the same momentum (the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge), with $Q(p) > 0$ and a Goldstone mode $\phi$ of Krein norm $1$, Krein self-adjointness fixes $Q_1u = -(p\cdot u)c$, $Q_1\phi = \beta c$, $Q_1\bar c = p + \beta\phi$, and $Q_1^2 = 0$ exactly when $\beta^2 = Q(p)$. Then $V_{q} = \mathrm{span}\{p, \phi, c, \bar c\}$ has a homotopy, and $V_{\mathrm{ph}} = p^{\perp}$, three-dimensional and Krein-positive: the physical space is the Fock space of three polarisations.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exact checks; computed.)} For $k = 5\gamma_0 + 3\gamma_1 + 4\gamma_2$, $\bar k = \tfrac{1}{50}(5\gamma_0 - 3\gamma_1 - 4\gamma_2)$, and $p = 5\gamma_0 + 4\gamma_1$, $\beta = 3$: the one-particle statements (with $\beta = 2$ not nilpotent; physical Krein Gram $25, 1$ and $9, 1, 1$); $Q_{B}^2 = 0$, Krein self-adjointness and $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = N_{q}$ on every sector with at most four quanta (gluon) and three quanta (massive); ghost-number-zero cohomology of dimensions $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ (gluon), $1, 3, 6, 10$ (massive) and $1, 4, 10, 20$ (two colours), with Krein signature $(\dim H, 0, \operatorname{rank})$ on $\ker Q_{B}$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The gauge algebra broken by two doublets; computed, given the vacuum as input.)} Take the twelve generators of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} acting on the two hypercharge-$\tfrac12$ doublets of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum} (eight real scalars), with a neutral aligned vacuum $(0, v_1)$, $(0, v_2)$ as input (the breaking pattern is not derived here). The Goldstone map $T_a \mapsto (T_a\phi_1, T_a\phi_2)$ has rank $3$, so nine vectors stay massless (its kernel: colour and one $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ mixing $T_3$ and hypercharge) and three are massive. The one-particle direct sum of the corresponding spaces of (ii) and (iii) is Krein-self-adjoint with a homotopy, has $27$ physical polarisations per momentum with Krein signature $(27, 0, 0)$, and $8 - 3 = 5$ scalars remain physical.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Under clauses (K1) and (K2) of the Krein-form premise (KF, \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}; the one-particle form of (K1) is restated in the store as the trace form of Clifford conjugation, \claimref{synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-twistor-adjoint-and-its-trace-form-is-the-one-particle-gupta-bleuler-form}, which does not derive the premise), that the polarisation states carry the Gupta-Bleuler form $-u\cdot w$ and the ghost pair the pairing $\langle c, \bar c\rangle_K = 1$, the free (asymptotic) gluons and the massive vectors (Feynman-'t Hooft gauge) have a positive physical space at every number of quanta, which the stored result had only up to three quanta; this is the quartet mechanism of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(ii), proved here in its free form by an explicit homotopy. The interacting statement is not proved: it needs Kugo and Ojima's hypotheses on the asymptotic fields, and the whole construction is perturbative, since beyond perturbation theory the covariant gauge condition has Gribov copies (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv); computed copies on the weak rotor lattice in \claimref{synthesis.non-abelian-gauge-fixing-has-gribov-copies-and-the-weak-rotor-lattice-with-doublets-has-a-perimeter-law}). The polarisation form used is the momentum-independent Gupta-Bleuler form $-u\cdot w$ (Feynman gauge); forms with a part along $k$ are not treated. All operators are real, so the unit $I_4$ commutes with them. Transport-absent.
synthesis.quartet-homotopy-makes-gluon-a.technical:
The stored covariant gauge fixing of the series' gauge fields showed, under the Krein-form premise, that the free BRST charge at one null momentum has a positive physical space, computed exactly up to three quanta. Positivity at every number of quanta is the content of the Kugo-Ojima quartet mechanism, and its free form has a short proof that the computation can follow exactly. On the one-particle space the unphysical modes (the polarisation along $k$, its partner $\bar k$, the ghost and the antighost) form a quartet, and there is an odd operator $R_1$ with $Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1$ equal to the projection onto the quartet. Second quantisation turns graded commutators of one-particle operators into graded commutators of their Fock-space lifts, so the lifted $R$ satisfies $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = N_{q}$, the number of quartet quanta. Every closed state with at least one quartet quantum is then exact, $x = Q_{B}(Rx)/n$, so the cohomology is the Fock space of the transverse polarisations, in every number of quanta. The Krein form is positive there because the transverse polarisations have positive Gupta-Bleuler norm and are Krein-orthogonal to the quartet.

The same structure covers the massive vectors of the broken weak factor in the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge, where the Goldstone and ghost modes share the vector's momentum: with a Goldstone mode of positive norm, self-adjointness fixes the charge and nilpotency forces the Goldstone coefficient to satisfy $\beta^2 = Q(p)$, the Feynman-'t Hooft shell; the quartet is the polarisation along $p$, the Goldstone mode and the ghost pair, and the physical modes are the three polarisations orthogonal to $p$. For the gauge algebra broken by the stored two doublets, with a neutral aligned vacuum taken as input, the rank of the Goldstone map is computed to be three: nine massless vectors with two polarisations and three massive ones with three, $27$ in all and all Krein-positive, and five physical scalars. The checks confirm each step exactly for rational momenta, including the Fock-space identity $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = N_{q}$ sector by sector and the cohomology dimensions, and that the computation reproduces the stored dimensions $1, 2, 3, 4$ and continues them.

What is not proved is the interacting statement. Kugo and Ojima derive it from hypotheses on the asymptotic fields: asymptotic completeness, the asymptotic charge being the linear one, and, for unbroken colour, a condition excluding massless coloured asymptotic states. None of these follows from the series' structures, and the Krein form itself remains a premise.
synthesis.quartet-homotopy-makes-gluon-a.lay: In the standard quantum theory of the strong and weak forces, the force fields carry unphysical parts, which come with negative probabilities, and ghost particles that cancel them. The cancellation works because the unphysical modes come in groups of four whose contributions vanish. Earlier work on the series checked this for states with up to three particles. This result proves it for any number of particles, for the gluons of the strong force and for the heavy W and Z of the weak force in one standard choice of gauge, by an explicit operator that counts the unphysical particles: any allowed state containing them is equivalent to zero, so the surviving states are made only of the physical polarisations, and they have positive probabilities. It holds for free particles and assumes two parts of the negative-norm bookkeeping the series has adopted as a premise; it is a statement of perturbation theory; the fully interacting case still rests on the standard assumptions of the literature.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} $S(V)$ is spanned by the monomials $e_{j_1}\cdots e_{j_T}$ in a basis of $V$, ordered, with odd basis elements anticommuting and squaring to zero and even ones commuting; on the even modes it is the palatial polynomial representation (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra}) with the positive form $\langle z^n, z^m\rangle = n!\,\delta_{nm}$ stated in the setting of \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}, on the odd modes the exterior algebra of a tower floor (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) with its orthonormal monomials. For a one-particle operator $X$ of parity $|X|$, $d\Gamma(X)$ is the graded derivation of $S(V)$ equal to $X$ on $V$: on a monomial it replaces one factor $e_{j}$ by $Xe_{j}$, with the sign $(-1)^{|X|m}$ for the $m$ odd factors passed. $\Gamma(J)$ is the algebra automorphism equal to $J$ on $V$, and the Fock Krein form is $\langle x, \Gamma(J)y\rangle$, the graded-symmetric extension of $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_K$.

\emph{(i).} The graded commutator $[D_1, D_2] = D_1D_2 - (-1)^{|D_1||D_2|}D_2D_1$ of two graded derivations is a graded derivation, and a graded derivation of $S(V)$ is fixed by its restriction to the generators $V$. On $V$, $[d\Gamma(X), d\Gamma(Y)]$ and $d\Gamma([X, Y])$ agree, so $d\Gamma$ is a homomorphism of Lie superalgebras. Hence $2Q_{B}^2 = [Q_{B}, Q_{B}] = d\Gamma([Q_1, Q_1]) = 2d\Gamma(Q_1^2) = 0$, and $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = d\Gamma(Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1) = d\Gamma(P_{q}) = N_{q}$. Since $V = V_{\mathrm{ph}} \oplus V_{q}$, $S(V) = S(V_{\mathrm{ph}}) \otimes S(V_{q})$ and $N_{q}$ is $n$ on $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}}) \otimes S^{n}(V_{q})$. $N_{q}$ commutes with $Q_{B}$, because $[Q_{B}, Q_{B}R + RQ_{B}] = [Q_{B}^2, R] = 0$, so $Q_{B}$ preserves each eigenspace. On the eigenspace $n > 0$, $Q_{B}x = 0$ gives $x = \tfrac1n(Q_{B}R + RQ_{B})x = Q_{B}(\tfrac1nRx)$: the cohomology vanishes there. On $n = 0$, $Q_{B} = d\Gamma(Q_1)$ acts on $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$ through $Q_1V_{\mathrm{ph}} = 0$, so it is zero, and nothing in $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$ is exact because $Q_{B}$ preserves $N_{q}$. So $\ker Q_{B} = S(V_{\mathrm{ph}}) \oplus (\ker Q_{B} \cap \{N_{q} > 0\}) = S(V_{\mathrm{ph}}) \oplus \operatorname{im}Q_{B}$ and the cohomology is $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$; $V_{\mathrm{ph}}$ carries no ghosts, so it sits at ghost number zero. Krein self-adjointness: $\Gamma(J)$ and the positive form are multiplicative over the monomials, and the Fock adjoint of a one-particle lift is the lift of the one-particle adjoint, so $Q_{B}$ is self-adjoint because $Q_1$ is. Then $\langle x, Q_{B}y\rangle_K = \langle Q_{B}x, y\rangle_K = 0$ for $x \in \ker Q_{B}$: $\operatorname{im}Q_{B}$ is orthogonal to $\ker Q_{B}$ and lies in it, hence is null. The Krein orthogonality of $V_{\mathrm{ph}}$ and $V_{q}$ makes $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$ orthogonal to every monomial containing a quartet factor. On $S(V_{\mathrm{ph}})$, with a Krein-orthonormal basis of the positive space $V_{\mathrm{ph}}$, the monomials are orthogonal with norms $\prod n_j! > 0$. So the form on $\ker Q_{B}$ is positive semi-definite with radical $\operatorname{im}Q_{B}$, and positive definite on the cohomology.

\emph{(ii).} With the form $-u\cdot w$ on the polarisation modes (K1) and $\langle c, \bar c\rangle_K = 1$ (K2), self-adjointness of $Q_1$ is $\langle Q_1u, \bar c\rangle_K = -(k\cdot u) = \langle u, k\rangle_K = \langle u, Q_1\bar c\rangle_K$; nilpotency is $Q_1^2\bar c = Q_1k = -Q(k)c = 0$. This is the one-particle form of the charge $L^{\dagger}b + d^{*}L$ of \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}(ii), $c$ and $\bar c$ the one-particle states of its two ghost modes. With $\bar k$ null, $k\cdot\bar k = 1$, and $t$ in the transverse plane $\{k, \bar k\}^{\perp}$: $Q_1\bar k = -c$, $Q_1k = Q_1t = Q_1c = 0$, $Q_1\bar c = k$. For $R_1$ as stated, $(Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1)$ sends $k \mapsto Q_1\bar c = k$, $\bar k \mapsto R_1(-c) = \bar k$, $c \mapsto Q_1(-\bar k) = c$, $\bar c \mapsto R_1k = \bar c$ and $t \mapsto 0$: it is $P_{q}$. The transverse plane is spacelike, so $-t\cdot t > 0$, and it is Krein-orthogonal to $k$, $\bar k$ (by definition) and to the ghosts. (i) applies; for several colours and momenta, take direct sums of one-particle spaces, charges and homotopies.

\emph{(iii).} Krein self-adjointness with $\langle\phi, \phi\rangle_K = 1$ gives $\langle Q_1u, \bar c\rangle_K = -(p\cdot u) = \langle u, Q_1\bar c\rangle_K$ and $\langle Q_1\phi, \bar c\rangle_K = \beta = \langle\phi, Q_1\bar c\rangle_K$, so $Q_1\bar c = p + \beta\phi$, and $Q_1^2\bar c = (-Q(p) + \beta^2)c$: nilpotency holds exactly when $\beta^2 = Q(p)$. Then $Q_1(p + \beta\phi) = 0$ and $Q_1\phi = \beta c$. Take $R_1c = \beta^{-1}\phi$, $R_1p = \bar c$, and $R_1$ zero on $\phi$, $\bar c$ and $p^{\perp}$. Then $Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1$ sends $c \mapsto Q_1\beta^{-1}\phi = c$, $\phi \mapsto R_1(\beta c) = \phi$, $p + \beta\phi \mapsto Q_1\bar c = p + \beta\phi$, $\bar c \mapsto R_1(p + \beta\phi) = \bar c$ and $p^{\perp}$ to $0$: it is $P_{q}$ (the check solves the linear system for an odd $R_1$ independently). The complement $p^{\perp}$ is spacelike, Krein-positive and Krein-orthogonal to $p$, $\phi$ and the ghosts, and $Q_1p^{\perp} = 0$; (i) applies. In the field theory the Goldstone shift $s\phi = mc$ and $sA = \nabla c$ give this charge in the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge, where the unphysical modes share the vector's shell $Q(p) = m^2$; in other covariant gauges the quartet lies on its own shell, with the same algebra (argued, not computed).

\emph{(iv).} The check builds the one-particle matrices, verifies nilpotency and $KQ_1 = Q_1^{\mathsf T}K$ for the Krein Gram $K$, solves the linear system for an odd $R_1$ with $Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1 = P_{q}$ ($P_{q}$ computed from the adapted basis), and verifies the Krein orthogonality and Gram of the physical span. On $S(V)$ it applies $d\Gamma$ monomial by monomial on every sector of fixed total number $T$ (sizes $1, 6, 19, 44, 85$ for the gluon and $1, 7, 26, 70$ for the massive vector) and confirms $Q_{B}^2 = 0$, $\langle u, Q_{B}w\rangle_K = \langle Q_{B}u, w\rangle_K$ and $Q_{B}R + RQ_{B} = d\Gamma(P_{q})$ on each basis monomial. It computes the ranks of $Q_{B}$ from ghost number $-1$ to $0$ and from $0$ to $1$, the cohomology dimensions ($\binom{T+1}{1}$, $\binom{T+2}{2}$ and $\binom{T+3}{3}$, the symmetric powers of spaces of dimension $2$, $3$ and $4$) and the Krein signature on $\ker Q_{B}$, $(\dim H, 0, \dim\operatorname{im}Q_{B})$. For the gluon the dimensions $1, 2, 3, 4$ at $T \le 3$ are those of the stored result.

\emph{(v).} The gauge algebra has twelve generators (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}). On a hypercharge-$\tfrac12$ doublet of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum} they act as an anti-Hermitian basis of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, as zero for colour, and as $\tfrac{1}{2}I_{4}$ for the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ (the unit of this parenthetical $2 \times 2$ reading is the doublet's complex structure, the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$). The vacuum is input: both doublets neutral and aligned, $(0, 3)$ and $(0, 4)$ in the check (any nonzero values give the same ranks). The check computes the real $8 \times 12$ Goldstone map $a \mapsto (T_a\phi_1, T_a\phi_2)$: rank $3$, kernel of dimension $9$, of which one vector lies in the electroweak block with nonzero components along both the diagonal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generator and hypercharge (the unbroken $\mathfrak{u}(1)$). The vector mass matrix is the Gram matrix of this map, so three vectors are massive and nine massless, and the three image directions are the Goldstone modes eaten, leaving $8 - 3 = 5$ physical scalars. It then forms the direct sum of nine gluon-type and three massive one-particle spaces ($75$ modes) and confirms, block by block, Krein self-adjointness, $Q_1^2 = 0$ and $Q_1R_1 + R_1Q_1 = P_{q}$; $P_{q}$ has rank $48$, and the Krein Gram matrix of the $27$ physical basis vectors has signature $(27, 0, 0)$. Giving the timelike polarisation the positive form instead breaks the self-adjointness and fails the check.

\emph{What is standard and what is not.} The quartet mechanism and the homotopy argument are standard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(ii)); new are the exact checks on the store's representations and the extension of the stored three-quanta computation to every number of quanta, for gluons and massive vectors. Clauses (K1) and (K2) of the Krein-form premise (KF, \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}) are hypotheses here: that the polarisation state space carries the Gupta-Bleuler form and the ghost pair the pairing $\langle c, \bar c\rangle_K = 1$; neither is derived. The breaking pattern of (v) takes the vacuum as input. The construction is perturbative: beyond perturbation theory gauge fixing has Gribov copies (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv); computed lattice copies in \claimref{synthesis.non-abelian-gauge-fixing-has-gribov-copies-and-the-weak-rotor-lattice-with-doublets-has-a-perimeter-law}). The interacting statement, on the asymptotic fields of the interacting theory, needs Kugo and Ojima's hypotheses and is not proved here.

synthesis.radical-normal-tame-wall-is-a-.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) and $g$ its derived metric, with inverse $G$ (the cometric). Let $\Sigma = \{t = 0\}$ in coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with physical side $t > 0$, and for exponents $(a, b)$ let $G_{a,b} = \mathrm{diag}(-t^{a}, t^{b}, 1, 1)$, with $g_{a,b} = \mathrm{diag}(-t^{-a}, t^{-b}, 1, 1)$ on $t \neq 0$; these components, and the line elements below, are written in the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ (dictionary C7), while the spacetime algebra of (ii) has $\gamma_{0}^{2} = +1$; the scalar curvature $R$ quoted below has the same value in the store's sign in $(+,-,-,-)$, and the Ricci square does not depend on the sign. The degeneration at $\Sigma$ is tame (Definition \claimref{sheaf.tameness}) exactly for $(a, b) = (1, 0)$, with radical $dt$, the conormal of $\Sigma$, and $(a, b) = (0, 1)$, with radical $dx$, tangent; in both the metric has the simple pole of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Radical the conormal: a regular initial surface; proved.)} For $(1, 0)$, with $\tau = 2\sqrt{t}$, $g_{1,0} = -d\tau^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2}$: the physical side is the half $\tau > 0$ of Minkowski space, flat, at proper time $2\sqrt{t}$ from $\Sigma$, and its slices $\tau = \varepsilon > 0$ are Cauchy surfaces; the far side is Riemannian. So the propagation of the Hadamard form (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadamard-form}, scalar field) carries a two-point function of Hadamard form near one slice $\tau = \varepsilon$ to the whole physical side.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Smoothness at the wall selects no bulk state; proved.)} $\partial_{\tau}^{2} = t\,\partial_{t}^{2} + \tfrac12\partial_{t}$, with indicial exponents $0$ and $\tfrac12$. A Klein-Gordon solution of any mass on the physical side is smooth in $t$ up to $\Sigma$ exactly when it is even in $\tau$, that is when $\partial_{\tau}\phi = 0$ on $\Sigma$; these solutions form a Lagrangian subspace for the symplectic form, so the fields they smear commute. In the constant frame of the chart $(\tau, x, y, z)$ (zero spin connection), a Dirac plane wave (Hestenes form, spatial wave vector $k$, mass $m$) obeys $\phi' = M\phi$ with $M^{2} = -(|k|^{2} + m^{2})$, so it is smooth in $t$ across $\Sigma$ only if it vanishes, unless $k = 0 = m$; the only Dirac solution with square-integrable data that is smooth in $t$ across $\Sigma$ in this frame is zero, for every mass. So no bulk field obeying the canonical commutation or anticommutation relations is smooth across $\Sigma$ in $t$, while in $\tau$ the surface imposes no condition: smoothness at the wall selects no bulk state. This does not concern the boundary modes the wall carries by the wall Fact, nor any selection by the Riemannian far side.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Radical tangent: a singular wall; proved.)} For $(0, 1)$, $g_{0,1} = -dt^{2} + t^{-1}dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2}$ has scalar curvature $R = \tfrac32 t^{-2}$, unbounded at $\Sigma$, at finite proper time; the far side has signature $(2, 2)$. Its slices $t = \varepsilon > 0$ are Cauchy surfaces of the physical side, and $\Sigma$ is a singular past boundary.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Power-law origins in cosmic time; proved.)} For a spatially flat expanding field $-dt^{2} + t^{2p}(dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2})$ of a perfect fluid with $P = w\rho$, $p = 2/(3(1 + w))$, in the cosmic coordinate $t$ the metric is $t^{2p}$ times a field whose cometric degenerates at $t = 0$ with radical $dt$, tamely exactly when $2p = 1$, that is $w = \tfrac13$; the radiation-dominated field is $t\,g_{1,0}$, with conformal time $\tau$, scalar curvature $0$ and Ricci square $\mathcal{R}(\partial_{a})\cdot\mathcal{R}(a) = \tfrac34 t^{-4}$ (in components $R_{ab}R^{ab}$). In its conformal time $\eta$ every such field with $p < 1$ has the bracket $-d\eta^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2}$, which is $g_{1,0}$ in $t' = \eta^{2}/4$: tameness of the bracket is a property of the time coordinate. For the conformally covariant fields (the massless Dirac, Maxwell and Yang-Mills fields) the radiation origin is the initial slice of half of Minkowski space, where the Weyl curvature vanishes. Which bulk solutions are smooth in $t$ there depends on the conformal weight: for the massless scalar ($R = 0$, so minimal and conformal coupling agree), $\phi = t^{-1/2}\phi_{\mathrm{flat}}$, they are the solutions odd in $\tau$ (indicial exponents $0$ and $-\tfrac12$), the other half from (ii); for the massless Dirac field, $\psi = t^{-3/4}\psi_{\mathrm{flat}}$, the exponents $-\tfrac34 + \tfrac{n}{2}$ are never integers and no nonzero solution is smooth in $t$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.radical-normal-tame-wall-is-a-.technical: The deposit chain needs the descent's surface to be a surface on which a state can be set and then carried forward by the standard propagation of the Hadamard form. The series' walls are tame corank-one degenerations of the inverse metric. In the two aligned normal forms the outcome depends on whether the degenerate direction is the wall's normal. If it is, the physical side, measured in its own proper time, is a flat half of Minkowski space, so slices near the wall are Cauchy surfaces and propagation works from any thin collar; but the bulk fields that are smooth across the wall in the wall's own coordinate have zero momentum there (half of the scalar phase space, on which the fields commute) and, for the Dirac field in the flat frame, vanish, so smoothness at the wall cannot carry quantum data and selects no state. Whether the wall's boundary modes or a Euclidean reading of its Riemannian far side select one is not examined. If the degenerate direction is tangent, the wall is a curvature singularity. In cosmic time a radiation-dominated expanding universe is, up to a conformal factor, exactly the normal case, and it is the only power law with this property in that coordinate; in conformal time every decelerating power law is. Under the radiation-type reading the chain's second step holds; what is missing is the state itself on the collar. Transport-absent.
synthesis.radical-normal-tame-wall-is-a-.lay: For a quantum field to be in a reasonable state everywhere, it is enough to set it up reasonably on one complete slice of time and let the equations carry it forward. This result asks whether the moment of the descent, where the series' geometry degenerates in the mild way the series assumes, can be that slice. In the case where the degenerate direction points along time, the moment behaves like an ordinary starting slice, so the carrying forward works, but requiring the fields to be smooth there puts no usable condition on the state, so it does not choose one. In the other case the moment is a genuine singularity. In the usual cosmic time, the early radiation-filled universe turns out to be the first case in disguise.

proofs.main:
The curvature statements below are computed in Gauge Theory Gravity on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}): each metric is, up to the overall sign of dictionary C7 (the line elements are written in $(-,+,+,+)$), the derived metric of a diagonal gauge field $\hb^{-1}(e_{t}) = N(t)\,e_{0}$, $\hb^{-1}(e_{x^{i}}) = A_{i}(t)\,e_{i}$ with constant orthonormal physical frame $e_{0}, \dots, e_{3}$ and $B_{i} = e_{0}\wedge e_{i}$. For such a field the torsion equation gives $\Omega(e_{t}) = 0$, $\Omega(e_{x^{i}}) = -(\dot A_{i}/N)\,B_{i}$, so $R(e_{t}\wedge e_{x^{i}}) = -\partial_{t}(\dot A_{i}/N)\,B_{i}$, $R(e_{x^{i}}\wedge e_{x^{j}}) = -(\dot A_{i}\dot A_{j}/N^{2})\,e_{i}\wedge e_{j}$, and the store-sign operator is diagonal on the frame planes:
\[
\mathcal{R}(B_{i}) = \frac{\partial_{t}(\dot A_{i}/N)}{N A_{i}}\,B_{i}, \qquad \mathcal{R}(e_{i}\wedge e_{j}) = \frac{\dot A_{i}\dot A_{j}}{N^{2}A_{i}A_{j}}\,e_{i}\wedge e_{j}.
\]
On a plane with eigenvalue $\kappa$ the contraction $\partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)$ contributes $\kappa$ to each of its two vectors, so the Ricci map is diagonal with $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}) = \sum_{i}\kappa_{0i}\,e_{0}$, $\mathcal{R}(e_{j}) = \bigl(\kappa_{0j} + \sum_{i \neq j}\kappa_{ij}\bigr)e_{j}$, and the scalar is $\mathcal{R} = 2\sum_{\text{planes}}\kappa$. The values below are store-sign values in $(+,-,-,-)$; the scalar and the Ricci square have the same values in the check's index convention in $(-,+,+,+)$, as the statement records ($g^{\circ} \to -g^{\circ}$ leaves the Ricci tensor of the index convention unchanged and flips the inverse metric, and the store's Ricci tensor is its negative, so the scalar is the same). The check computes each field with the library's engine on exact jets, $\Omega$ solved from the torsion equation (check\_gtg\_wall\_field\_strengths).

\emph{The models are tame.} For $G_{a,b} = \mathrm{diag}(-t^{a}, t^{b}, 1, 1)$, $\det G_{a,b} = -t^{a + b}$, so the degeneration at $t = 0$ is of corank one and first order exactly when $a + b = 1$; the pairs $(2, 0)$, $(0, 2)$, $(1, 1)$ are not tame. For $(1, 0)$ the radical is spanned by $k = dt$, the conormal of $\Sigma$, with $G(k, k) = -t$ and transversality datum $\partial_{t}G(k, k) = -1 \neq 0$; for $(0, 1)$ it is spanned by $k = dx$, tangent to $\Sigma$ in the sense that $k$ is not a multiple of $dt$, with $G(k, k) = t$. Both satisfy (T1) to (T3) of Definition \claimref{sheaf.tameness}, and in both the metric has a simple pole in one direction ($g_{tt} = -t^{-1}$, respectively $g_{xx} = t^{-1}$), as Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem} and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist} require.

\emph{(i)} With $\tau = 2\sqrt{t}$, $dt = \tfrac{\tau}{2}\,d\tau$ and $t = \tfrac{\tau^{2}}{4}$, so $-t^{-1}dt^{2} = -d\tau^{2}$ and $g = -d\tau^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2}$ on $t > 0$: the half $\tau > 0$ of Minkowski space. The proper time from $\Sigma$ to the slice $t$ is $\int_{0}^{t}s^{-1/2}ds = 2\sqrt{t}$. On the half space every inextendible causal curve has $\tau$ strictly monotone, tending to $0$ in the past and to $\infty$ in the future, so it meets each slice $\tau = c > 0$ exactly once: the slices are Cauchy surfaces of the physical side. For $t < 0$ the cometric is $\mathrm{diag}(|t|, 1, 1, 1)$, positive definite. In Gauge Theory Gravity the field is $N = t^{-1/2}$, $A_{i} = 1$: each $\hb^{-1}(e_{\mu})$ depends only on its own label, so $\Omega = 0$ solves the torsion equation and the field strength vanishes: the physical side is flat in the coordinate $t$ as well (the check's coordinate engine also returns vanishing Ricci tensor). Since each $\tau = \varepsilon$ is a Cauchy surface, the propagation of the Hadamard form (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadamard-form}, scalar field) carries a two-point function of Hadamard form on a neighbourhood of $\tau = \varepsilon$ to the whole physical side.

\emph{(ii), scalar.} $\partial_{\tau} = \tfrac{dt}{d\tau}\partial_{t} = \sqrt{t}\,\partial_{t}$, hence $\partial_{\tau}^{2} = \sqrt{t}\,\partial_{t}(\sqrt{t}\,\partial_{t}) = t\,\partial_{t}^{2} + \tfrac12\partial_{t}$, whose indicial polynomial on $t^{r}$ is $r(r - 1) + \tfrac{r}{2} = r(r - \tfrac12)$, with exponents $0$ and $\tfrac12$. A solution of $(-\partial_{\tau}^{2} + \Delta - m^{2})\phi = 0$ on the physical side is the restriction of a solution on Minkowski space, smooth in $\tau$ at $\tau = 0$, and the reflection $\tau \mapsto -\tau$ maps solutions to solutions, so $\phi = \phi_{+} + \phi_{-}$ with $\phi_{\pm}$ even and odd in $\tau$. A smooth even function of $\tau$ is a smooth function of $\tau^{2} = 4t$ (Whitney's theorem on even functions, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-bochner-theorem-moment-lemma-and-whitney-even-functions}(c)), so $\phi_{+}$ is smooth in $t$ up to $\Sigma$. If $\phi_{-} \neq 0$, its Cauchy data at $\tau = 0$ are $(0, \partial_{\tau}\phi_{-})$ with $\partial_{\tau}\phi_{-} \neq 0$ (zero data give the zero solution), so $\phi_{-} = \tau\,\psi(\tau^{2})$ with $\psi(0) \neq 0$, that is $2\sqrt{t}\,\psi(4t)$, whose $t$-derivative is unbounded at $t = 0$; and $\phi_{+}$ is smooth in $t$, so $\phi$ is smooth in $t$ up to $\Sigma$ exactly when $\phi_{-} = 0$, that is when $\partial_{\tau}\phi = 0$ on $\Sigma$. In the coordinate $t$ the conjugate momentum is $\sqrt{t}\,\partial_{t}\phi$, which vanishes on $\Sigma$ for every $\phi$ smooth in $t$. On solutions with data $(f, 0)$ the symplectic form $\sigma(\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}) = \int_{\Sigma}(\phi_{1}\partial_{\tau}\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\partial_{\tau}\phi_{1})\,d^{3}x$ vanishes, and they are maximal with this property, since $\sigma((f, 0), (0, g)) = \int fg$ pairs them nondegenerately with the data $(0, g)$: a Lagrangian subspace. The field operators smeared with these solutions therefore commute, and no field obeying the canonical commutation relations on the physical side is smooth in $t$ across $\Sigma$. The check verifies the mode form exactly: for $\omega^{2} = k^{2} + m^{2}$ at three rational values, $\cos(\omega\tau)$ written as a series in $t$ satisfies $(t\,\partial_{t}^{2} + \tfrac12\partial_{t})C = -\omega^{2}C$ coefficient by coefficient (to order $t^{6}$), $\sin(\omega\tau)/\omega$ has only odd powers of $\tau$ (the exponent $\tfrac12$ branch), $\sigma(\cos, \cos) = 0$ and $\sigma(\cos, \sin/\omega) = 1$ at $\tau = 0$, and $\sqrt{t}\,\partial_{t}C$ starts at $t^{1/2}$.

\emph{(ii), Dirac.} Work in the constant frame of the chart $(\tau, x, y, z)$, in which the spin connection vanishes. In Hestenes form $\nabla\psi I\sigma_{3} = m\psi\gamma_{0}$ with $\nabla = \gamma^{0}\partial_{\tau} + \gamma^{i}\partial_{i}$. Put $\psi = \phi(\tau)\,e$, $e = \exp(-I\sigma_{3}\,k\cdot x)$, $\phi$ in the even subalgebra. Since $I\sigma_{3} = -\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$ commutes with $\gamma_{0}$ and $(I\sigma_{3})^{2} = -1$, one has $\partial_{i}e = -k_{i}\,e\,I\sigma_{3}$, and the equation becomes, after cancelling the invertible factor $e$ on the right, $\gamma_{0}\phi' I\sigma_{3} + \kappa\phi = m\phi\gamma_{0}$ with $\kappa = k_{i}\gamma^{i}$. So $\phi' = M\phi$, $M\phi = \gamma_{0}(m\phi\gamma_{0} - \kappa\phi)(I\sigma_{3})^{-1}$, a linear map of the even subalgebra (the check uses $\kappa = \sum k_{i}\gamma_{i}$; the sign of $k$ is immaterial). The check computes, exactly on the eight even blades and five samples of $(k, m)$, that $M$ preserves the even subalgebra and $M^{2} = -\omega^{2}$, $\omega^{2} = |k|^{2} + m^{2}$; by hand, write $J = I\sigma_{3}$ and $L_{a}$, $R_{b}$ for left and right multiplication, which commute, with $R_{b}R_{c} = R_{cb}$; then $M = A + B$, $A = m L_{\gamma_{0}}R_{\gamma_{0}J^{-1}}$, $B = -L_{\gamma_{0}\kappa}R_{J^{-1}}$, and since $J$ commutes with $\gamma_{0}$, $J^{2} = -1$, $\gamma_{0}\kappa = -\kappa\gamma_{0}$ and $\kappa^{2} = -|k|^{2}$: $A^{2} = m^{2}R_{(\gamma_{0}J^{-1})^{2}} = -m^{2}$, $B^{2} = L_{(\gamma_{0}\kappa)^{2}}R_{J^{-2}} = -|k|^{2}$, and $AB + BA = -m(L_{\kappa} - L_{\kappa})R_{-\gamma_{0}} = 0$, so $M^{2} = -(m^{2} + |k|^{2})$. Hence $\phi(\tau) = \cos(\omega\tau)\phi_{0} + \omega^{-1}\sin(\omega\tau)M\phi_{0}$, whose odd part vanishes exactly when $M\phi_{0} = 0$, and $M$ is invertible for $\omega \neq 0$ (the check finds rank $8$, and rank $0$ at $k = 0 = m$). By the argument of the scalar case a Dirac plane wave is smooth in $t$ across $\Sigma$ only if it is even in $\tau$, so only if $\phi_{0} = 0$, unless $k = 0 = m$. A solution with square-integrable data on the flat slice is a superposition of plane waves whose odd part is $\int \omega_{k}^{-1}\sin(\omega_{k}\tau)M_{k}\phi_{0}(k)\,d^{3}k$; it vanishes exactly when $M_{k}\phi_{0}(k) = 0$ for almost every $k$, that is when $\phi_{0} = 0$. So the only Dirac solution with square-integrable data that is smooth in $t$ across $\Sigma$ is zero, for every mass. The frame matters: a spin rotation odd in $\tau$, for example $R = \exp(-I\sigma_{3}m\tau)$ at $k = 0$, makes the rest-frame solution constant, at the price of a spin connection $\Omega(\partial_{t}) \propto t^{-1/2}$, not smooth in $t$; the statement is for the constant frame, or equivalently for gauge fields $(\hb, \Omega)$ whose spin connection vanishes there. \emph{(Argued, beyond the model.)} With a transverse metric $h(t)$ smooth in $t$, the spin-connection term along $\gamma^{0}$ is odd in $\tau$ and the transverse Dirac operator with mass, $K(\tau)$, is even, so an even solution must satisfy $K\psi = 0$ and is a static zero mode of the transverse Dirac Hamiltonian, of which there is none in $L^{2}$ when $m \neq 0$, since that Hamiltonian squares to $D_{h}^{2} + m^{2} \geq m^{2}$.

\emph{(iii)} For $(0, 1)$, $g = -dt^{2} + t^{-1}dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2}$ and the proper time to $\Sigma$ is $t$. The field is $N = t^{-a/2}$, $A_{1} = t^{-b/2}$, $A_{2} = A_{3} = 1$: only the plane $B_{1}$ carries field strength, with $\kappa = \partial_{t}(\dot A_{1}/N)/(NA_{1})$; $\dot A_{1}/N = -\tfrac{b}{2}t^{(a - b)/2 - 1}$, so $\kappa = \tfrac{b}{4}(b + 2 - a)\,t^{a - 2}$ and $\mathcal{R} = 2\kappa = \tfrac{b}{2}(b + 2 - a)\,t^{a - 2}$; for $(0, 1)$ ($N = 1$, $\kappa = \ddot A_{1}/A_{1}$, $A_{1} = t^{-1/2}$, $\ddot A_{1} = \tfrac34 t^{-5/2}$) this is $\mathcal{R} = \tfrac32 t^{-2}$. The check computes it with the engine for all five pairs, and its coordinate engine ($R^{\rho}{}_{\sigma\mu\nu} = \partial_{\mu}\Gamma^{\rho}_{\nu\sigma} - \partial_{\nu}\Gamma^{\rho}_{\mu\sigma} + \Gamma^{\rho}_{\mu\lambda}\Gamma^{\lambda}_{\nu\sigma} - \Gamma^{\rho}_{\nu\lambda}\Gamma^{\lambda}_{\mu\sigma}$, $R = 2\ddot A/A$ for $-dt^{2} + A(t)^{2}dx^{2}$ plus a flat block) agrees. For $t < 0$ the cometric $\mathrm{diag}(-1, -|t|, 1, 1)$ has two negative entries: signature $(2, 2)$. On $t > 0$, $t$ is a time function and causal curves have $|dx/dt| \le \sqrt{t}$, so each inextendible one meets every slice $t = \varepsilon$ once: these slices are Cauchy surfaces, and propagation acts on $t > 0$ from any of them; at $\Sigma$ itself the curvature is unbounded, and a state there is initial data to be matched, as in Premise \claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into-descended-phase-premise}.

\emph{(iv)} $-dt^{2} + t^{2p}\delta = t^{2p}(-t^{-2p}dt^{2} + \delta)$; the bracket's cometric $\mathrm{diag}(-t^{2p}, 1, 1, 1)$ has radical $dt$ at $t = 0$ for $p > 0$ and determinant of order $2p$, so it is tame exactly when $2p = 1$. For a spatially flat field of a perfect fluid with $P = w\rho$ the standard solution is $a = t^{p}$, $p = 2/(3(1 + w))$; in Gauge Theory Gravity the field $N = 1$, $A_{i} = t^{p}$ has $\kappa_{0i} = p(p - 1)t^{-2}$, $\kappa_{ij} = p^{2}t^{-2}$, so $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}) = 3p(p - 1)t^{-2}e_{0}$, $\mathcal{R}(e_{j}) = p(3p - 1)t^{-2}e_{j}$, $\mathcal{R} = 6p(2p - 1)t^{-2}$, and the Einstein map is $\mathcal{G}(e_{0}) = -3p^{2}t^{-2}e_{0}$, $\mathcal{G}(e_{j}) = p(2 - 3p)t^{-2}e_{j}$; the field equation $\mathcal{G}(a) = -8\pi T(a)$ with $T(e_{0}) = \rho e_{0}$, $T(e_{j}) = -Pe_{j}$ gives $\rho = 3p^{2}/(8\pi t^{2})$, $P = p(2 - 3p)/(8\pi t^{2})$, and $P = w\rho$ is $2 - 3p = 3wp$, $p = 2/(3(1 + w))$. The check recomputes it at five values of $w$ (in GTG and with the coordinate engine, $G_{xx} = w\,a^{2}G_{tt}$) and finds the tame case only at $w = \tfrac13$, $p = \tfrac12$. Then $g_{\mathrm{FRW}} = t\,g_{1,0}$, and the wall's $\tau = 2\sqrt{t}$ is the conformal time $\int dt/a$. At $p = \tfrac12$: $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}) = -\tfrac34 t^{-2}e_{0}$, $\mathcal{R}(e_{j}) = \tfrac14 t^{-2}e_{j}$, so $\mathcal{R} = 0$ and the Ricci square is $\mathcal{R}(\partial_{a})\cdot\mathcal{R}(a) = \sum_{a}\mathcal{R}(e^{a})\cdot\mathcal{R}(e_{a}) = \tfrac{9}{16}t^{-4} + 3\cdot\tfrac{1}{16}t^{-4} = \tfrac34 t^{-4}$ (in components $R_{ab}R^{ab}$, which the coordinate engine also returns). The massless Dirac field and the Maxwell and Yang-Mills fields are conformally covariant in four dimensions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(b); the stored Fact \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly} names the Yang-Mills actions as conformal-level objects), so for them the radiation-dominated field is, up to the factor $t$, the physical side of (i): the origin is the initial slice $\tau = 0$ of half of Minkowski space, a Cauchy surface of its extension, and the Weyl curvature vanishes there. The conformal-time reading is not special to radiation: for every $p < 1$ the conformal time $\eta = t^{1 - p}/(1 - p)$ is finite, $d\eta/dt = t^{-p}$ turns the bracket into $-d\eta^{2} + \delta$ (the check verifies $-t^{-2p}(dt/d\eta)^{2} = -1$ at the four sampled $w$ with $p < 1$), and in $t' = \eta^{2}/4$ this is $g_{1,0}$, by the computation of (i). What singles out $w = \tfrac13$ is only that the bracket is a tame wall in the cosmic coordinate $t$. \emph{Smoothness in $t$ at the radiation origin depends on the conformal weight, not on (ii).} With $a = t^{1/2} = \tau/2$, a conformally covariant field of weight $s$ is $a^{-s}$ times a solution on the flat half-space. For the massless scalar ($R = 0$, so minimal and conformal coupling agree) $\phi = t^{-1/2}\phi_{\mathrm{flat}}$; its equation $\phi'' + \tfrac{3}{2t}\phi' + \tfrac{k^{2}}{t}\phi = 0$ has indicial exponents $0$ and $-\tfrac12$, and the solutions smooth in $t$ are those with $\phi_{\mathrm{flat}}$ odd in $\tau$ (for example $2\sin(k\tau)/\tau$, which the check expands in $t$ and verifies coefficient by coefficient at three values of $k^{2}$, while $2\cos(k\tau)/\tau$ starts at $t^{-1/2}$): the opposite half from (ii). For the massless Dirac field $\psi = a^{-3/2}\psi_{\mathrm{flat}} = t^{-3/4}\psi_{\mathrm{flat}}$, and $\psi_{\mathrm{flat}}$ smooth in $\tau$ contributes powers $\tau^{n} = 2^{n}t^{n/2}$, so the exponents of $\psi$ are $-\tfrac34 + \tfrac{n}{2}$, never integers: no nonzero solution is smooth in $t$, whatever its parity. So which solutions are smooth in $t$ is weight-dependent, and at the radiation origin the cosmic coordinate supplies no Dirac data for a reason different from (ii). \emph{(Argued.)} For a gauge potential smooth in $t$ the electric field $F_{\tau i} = \sqrt{t}\,F_{ti}$ vanishes on $\Sigma$: the same Lagrangian half.

\emph{Reading (argued, not part of the statement).} The chain of op.deposit-state-is-hadamard needs, at its second step, the descent's surface to be a Cauchy surface on which the deposit is Hadamard. At an aligned tame wall with the radical normal, and for the conformal fields at a radiation-dominated origin, the surface is a regular initial slice in the proper (conformal) time and the propagation step holds from any collar $0 < \tau < \varepsilon$; but smoothness at the wall supplies no state: in its own smooth structure it carries a Lagrangian half of the bulk scalar data and none of the Dirac data in the constant frame, and in the proper time it is a regular boundary imposing no condition. Two possible selectors are not examined here: the boundary modes that the wall carries by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem} (the Witt partner and its bilinears), which are not bulk fields, and the Riemannian far side read as the domain of a Euclidean (no-boundary) path integral, which for the flat half-space would give the vacuum's wave functional. The descent's conditional expectation selects nothing either: it is the identity on its range (Theorem \claimref{transport.pinching-kernel}(i)), so there it returns the state it is applied to, and outside its range it only erases the coherences with the adjoined pair; every state, Hadamard or not, is a possible input. The missing datum is therefore a Hadamard state on a collar of the wall, which neither smoothness at the wall nor the descent's expectation selects. At a wall with the radical tangent, and at the Kasner walls of (P1) and (P2), the surface is singular and the state there is initial data to be matched. Which case the descent is, the store does not fix: the dating's pre-metric reading (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}, a conjecture) is silent on the wall's normal form, and the far side of a radical-normal wall is Riemannian rather than pre-metric. The propagation reaches only the domain of dependence of the collar, by the definition of a Cauchy surface: where a later field has a Cauchy horizon, as the store's charged and rotating holes do, it stops there; for the Reissner-Nordstr\"om-de Sitter field the renormalised stress tensor of a Hadamard state generically diverges at the Cauchy horizon (Hollands, Wald and Zahn 2020, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-stress-tensor-diverges-at-the-reissner-nordstrom-de-sitter-cauchy-horizon}). Transport-absent: the computations are standard signature-change and conformal geometry, applied to the series' tame walls. Signature change at a degenerate metric, and the question whether momenta vanish at the change, were studied by Ellis, Sumeruk, Coule and Hellaby (Class. Quantum Grav. 9 (1992) 1535) and by Dray, Manogue and Tucker (Gen. Rel. Grav. 23 (1991) 967), cited from memory; there the metric, not the cometric, degenerates.

synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower.technical:
Read as an element of the tower, the rung field $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ is odd, so every state invariant under the tower grading gives it zero expectation; its invariants are even, $c^{2} = Q(c)$ and $\{c^{*}, c\} = 2\mathsf{N}(c)$, and in the Fock state annihilated by the $w_{a}$, $\omega(c^{*}c) = |\alpha|^{2}$ and $\omega(cc^{*}) = |\beta|^{2}$, so $m = \tfrac12\omega(c^{*}c - cc^{*})$.

On the sixteen-dimensional algebra of the two rung planes the isospin Casimir is $0$ on five and $2$ on three even dimensions and $\tfrac34$ on all eight odd ones: only odd elements are doublets, so nothing bosonic built from the rung modes alone carries the rung field's quantum numbers. With a generator $g$ from outside the rung planes, $x_{a} = v_{a}g$ is an even doublet, but it obeys the canonical anticommutation relations ($\{x_{a}, x_{b}^{*}\} = \delta_{ab}$, $x_{a}^{2} = 0$), not the canonical commutation relations. The time direction $\gamma_{0}$ would serve as $g$, but then $v_{a}\gamma_{0}$ is not a Lorentz scalar; a Lorentz-scalar even doublet needs a generator outside both spacetime and the rung planes.
synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower.lay: The series' Higgs candidate, the rung field, takes its values in four special directions of the series' algebra, the same directions that serve as fermion creation and annihilation operators. Read that way the field itself is fermion-like and can have no average value, so it cannot be the condensate. Built purely from those four directions, no boson-like quantity has the Higgs field's charges at all. Borrowing one further direction gives a boson-like quantity with the right charges, but it still obeys fermion rules, and if the borrowed direction is the time direction the quantity is not even a scalar. The route this leaves for a composite Higgs, argued here rather than proved, is a condensate of further fermion fields, as in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio picture, not of the rung directions themselves.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Realise the two rung planes in $\Cl(2,2)$ with orthonormal $e_{a}$, $f_{a}$ ($e_{a}^{2} = 1$, $f_{a}^{2} = -1$) and $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} + f_{a})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} - f_{a})$; then $v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$ and $\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \delta_{ab}$, the tower's CAR on these planes (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), and $\mathcal{A} = \Cl(2,2)$, sixteen-dimensional, with parity the grade parity. The bilinears $t_{j} = \sum v_{a}(\tfrac12\sigma_{j})_{ab}w_{b}$ satisfy $[t_{j}, v_{c}] = \sum_{a}(\tfrac12\sigma_{j})_{ac}v_{a}$ (from $[v_{a}w_{b}, v_{c}] = \delta_{bc}v_{a}$), so their commutators realise the slot mixing on the $v_{a}$ as the doublet and on the $w_{a}$ as the conjugate doublet of \claimref{standard-model.ten-transported-ambient-space-doublets-are}. The check uses the real elements $t_{1}$, $t_{3}$ and $t_{2}' = [t_{3}, t_{1}] = I_{4}t_{2}$ (coefficients read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, as below), verifies $[t_{3}, t_{2}'] = t_{1}$, and forms the Casimir $C(x) = [t_{1},[t_{1},x]] + [t_{3},[t_{3},x]] - [t_{2}',[t_{2}',x]]$, which is $\sum_{j}\mathrm{ad}_{t_{j}}^{2}$ because $\mathrm{ad}_{t_{2}}^{2} = -\mathrm{ad}_{t_{2}'}^{2}$. The coefficients of $c$ lie in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, which commutes with the rung vectors (four sign changes past $\gamma_{0}, \ldots, \gamma_{3}$), so every statement below holds verbatim with $I_{4}$-complex coefficients; the check uses real coefficients.

\emph{(1).} $c$ is a combination of vectors, so odd. If $\omega\circ\theta = \omega$ for the grading automorphism $\theta$, then $\omega(c) = \omega(\theta(c)) = -\omega(c) = 0$. The Fock state annihilated by $w_{4}, w_{5}$ is grading invariant (it is $x \mapsto \langle PxP\rangle_{0}/\langle P\rangle_{0}$ with the even projector $P = w_{4}v_{4}w_{5}v_{5}$; the check confirms it vanishes on every odd blade and is normalised). $c^{2} = \sum\alpha_{a}\beta_{b}\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = Q(c)$ and $\{c^{*}, c\} = |\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2} = 2\mathsf{N}(c)$ by the CAR. With $w_{a}\Omega = 0$ the only nonzero two-point values are $\omega(w_{a}v_{b}) = \delta_{ab}$, so $\omega(c^{*}c) = \sum|\alpha_{a}|^{2}\omega(w_{a}v_{a}) = |\alpha|^{2}$ and $\omega(cc^{*}) = |\beta|^{2}$; hence $m = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2}) = \tfrac12\omega(c^{*}c - cc^{*})$. The check evaluates all of these exactly at two points.

\emph{(2).} The even part of $\mathcal{A}$ is spanned by the products of an even number of the $v_{a}, w_{a}$, which as $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ modules are summands of tensor products of an even number of doublets, so they carry integer isospin; the odd part, of an odd number, carries half-integer isospin, and since the Casimir has eigenvalue $j(j+1)$, the possible values are $0, 2$ on the even part and half-integer values on the odd part; which values occur is settled by the computation. The check computes the Casimir on all sixteen basis blades and finds, exactly by rank, $0$ on a five-dimensional subspace (the scalars $1$, the total mode number, $v_{4}v_{5}$, $w_{4}w_{5}$ and $v_{4}w_{4}v_{5}w_{5}$ span it), $2$ on a three-dimensional one (the traceless bilinears $t_{j}$), and $\tfrac34$ on the whole odd part. A charge-preserving vacuum of the rung field has a doublet order parameter (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(1): the stabiliser of $c_{\lambda}$ in $U(2)$ is one circle, so the vacuum value is a doublet direction, not a singlet or triplet); an expectation value of an even element of $\mathcal{A}$ transforms in the even module, isospin $0$ or $1$, so it is never that order parameter. (An isospin-one condensate $\omega(t_{j}) \ne 0$ would be a triplet vacuum, a different breaking pattern.)

\emph{(3).} Let $g$ anticommute with the four rung vectors, so it commutes with every even element, in particular with the $t_{j}$, and $g^{2} = 1$. Then $x_{a} = v_{a}g$ is even and $[t_{j}, x_{a}] = [t_{j}, v_{a}]g$, a doublet with Casimir $\tfrac34$. With $x_{a}^{*} = g w_{a}$: $x_{a}x_{b}^{*} = v_{a}g^{2}w_{b} = v_{a}w_{b}$ and $x_{b}^{*}x_{a} = gw_{b}v_{a}g = w_{b}v_{a}$, so $\{x_{a}, x_{b}^{*}\} = \delta_{ab}$; $x_{a}x_{b} = -v_{a}v_{b}$, so $\{x_{a}, x_{b}\} = -\{v_{a}, v_{b}\} = 0$ and $x_{a}^{2} = 0$; and $[x_{a}, x_{a}^{*}] = v_{a}w_{a} - w_{a}v_{a} = 2v_{a}w_{a} - 1$. These are the relations of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iv) for slot operators, here read for the rung modes. The hypotheses on $g$ are met by $\gamma_{0}$: it squares to $1$ and anticommutes with the rung vectors, which are orthogonal to spacetime. But $\gamma_{0}$ anticommutes with $\gamma_{1}$, so $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$ commutes with $v_{a}$ and anticommutes with $\gamma_{0}$, giving $[\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}, v_{a}\gamma_{0}] = 2\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}v_{a}\gamma_{0} \ne 0$: $v_{a}\gamma_{0}$ is moved by the boost rotors, not a Lorentz scalar. A Lorentz-scalar even doublet therefore needs $g$ orthogonal to spacetime as well as to the rung planes (the check verifies the $\gamma_{0}$ case in $\Cl(3,5)$).

\emph{Reading (argued).} A bosonic doublet with $[b, b^{*}] \to 1$ therefore needs many modes: with $n$ momentum modes of a doublet fermion field paired with $n$ modes of a singlet one, $b_{a} = n^{-1/2}\sum_{j}v_{a,j}u_{j}$ is the doublet analogue of the quasi-spin of \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}, reaching the canonical commutation relations only as $n \to \infty$ on bounded occupation. The two rung planes are fixed directions of the transported ambient space, one null pair each, not such a field. So within the tower the remaining composite route is a doublet-singlet fermion condensate of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio kind (\claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}, at mean field), not a composite of the rung modes; whether a light composite of several fermion species exists is not decided here. The conclusion that the rung field is an elementary (palatial) field is argued, not proved: a separate locality argument for the attached free fields (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}) reaches it for a local elementary rung scalar. Transport-convenient: the identification of the rung field's values with tower modes is the series'; the representation theory is standard.

synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-str.formal:
Let the rung field $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus} take values in the complexified rung summand inside $\Cl(3,5)$ (spacetime and the two rung planes), with coefficients in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, \claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}), eight real components each with kinetic coefficient one, and the scale-free quartic of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(3), $V = k_{1}A^{2} + k_{2}B^{2} + k_{3}AB + A(k_{4}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{5}\operatorname{Im}Q) + B(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}Q) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$, $A = |\alpha|^{2}$, $B = |\beta|^{2}$, $Q = c^{2} = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$. Gauge couplings $g$, $g'$; third family coupled as in \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix} with $\tilde{Y}_{33} = y$ and $Y_{33}$ neglected. Write $w = 9g^{2} + 3g'^{2}$, $G = \tfrac{9}{32}g^{4} + \tfrac{3}{16}g^{2}g'^{2} + \tfrac{3}{32}g'^{4}$, $s = k_{8}^{2} + k_{9}^{2}$, $t = \ln\mu$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The field's symmetries and coupling from the algebra; proved.)} With $b_{a} = v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$, the maps $\tfrac12[I_{4}(v_{4}w_{5} + v_{5}w_{4}), \cdot]$, $\tfrac12[v_{4}w_{5} - v_{5}w_{4}, \cdot]$, $\tfrac12[I_{4}(b_{4} - b_{5}), \cdot]$ and $\tfrac12[I_{4}(b_{4} + b_{5}), \cdot]$ on rung values are the stored $T_{1}$, $T_{2}$, $T_{3}$ and $Y$ (on the coefficients, $\alpha \mapsto \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \overline{\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{j}}\beta$, and $\pm\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}$), and $V$ is invariant. At the third family the covariant coupling is $y\,\epsilon(q, \bar{\beta})u^{c} - y\,(q\cdot\bar{\alpha})d^{c}$ in Weyl fields, invariant under $SU(2) \times U(1)$ with hypercharges $\tfrac16$, $-\tfrac23$, $\tfrac13$: the doublet $\beta$ carries the top mass and the doublet $\alpha$ couples to $(q, d^{c})$ with the same strength. Below, $y_{2}$ is its coefficient on $\bar\beta$ and $y_{1}$ on $\bar\alpha$; the covariant coupling has $y_{1} = y_{2} = m_{t}/v$ at the vacuum.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One loop; proved, computed exactly; the terms in $g$, $g'$ come from internal gauge lines in Landau gauge and hold under the Krein premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, as for the stored one-loop running.)} On the branch $k_{4} = k_{5} = k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$, which the running preserves at one and at two loops,
\begin{align*}
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{1} &= 96k_{1}^{2} + 8k_{3}^{2} + 8k_{3}k_{10} + 4k_{10}^{2} + 4s + G - wk_{1} + 24k_{1}y_{1}^{2} - 6y_{1}^{4},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{2} &= 96k_{2}^{2} + 8k_{3}^{2} + 8k_{3}k_{10} + 4k_{10}^{2} + 4s + G - wk_{2} + 24k_{2}y_{2}^{2} - 6y_{2}^{4},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{3} &= 48(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{3} + 16(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{10} + 16k_{3}^{2} + 8k_{10}^{2} + 8s + \tfrac{9}{16}g^{4} - \tfrac38g^{2}g'^{2} + \tfrac{3}{16}g'^{4} - wk_{3} + 12k_{3}(y_{1}^{2} + y_{2}^{2}) - 12y_{1}^{2}y_{2}^{2},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{10} &= 16(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{10} + 32k_{3}k_{10} + 16k_{10}^{2} + 32s + \tfrac34g^{2}g'^{2} - wk_{10} + 12k_{10}(y_{1}^{2} + y_{2}^{2}) + 12y_{1}^{2}y_{2}^{2},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{8,9} &= k_{8,9}\bigl(16(k_{1} + k_{2}) + 32k_{3} + 48k_{10} - w + 12(y_{1}^{2} + y_{2}^{2})\bigr);
\end{align*}
the forms with $k_{4}, \ldots, k_{7}$ are in Step 2. Under $\lambda_{1} = 8k_{1}$, $\lambda_{2} = 8k_{2}$, $\lambda_{3} = 4k_{3}$, $\lambda_{4} = 4k_{10}$, $\lambda_{5} = 4(k_{8} - I_{4}k_{9})$, $y_{b} = \sqrt2y_{1}$, $y_{t} = \sqrt2y_{2}$ these are the standard one-loop equations of the two-doublet model with a discrete symmetry and type-II couplings (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-general-quartic-running-and-two-doublet-renormalisation-group-equations}(ii)); under the covariant completion the down-type doublet's coupling is the top's.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Two loops, pure-quartic part; proved, computed exactly.)} On the same branch,
\begin{align*}
(16\pi^{2})^{2}\dot k_{1}^{(2)} &= -4992k_{1}^{3} - 320k_{1}k_{3}^{2} - 320k_{1}k_{3}k_{10} - 192k_{1}k_{10}^{2} - 224k_{1}s - 128k_{3}^{3} - 192k_{3}^{2}k_{10} - 256k_{3}k_{10}^{2} - 96k_{10}^{3} - 320k_{3}s - 352k_{10}s,\\
(16\pi^{2})^{2}\dot k_{3}^{(2)} &= -(k_{1}^{2} + k_{2}^{2})(960k_{3} + 256k_{10}) - (k_{1} + k_{2})(1152k_{3}^{2} + 512k_{3}k_{10} + 448k_{10}^{2} + 576s) - 192k_{3}^{3} - 64k_{3}^{2}k_{10} - 256k_{3}k_{10}^{2} - 192k_{10}^{3} - 288k_{3}s - 704k_{10}s,\\
(16\pi^{2})^{2}\dot k_{10}^{(2)} &= -448(k_{1}^{2} + k_{2}^{2})k_{10} - 1280(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{3}k_{10} - 640(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{10}^{2} - 768(k_{1} + k_{2})s - 448k_{3}^{2}k_{10} - 448k_{3}k_{10}^{2} - 768k_{3}s - 416k_{10}s,\\
(16\pi^{2})^{2}\dot k_{8,9}^{(2)} &= k_{8,9}\bigl(-448(k_{1}^{2} + k_{2}^{2}) - 1280(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{3} - 1408(k_{1} + k_{2})k_{10} - 448k_{3}^{2} - 1216k_{3}k_{10} - 512k_{10}^{2} + 96s\bigr),
\end{align*}
and $\dot k_{2}^{(2)}$ is $\dot k_{1}^{(2)}$ with $k_{1} \to k_{2}$. The two-loop gauge and Yukawa terms are not computed.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The flat direction; proved.)} On the stored flat ray ($k_{2} = k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$, vacuum $\alpha = 0$, $|\beta| = v$), with the stored tree masses $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac14g^{2}v^{2}$, $M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac14(g^{2} + g'^{2})v^{2}$, $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2k_{3}v^{2}$, $m_{H,A}^{2} = 2v^{2}(k_{3} + k_{10} \pm \sqrt{s})$, $m_{t} = y_{2}v$,
\[
2v^{4}\cdot16\pi^{2}\dot k_{2} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4} + 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} - 12m_{t}^{4},
\]
so the Gildener-Weinberg scalon mass of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(4) is $m_{h}^{2} = 4v^{2}\dot k_{2}$: the scalon sum is the one-loop running of the flat-direction quartic (standard, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}). Along the ray the one-loop potential $B\rho^{4}(\ln(\rho^{2}/v^{2}) - \tfrac12)$ gives $V''(v) = 8Bv^{2} = m_{h}^{2}$ and $V'''(v) = 40Bv = \tfrac53\cdot3m_{h}^{2}/v$ (standard for Gildener-Weinberg potentials).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Strong coupling; computed.)} If the Gildener-Weinberg formula holds and the Majorana and Pati-Salam sectors decouple (the hypotheses of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(4)), then starting at $\mu_{0} = m_{t}$ on the scalon-sum surface $2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} \in (2\cdot450^{4}, 2\cdot456^{4})$ GeV$^{4}$ with $k_{1}(\mu_{0}) = k_{2}(\mu_{0}) = 0$, the gauge couplings running with the stored two-doublet coefficients of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}, the largest of $|\lambda_{1}|, \ldots, |\lambda_{5}|$ reaches $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV with the one-loop equations, and the one-loop couplings diverge between about $2$ and $11$ TeV; a larger $k_{1}(\mu_{0}) \ge 0$ lowers these scales. At the crossing the two-loop pure-quartic terms of (iii) are already $30$ to $70$ percent of the one-loop terms; adding them moves the crossing to between about $1$ and $15$ TeV, a shift that marks strong coupling rather than a controlled estimate.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-str.technical:
Quantised as an elementary field, the series' rung field is a two-doublet scalar field, and on its scale-free branch the measured Higgs mass fixes the fourth powers of the other scalar masses through the scalon sum, which forces large quartic couplings. This result gives the running of those couplings in the series' own variables. The gauge generators are commutators with bivectors of the two rung planes (with $I_{4}$ as the unit), the quartic is the stored ten-invariant potential, and the top coupling is the series' covariant reading, under which the doublet without a vacuum value couples to the top with full strength, like the other doublet.

The one-loop equations follow from the renormalisation-group invariance of the one-loop effective potential and coincide with the standard two-doublet equations under an explicit dictionary; the two-loop pure-quartic terms follow from the general formula. Both are checked in exact arithmetic against the field's own fourth-derivative tensor. On the flat direction the running of the vanishing quartic reproduces the stored scalon sum with the neutral normal pair, so the stored Higgs mass relation is a statement about running. Integrating the one-loop equations from the top mass on the scalon-sum surface, some quartic reaches $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV, where the two-loop terms are already a large fraction of the one-loop ones: the transmutation branch of the elementary rung field is a strongly coupled theory not far above the weak scale. The gauge contributions come from internal gauge lines and hold under the Krein premise, as the stored running coefficients do. With the same coupling reading the branch is also excluded by $B$-meson mixing (\claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch}).
synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-str.lay: The series' Higgs field, read as an elementary quantum field, has eight components and, on the branch where all masses come from quantum effects, must have its extra particles near 400 to 500 GeV. That needs strong self-interactions. This result computes how those interactions change with energy, using the series' own description of the field, and finds that, under the approximations assumed for that branch, they grow too strong for ordinary calculation within a few TeV.

\emph{Step 1 (clause (i)).} The rung field is that of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}, with the stored slot action. In $\Cl(3,5)$ take $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} + f_{a})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} - f_{a})$ for the rung planes $a = 4, 5$, so $v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$, $\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \delta_{ab}$, and $I_{4}$ commutes with every $v_{a}$, $w_{a}$ (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(1)). For $x, y$ in $\{v_{4}, v_{5}, w_{4}, w_{5}\}$, $[xy, z] = x\{y, z\} - \{x, z\}y$ for a vector $z$, so $[v_{4}w_{5}, v_{5}] = v_{4}$, $[v_{4}w_{5}, w_{4}] = -w_{5}$, $[v_{5}w_{4}, v_{4}] = v_{5}$, $[v_{5}w_{4}, w_{5}] = -w_{4}$, and $[b_{a}, v_{a}] = v_{a}$, $[b_{a}, w_{a}] = -w_{a}$ (loc. cit. Step 2). Reading the coefficients of $c$ gives: $\tfrac12[I_{4}(v_{4}w_{5} + v_{5}w_{4}), \cdot]$ maps $\alpha \mapsto \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{1}\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto -\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{1}\beta$; $\tfrac12[v_{4}w_{5} - v_{5}w_{4}, \cdot]$ maps both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ by the real matrix $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{2}$; $\tfrac12[I_{4}(b_{4} \mp b_{5}), \cdot]$ maps $\alpha \mapsto \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{3}\alpha$ or $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\alpha$ and $\beta$ by the conjugates. These are the stored $T_{1}$, $T_{2}$, $T_{3}$, $Y$ with the unit $I_{4}$. The coefficients are read back by $\alpha_{a} = \{w_{a}, c\}$, $\beta_{a} = \{v_{a}, c\}$, and $Q = c^{2}$ by the Clifford product. The check builds the four generators and the form $Q$ in the GA engine and verifies them against the stored action, and verifies $\nabla V\cdot t\varphi = 0$ for all four. For the coupling: by \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}, at a point with only rung-$4$ components $M_{d} = \beta Y + \bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y}$ and $M_{u} = \alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y}$; with $Y_{33}$ neglected the third family has $M_{u} = \bar{\beta}_{4}y$, $M_{d} = \bar{\alpha}_{4}y$, whose $SU(2)$-covariant completion in Weyl fields $q$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$ is $y\,\epsilon(q, \bar\beta)u^{c} - y\,(q\cdot\bar\alpha)d^{c}$ (under $X \in SU(2)$, $\bar{\beta} \mapsto X\bar{\beta}$, $\bar{\alpha} \mapsto \bar{X}\bar{\alpha}$, and $\epsilon(Xq, X\bar\beta) = \epsilon(q, \bar\beta)$, $(Xq)\cdot(\bar X\bar\alpha) = q\cdot\bar\alpha$); the hypercharges balance, $\tfrac16 + \tfrac12 - \tfrac23 = 0$ and $\tfrac16 - \tfrac12 + \tfrac13 = 0$. The check verifies the invariance $M_{F}(t\varphi) + \tau^{\mathsf T}M_{F} + M_{F}\tau = 0$ for the four generators exactly, and that at $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-1, 0)$ only the top pair has mass. Both couplings equal $\tilde{Y}_{33}$, so $y_{1} = y_{2} = m_{t}/v$ at the vacuum.

\emph{Step 2 (clause (ii)).} The gauge loops are taken in Landau gauge with the indefinite form of the Krein premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields} on the gauge field, as in the stored one-loop running; the scalar and Yukawa terms do not use it. For real scalars $\varphi$ with a scale-free quartic $V$, vector masses $M_{V}^{2}(\varphi)_{AB} = g_{A}g_{B}(t_{A}\varphi)\cdot(t_{B}\varphi)$ and Weyl mass matrix $M_{F}(\varphi)$, the one-loop effective potential in Landau gauge is $V + \tfrac{1}{64\pi^{2}}\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4}(\ln M^{2}/\mu^{2} - c)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}(i)), with $\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4} = \operatorname{Tr}V''^{2} + 3\operatorname{Tr}M_{V}^{4} - 2\operatorname{Tr}(M_{F}M_{F}^{\dagger})^{2}$. Its independence of $\mu$ at this order, together with the field's anomalous dimension $\gamma = Y_{2}(S) + 3\sum_{A}g_{A}^{2}t_{A}t_{A}$, $Y_{2}(S)_{ab} = \tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(Y^{a\dagger}Y^{b} + Y^{b\dagger}Y^{a})$, $Y^{a} = \partial M_{F}/\partial\varphi_{a}$, gives
\[
16\pi^{2}\beta_{V}(\varphi) = \tfrac12\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}V''^{2} + 3\operatorname{Tr}M_{V}^{4} - 2\operatorname{Tr}(M_{F}M_{F}^{\dagger})^{2}\bigr) + \varphi\cdot\gamma\nabla V,
\]
the one-loop part of the general formula \cite{MachacekVaughn1985, LuoWangXiao2003} written as a polynomial (cited from memory). The check confirms the normalisation on one doublet ($V = \lambda|H|^{4}$ gives $24\lambda^{2} - 3\lambda(3g^{2} + g'^{2}) + \tfrac38(2g^{4} + (g^{2} + g'^{2})^{2}) + 12\lambda y_{t}^{2} - 6y_{t}^{4}$) and on $O(N)$, $N = 1, 8$ ($(N + 8)/3$ times $\lambda^{2}$ for $V = \tfrac{\lambda}{24}(\varphi^{2})^{2}$ \cite{KleinertSchulteFrohlinde2001}). Since $\beta_{V}$ is $U(2)$-invariant and quartic it is a combination of the ten invariants; the check computes the fourth-derivative tensor of $V$ by polarisation, $\beta_{V}$ at sampled points and couplings, and compares with $\sum_{i}\dot k_{i}P_{i}(\varphi)$ for the closed forms. The general forms are those of clause (ii) plus, with $\kappa = 12(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2})$ and $\kappa' = 12(k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2})$: $\kappa$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{1}$, $\kappa'$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{2}$, $4(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2}) + 16(k_{4}k_{6} + k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{3}$, $10(k_{4}^{2} - k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} - k_{7}^{2}) + 4(k_{4}k_{6} - k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{8}$, $20(k_{4}k_{5} + k_{6}k_{7}) + 4(k_{4}k_{7} + k_{5}k_{6})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{9}$, $10(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2}) + 4(k_{4}k_{6} + k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{10}$, and
\begin{align*}
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{4} &= (96k_{1} + 24k_{3} + 32k_{10} + 40k_{8})k_{4} + 40k_{9}k_{5} + (24k_{3} + 16k_{10} + 8k_{8})k_{6} + 8k_{9}k_{7} - wk_{4} + (18y_{1}^{2} + 6y_{2}^{2})k_{4},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{5} &= (96k_{1} + 24k_{3} + 32k_{10} - 40k_{8})k_{5} + 40k_{9}k_{4} + (24k_{3} + 16k_{10} - 8k_{8})k_{7} + 8k_{9}k_{6} - wk_{5} + (18y_{1}^{2} + 6y_{2}^{2})k_{5},
\end{align*}
and $\dot k_{6}$, $\dot k_{7}$ the same with $(k_{1}, k_{4}, k_{5}, y_{1}, y_{2}) \leftrightarrow (k_{2}, k_{6}, k_{7}, y_{2}, y_{1})$. Every term of $\dot k_{4}, \ldots, \dot k_{7}$ contains one of $k_{4}, \ldots, k_{7}$, so the branch $k_{4} = \cdots = k_{7} = 0$ is preserved; it is the branch of the stored physical ray when also $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$ there is required (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(3)). The coupling is invariant under $\alpha \to -\alpha$, $d^{c} \to -d^{c}$, which is why no $k_{4}, \ldots, k_{7}$ is generated; the neglected $Y_{33}$ breaks it at order $y_{t}^{3}y_{b}$.

\emph{Step 3 (dictionary).} With canonical real components $|\beta|^{2} = v^{2}$, so the doublets of the standard normalisation are $\Phi = \beta/\sqrt2$, $\alpha/\sqrt2$ (with the conjugations of Step 1), and $|\Phi_{1}^{\dagger}\Phi_{2}| = \tfrac12|Q|$: $\tfrac{\lambda_{1}}{2}|\Phi_{1}|^{4} = k_{1}A^{2}$ gives $\lambda_{1} = 8k_{1}$, and likewise $\lambda_{2} = 8k_{2}$, $\lambda_{3} = 4k_{3}$, $\lambda_{4} = 4k_{10}$, $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_{5} = 4k_{8}$, $|\operatorname{Im}\lambda_{5}| = 4|k_{9}|$; the top coupling of the canonical doublet is $\sqrt2 y_{2} = y_{t}$. The check substitutes these into the standard one-loop equations of the two-doublet model with a discrete symmetry and type-II couplings (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-general-quartic-running-and-two-doublet-renormalisation-group-equations}(ii): $16\pi^{2}\dot\lambda_{1} = 12\lambda_{1}^{2} + 4\lambda_{3}^{2} + 4\lambda_{3}\lambda_{4} + 2\lambda_{4}^{2} + 2|\lambda_{5}|^{2} + \tfrac34(3g^{4} + g'^{4} + 2g^{2}g'^{2}) - 3\lambda_{1}(3g^{2} + g'^{2}) + 12\lambda_{1}y_{b}^{2} - 12y_{b}^{4}$, and the forms for $\lambda_{2}$ to $\lambda_{5}$) and finds them equal to the closed forms term by term at sampled couplings. The masses of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(3), $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2k_{3}v^{2}$, $m_{H,A}^{2} = m_{\pm}^{2} + 2v^{2}(k_{10} \pm r)$, are the familiar $\tfrac12\lambda_{3}v^{2}$ and $\tfrac12(\lambda_{3} + \lambda_{4} \pm |\lambda_{5}|)v^{2}$ of a doublet without a vacuum value.

\emph{Step 4 (clause (iii)).} For $V = \tfrac{1}{24}\lambda_{abcd}\varphi_{a}\varphi_{b}\varphi_{c}\varphi_{d}$ the pure-quartic two-loop term of the general formula, $-\tfrac14\sum_{\mathrm{perms}}\lambda_{abef}\lambda_{cegh}\lambda_{dfgh} + \sum_{\mathrm{legs}}\gamma^{(2)}\lambda$ with $\gamma^{(2)}_{ab} = \tfrac{1}{12}\lambda_{acde}\lambda_{bcde}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-general-quartic-running-and-two-doublet-renormalisation-group-equations}(i)), contracted with $\varphi^{4}/24$ is $-\tfrac12V''_{ef}V'''_{egh}V'''_{fgh} + \tfrac{1}{12}(\lambda\lambda)_{ab}\varphi_{a}\partial_{b}V$, since $\lambda_{abef}\varphi_{a}\varphi_{b} = 2V''_{ef}$ and $\lambda_{cegh}\varphi_{c} = V'''_{egh}$. One real scalar gives $-\tfrac14\cdot24 + \tfrac13 = -\tfrac{17}{3}$, and $O(N)$ gives $-(3N + 14)/3$ \cite{KleinertSchulteFrohlinde2001}; the check confirms both for $N = 1$ and $N = 8$, then compares the closed forms of clause (iii) with the field computation at three points; $\dot k_{4}^{(2)}, \ldots, \dot k_{7}^{(2)}$ vanish on the branch. For orientation (computed): at the symmetric point $k_{1} = k_{2} = 0$, $k_{3} = \tfrac65$, $k_{10} = s = 0$ the two-loop term of $\dot k_{3}$ is $-192k_{3}^{3}/(16\pi^{2})^{2}$ against $16k_{3}^{2}/(16\pi^{2})$, a ratio of about $-0.09$.

\emph{Step 5 (clause (iv)).} On the ray $\varphi = (0, 0, 0, 0, -v, 0, 0, 0)$ with $k_{2} = k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$, $\nabla V = 0$ (every term is at least quadratic in $\alpha$ or proportional to $k_{2}$), so $16\pi^{2}\beta_{V} = \tfrac12\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4}$ there and $\beta_{V} = \dot k_{2}v^{4}$. Directly from clause (ii) at $k_{2} = 0$: $2v^{4}(8k_{3}^{2} + 8k_{3}k_{10} + 4k_{10}^{2} + 4s) = 8k_{3}^{2}v^{4} + 8v^{4}((k_{3} + k_{10})^{2} + s) = 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$, $2v^{4}G = \tfrac{1}{16}(6g^{4} + 3(g^{2} + g'^{2})^{2})v^{4} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4}$, and $2v^{4}(-6y_{2}^{4}) = -12m_{t}^{4}$. Along the ray $V_{1\text{-loop}} = (k_{2}(\mu) + B\ln(\rho^{2}/\mu^{2}))\rho^{4}$ up to a constant times $\rho^{4}$, and $\mu$-independence gives $B = \tfrac12\dot k_{2}$; with Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}(ii), $m_{h}^{2} = 8Bv^{2} = 4v^{2}\dot k_{2}$, which is \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(4) and, at its standard reading, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(i). The check verifies the identity at three samples both from the closed form and from the field computation on the ray, and that dropping $m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$ breaks it. For the self-coupling, with $L = \ln(\rho^{2}/v^{2})$ and $dL/d\rho = 2/\rho$, $V = B\rho^{4}(L - \tfrac12)$ has $V' = 4B\rho^{3}L$, $V'' = 12B\rho^{2}L + 8B\rho^{2}$, $V''' = 24B\rho L + 40B\rho$, so at $\rho = v$: $V' = 0$, $V'' = 8Bv^{2} = m_{h}^{2}$, $V''' = 40Bv = \tfrac53(3m_{h}^{2}/v)$, the tree value for the same mass being $3m_{h}^{2}/v$ (standard for Gildener-Weinberg potentials). By homogeneity the scalon couples to each heavy pair with $\partial m_{X}^{2}/\partial\rho = 2m_{X}^{2}/v$, the unit weight used in \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(5).

\emph{Step 6 (clause (v), computed).} Initial values at $\mu_{0} = m_{t}$ (from memory, $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$): $g = 0.648$, $g' = 0.358$, $g_{3} = 1.164$, $y_{t} = 0.936$, so $y_{1} = y_{2} = 0.662$; the gauge couplings run at one loop with the stored two-doublet coefficients $(\tfrac{21}{5}, -3, -7)$ of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces} (gauge loops, so under the Krein premise there too), that is $(7, -3, -7)$ for $(g', g, g_{3})$ with $g'$ in the non-GUT normalisation, and $y_{1} = y_{2}$ with $16\pi^{2}\dot y_{2} = y_{2}(y_{1}^{2} + 9y_{2}^{2} - 8g_{3}^{2} - \tfrac94g^{2} - \tfrac{17}{12}g'^{2})$ (the Yukawa part from the general one-loop formula applied to the coupling of Step 1, computed; its $y_{1} = 0$ limit is the standard $\tfrac92y_{t}^{3}$), with the hypercharge term of the $d^{c}$ coupling, $-\tfrac{5}{12}g'^{2}$, averaged in (negligible here). The quartics start at $k_{3} = m_{\pm}^{2}/(2v^{2})$, $k_{10} = (m_{H}^{2} + m_{A}^{2} - 2m_{\pm}^{2})/(4v^{2})$, $|k_{8}| = |m_{H}^{2} - m_{A}^{2}|/(4v^{2})$, $k_{9} = 0$, $k_{1} = k_{2} = 0$. Fourth-order Runge-Kutta in $t$, step $0.002$ to $0.01$, over a grid of points of the surface (both ends of the sum, $m_{\pm}$ from $80$ to $450$ GeV, the share of $m_{A}^{4}$ from $0$ to $\tfrac12$, $m_{A} > M_{Z}/2$): the scale at which $\max_{i}|\lambda_{i}| = 4\pi$ is between $0.80$ TeV ($m_{\pm} = 80$, $m_{H} = 528$, $m_{A} = 305$ GeV) and $4.0$ TeV ($m_{\pm} = 320$, $m_{H} = m_{A} = 418$ GeV) at one loop, between $1.08$ and $15.1$ TeV with the two-loop pure-quartic terms, which at the one-loop crossing are already $-0.67$ (degenerate end) to $-0.31$ (light charged end) times the one-loop term of the largest coupling, so this shift is not a controlled estimate and is not part of the claim; the first coupling to reach $4\pi$ is $\lambda_{3}$ near the degenerate point and $\lambda_{4}$ for a light charged pair. Starting at $\mu_{0} = v$ instead raises the scales by about $\tfrac{v}{m_{t}} \approx 1.4$; $k_{1}(\mu_{0}) = \tfrac12$ lowers the one-loop scale to about $0.6$ to $0.9$ TeV. Since $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ start equal and $y_{1} = y_{2}$, they run equally on the branch. The check reproduces the two endpoints in exact arithmetic at one loop: the closed forms of clause (ii) with $y_{1} = y_{2} = y$, the gauge and top flow above, fourth-order Runge-Kutta in $t$ with step $\tfrac{1}{25}$ and states rounded to $10^{-12}$, run with $\pi$ replaced by each of $\tfrac{333}{106} < \pi < \tfrac{355}{113}$; the first step with $\max_{i}|\lambda_{i}| \ge 4\pi$ is step $39$ and step $79$, which by rational bounds on $e^{t}$ puts the crossing between $0.75$ and $0.85$ TeV for $(80, 528, 305)$ GeV and between $3.8$ and $4.2$ TeV for $(320, 418, 418)$ GeV (computed; the rounding and the step size are not error-controlled, so this is a reproducible bracket of the computed flow, not a proof).

\emph{Reading.} \claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch} excludes the same branch under the same coupling reading by tree-level $B$-meson mixing. Standard: the one-loop two-doublet equations, the general two-loop formula, the Gildener-Weinberg relation between the flat-direction running and the scalon mass, the $\tfrac53$ self-coupling. New: the equations in the series' invariants with the series' generators and coupling reading (both doublets at top strength), the two-loop pure-quartic terms in those invariants, the check that the stored sum with the normal pair is that running, and the strong-coupling scale of the transmutation branch, which says the elementary rung field on that branch is a perturbative theory only up to a few TeV. The running is regulator independent at this order (only $\mu$ enters). Transport-convenient.
