synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.formal:
Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with the vectors $\gamma_{\mu}$ as Dirac matrices, the unit of the Feynman rules the right unit $x \mapsto xI_{4}$, a coefficient outside the Clifford product (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(5); numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), and the chirality $\gamma_{5}$ acting as $x \mapsto I_{4}xI_{4}$, $I_{4}$ inside the product on the left and that unit on the right, so $\mathrm{Tr}\,X = 4\langle X\rangle_{0}$. Write $S(p) = (p + M)/(Q(p) - M^{2})$. For momenta $k_{1}$, $k_{2}$, $q = k_{1} + k_{2}$ let
\[
D_{1}(\ell) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(\ell)\gamma^{\nu}S(\ell - k_{1})\gamma^{\rho}S(\ell - q)], \quad D_{2}(\ell) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(\ell)\gamma^{\rho}S(\ell - k_{2})\gamma^{\nu}S(\ell - q)],
\]
$P_{1}$, $P_{2}$ the same with $\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}$ replaced by $\gamma_{5}$, and regulate with the Pauli-Villars fields of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(iii) on the fermion loop, weights $c_{i}$ with $\sum_{i}c_{i} = 0$ ($c_{0} = 1$, $M_{0} = m$), $T^{\mu\nu\rho} = \sum_{i}c_{i}\int\frac{d^{4}\ell}{(2\pi)^{4}}(D_{1} + D_{2})|_{M = M_{i}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Trace.) $\mathrm{Tr}(\gamma_{5}abcd) = 4\langle I_{4}abcd\rangle_{0}\,I_{4} = -4\lambda I_{4}$, where $a\wedge b\wedge c\wedge d = \lambda I_{4}$; it is real up to the unit and totally antisymmetric.
\item[(ii)] (Vector Ward identities.) For every $\ell$ and mass, $k_{1\nu}(D_{1} + D_{2})(\ell) = B(\ell - k_{1}) - B(\ell)$ with $B(p) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(p)\gamma^{\rho}S(p - k_{2})]$, and likewise for $k_{2\rho}$. The pseudoscalar part of the numerator of $B$ does not depend on the mass and is odd about the centre of the loop, and $\sum_{i}c_{i}/((Q(\ell) - M_{i}^{2})(Q(\ell - k) - M_{i}^{2})) = O(|\ell|^{-6})$ exactly when $\sum_{i}c_{i} = 0$; so the regulated shift difference integrates to zero and $k_{1\nu}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = k_{2\rho}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = 0$.
\item[(iii)] (Axial divergence.) For every $\ell$, $q_{\mu}(D_{1} + D_{2}) = -2M(P_{1} + P_{2})$ plus four two-point terms of the kind in (ii), which integrate to zero under the regulators. The numerator of $P_{1}$ and of $P_{2}$ over its three denominators is $M \cdot 4\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}\,I_{4}$, independent of $\ell$. With the imported integral $\int\frac{d^{4}\ell}{(2\pi)^{4}}(\ell^{2} - \Delta)^{-3} = -I_{4}/(32\pi^{2}\Delta)$ and $M_{i} \to \infty$ for $i \geq 1$, at $m = 0$
\[
q_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = \frac{1}{2\pi^{2}}\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0},
\]
which depends on the regulators only through $\sum_{i \geq 1}c_{i} = -1$. In the index reading the right side is $\pm\tfrac{1}{2\pi^{2}}\epsilon^{\nu\rho\alpha\beta}k_{1\alpha}k_{2\beta}$, the sign fixed by the orientation convention of $\epsilon$.
\item[(iv)] (Field form.) For polarisations $a_{1}$, $a_{2}$, $\langle I_{4}a_{1}k_{1}a_{2}k_{2}\rangle_{0} = \langle I_{4}f_{1}f_{2}\rangle_{0}$ with the plane-wave field-strength bivectors $f_{j} = a_{j} \wedge k_{j}$, symmetric in the two photons; it is the bilinear form of $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0}$, and for $F = E + I_{4}B$ ($E$, $B$ relative vectors) $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -2E\cdot B$.
\item[(v)] (Chiral fields.) With $P_{L,R} = \tfrac12(1 \mp \gamma_{5})$, $\mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}P_{L}a\gamma^{\nu}P_{L}b\gamma^{\rho}P_{L}c] = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}a\gamma^{\nu}b\gamma^{\rho}cP_{R}]$, half the vector trace plus half the $\gamma_{5}$ trace, so a Weyl loop carries half the Dirac axial term with the sign of its chirality. For left-handed Weyl fields in a representation of a gauge algebra the anomalous part of the three-current triangle is proportional to the symmetric tensor $d(X, Y, Z) = \mathrm{tr}(X\{Y, Z\})$. The projector identity is proved; the reduction to $d$ is argued (Bose symmetrisation, standard).
\item[(vi)] (One generation.) For the left-handed content $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar 3)_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar 3)_{1/3}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content} ($m = 1$), $d$ vanishes on the whole complexified gauge algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{sl}(2) \oplus \C$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors) and $\mathrm{tr}\,X = 0$ for every $X$ (for the hypercharge this is $\mathrm{tr}\,Y = 0$, the imported mixed gravitational coefficient: a trace count, not a computed gauge-gravitational triangle); the cancellation is between fields (the quark doublet alone gives $\mathrm{tr}\,Y^{3} = \tfrac{1}{36}$) and holds generation by generation, for any number of generations.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.technical: In the spacetime algebra the Dirac matrices are the vectors, the trace is four times the scalar part, and the chirality acts as $x \mapsto I_{4}xI_{4}$, the left $I_{4}$ inside the product and the unit, the right $I_{4}$, standing outside it, as the stored one-loop result requires on massive lines. Then the trace of the chirality element with four vectors is four times the pseudoscalar coefficient of their product. For the triangle with one axial and two vector vertices, regulated by Pauli-Villars fermions with weights summing to zero, contracting a vector vertex with its momentum turns the integrand into a difference of two-point terms shifted by that momentum, and since the regulators make those terms fall off fast enough the difference integrates to zero: both vector currents are conserved. Contracting the axial vertex gives the mass term $-2M$ times the pseudoscalar triangle plus terms that integrate to zero. For each regulator the pseudoscalar triangle's numerator is $M$ times a constant, $4\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}\,I_{4}$, with no loop-momentum dependence, so the regulator term tends to a finite limit as its mass grows: the axial divergence of the massless loop is $(1/(2\pi^{2}))\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}$, depending on the regulators only through the sum of their weights. Contracted with polarisations this is the bilinear form of $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -2E\cdot B$, the pseudoscalar part of the square of the field bivector. A chiral vertex collapses its projectors to one, so a Weyl loop carries half the Dirac anomaly with its chirality's sign, and a content of Weyl fields is anomalous through the symmetric tensor $\mathrm{tr}(X\{Y, Z\})$ (the standard reduction, argued here); for one stored generation that tensor vanishes on the whole gauge algebra, generation by generation, and the trace $\mathrm{tr}\,Y$ that enters the imported mixed gravitational condition is zero (a trace count, not a computed triangle). These are standard results (Adler; Bell and Jackiw, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-adler-bell-jackiw-axial-anomaly}); what is new is their form in the spacetime algebra. Every covariant extension conserving both vector currents gives the same axial divergence (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}(iii), given the imported existence of such extensions), so the value does not depend on the Pauli-Villars scheme.
synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.lay: Some symmetries of classical fields fail once quantum effects are included; the classic case is the axial anomaly of a charged particle in an electromagnetic field, found in 1969. This result recomputes that anomaly in the series' own algebra of spacetime, using a standard method of taming the infinities. The anomaly comes out as the part of the squared electromagnetic field that measures how electric and magnetic fields line up, with the textbook strength. For a theory to be consistent, such anomalies must cancel between all the particles that feel a force; the result checks that they cancel within one generation of the series' particles, so the cancellation does not depend on how many generations there are.

synthesis.two-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-.formal:
Under the Krein-form premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields} (the covariant photon, the map $a \mapsto (a - (1 - \xi)(a\cdot r)\,r/Q(r))/Q(r)$ on vectors, in components $(\delta_{\alpha\beta} - (1 - \xi)r_{\alpha}r_{\beta}/Q(r))/Q(r)$, on internal lines, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(iv)), with the vertex of \claimref{field-theory.coupled-system-tree-level}, the conventions of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra} (trace equal to four times the scalar part; the unit of the Feynman rules a coefficient outside the Clifford product), after the Wick rotation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(ii)) and in dimensional regularisation, $d = 4 - 2\epsilon$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(i)). Write $a = \alpha/(4\pi)$, $\Pi_{q}(a) = (Q(q)\,a - (a\cdot q)\,q)\,\Pi(Q(q))$ for the polarisation map of one massless Dirac fermion (in components $\Pi_{\mu\nu}(q) = (Q(q)\delta_{\mu\nu} - q_{\mu}q_{\nu})\Pi(Q(q))$, $\Pi_{\mu\nu} = \gamma_{\mu}\cdot\Pi_{q}(\gamma_{\nu})$), and $G(a_{1}, a_{2})$ for the massless one-loop bubble. The $d$-dimensional integral rules used (the radial integral, symmetric integration in $d$ dimensions, translation invariance, the vanishing of scale-free integrals and of total derivatives, hence integration by parts), the bubble formula and the five-line benchmark are those of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(iv) \cite{ChetyrkinTkachov1981}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (The algebra in $d$ dimensions; computed.) The rule $\gamma_{\alpha}\gamma_{\alpha} = d$, $\gamma_{\alpha}Xb\gamma_{\alpha} = -(\gamma_{\alpha}X\gamma_{\alpha})b + 2bX$ ($b$ a vector, $X$ a product of vectors) reproduces $\sum_{\alpha}\gamma_{\alpha}X\gamma^{\alpha}$ in $\Cl(D, 0)$ for $D = 4, \ldots, 8$ and in $\Cl(1, D-1)$ for $D = 4, 5, 6$, and the resulting traces of every word below equal four times the scalar part of the explicit Clifford products in $\Cl(D, 0)$, $D = 4, 5, 6$.
\item (Reduction; computed.) With the denominators $Q(k)$, $Q(k - q)$, $Q(l)$, $Q(l - q)$, $Q(k - l)$, every two-loop integral that occurs is an exact rational function of $d$ times $M_{1} = G(1,1)^{2}$ plus a rational function of $d$ times $M_{2} = G(1,1)G(1, 3 - d/2)$ (integration by parts \cite{ChetyrkinTkachov1981}); on the benchmark with five unit lines this gives $6\zeta_{3} + O(\epsilon)$.
\item (One loop; computed.) $\Pi^{(1)} = -\tfrac{2(d-2)}{d-1}\,a\,(4\pi)^{\epsilon}G(1,1)\,Q(q)^{-\epsilon} = -\tfrac43\tfrac{a}{\epsilon} + \dots$, so $\beta_{0} = \tfrac43$ in $\mu^{2}da/d\mu^{2} = \beta_{0}a^{2} + \beta_{1}a^{3}$; the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ constant is $-\tfrac{20}{9}a$.
\item (Two loops; computed.) Summed over the two self-energy insertions and the vertex correction: the coefficient of $1 - \xi$ vanishes identically in $d$, so the result does not depend on $\xi$ and holds in particular in the Feynman gauge $\xi = 1$, the gauge whose Fock space realises the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form $-u\cdot w$ of (K1), which the store restates as the trace form of Clifford conjugation (\claimref{synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-twistor-adjoint-and-its-trace-form-is-the-one-particle-gupta-bleuler-form}; a restatement, not a derivation of the premise), and $q\cdot\Pi^{(2)}_{q}(q) = 0$ (in components $q_{\mu}q_{\nu}\Pi^{(2)}_{\mu\nu} = 0$) identically in $d$; in the Feynman gauge the self-energy insertions carry $+\tfrac43 a^{2}/\epsilon^{2}$ and the vertex correction $-\tfrac43 a^{2}/\epsilon^{2}$; the sum is $\Pi^{(2)} = a^{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{2}{\epsilon} + 16\zeta_{3} - \tfrac{55}{3} + 4\ln(Q(q)/\mu^{2}) + O(\epsilon)\bigr)$ in $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ normalisation. Hence $Z_{3} = 1 - \tfrac43\tfrac{a}{\epsilon} - 2\tfrac{a^{2}}{\epsilon}$, $\beta_{1} = 4$, and with $n_{f}$ fermions $\mu\,d\alpha/d\mu = \tfrac{2n_{f}}{3\pi}\alpha^{2} + \tfrac{n_{f}}{2\pi^{2}}\alpha^{3}$ \cite{JostLuttinger1950, Steinhauser2002, FanchiottiKniehlSirlin1993} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lsz-reduction-ward-identity-and-the-second-qed-beta-coefficient}(iii)).
\item (Ward identity at two loops; proved for the integrands, argued for the integrals.) In $\Cl(1,3)$ with massive lines and the unit outside the product, $S(k + h) - S(k) = -S(k + h)hS(k)$ makes the sum of the insertions of $h$ into the open fermion line of the rainbow, crossed and polarisation-insertion self-energies equal to minus the difference of the line at $p + h$ and at $p$, and the insertions into a closed loop telescope to the difference of one integrand at loop momenta $l + h$ and $l$; with the shift invariance of dimensional regularisation, $\Lambda^{(2)}(p, p) = -\partial\Sigma^{(2)}/\partial p$ and $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ at two loops \cite{Ward1950} (as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lsz-reduction-ward-identity-and-the-second-qed-beta-coefficient}(ii)).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.two-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-.technical:
Under the Krein-form premise, with the series' vertex and the conventions of one-loop electrodynamics in the spacetime algebra (traces four times the scalar part, the unit outside the product), after the Wick rotation and in dimensional regularisation, the two-loop vacuum polarisation of a massless Dirac fermion is computed exactly in the dimension $d$. The Dirac algebra is continued by one Clifford rule, $\gamma_{\alpha}\gamma_{\alpha} = d$ and $\gamma_{\alpha}Xb\gamma_{\alpha} = -(\gamma_{\alpha}X\gamma_{\alpha})b + 2bX$, which agrees with the explicit Clifford algebras of every integer dimension from four to eight; no $I_{4}$ enters the vector-like loop, so the obstruction recorded for the unit does not arise.

Scalar products are rewritten through the five denominators and every integral is reduced by integration by parts and the Gamma-function bubble (standard rules of dimensional regularisation, imported) to two masters with exact rational coefficients in $d$; the reduction reproduces the known value $6\zeta_{3}$ of the two-loop integral with five unit lines. At one loop the code gives $\beta_{0} = 4/3$ (with $a = \alpha/(4\pi)$). At two loops the dependence on the gauge parameter cancels identically in $d$ (so the Feynman gauge, whose Fock space realises the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form, gives the same result as every covariant gauge), the polarisation is transverse identically in $d$, and the double pole of the self-energy insertions ($+4/3$) cancels that of the vertex correction ($-4/3$), which is the cancellation of the one-loop counterterms by $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$. What is left is a simple pole, $-2a^{2}/\epsilon$, so $\beta_{1} = 4$ per fermion, the standard value of Jost and Luttinger, $\mu\,d\alpha/d\mu = 2\alpha^{2}/(3\pi) + \alpha^{3}/(2\pi^{2})$, and the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ constant $16\zeta_{3} - 55/3$ agrees with the literature. For a single coupling $\beta_{1}$ is the same in every mass-independent scheme, so it does not depend on the choice of dimensional regularisation; of the one-loop Fact only the Wick rotation and the covariant photon are used, not its Pauli-Villars clause.

At the level of integrands the Ward-Takahashi identity holds at two loops in $\Cl(1,3)$ with massive lines: the resolvent identity telescopes the insertions on each open line and on the closed loop, so with the shift invariance of dimensional regularisation $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ at two loops.
synthesis.two-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-.lay: Electrodynamics in the series' algebra of spacetime now goes one step beyond the first quantum corrections. The screening of charge by virtual electron pairs is computed to second order, with the dimension of spacetime treated as a variable so that the infinities appear in a controlled way; the algebra continues to any dimension through one rule, checked in every whole dimension from four to eight. The result has the textbook structure: it does not depend on the arbitrary choice of how the photon is described, it conserves charge, and the nested infinities of its pieces cancel among themselves because of the identity that keeps the electron's charge and its normalisation in step. The strength of the electric force grows with energy at the standard rate, including the standard second-order term. All of this holds under the series' premise that the photon's states carry the standard indefinite measure; the method of taming the infinities is borrowed, not the series' own, but the second-order rate does not depend on which standard method is used.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} After the Wick rotation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(ii)) all momenta are Euclidean, $Q(q) > 0$, and the Dirac algebra is the Clifford algebra of the Euclidean vectors, $\gamma_{\alpha}\gamma_{\beta} + \gamma_{\beta}\gamma_{\alpha} = 2\delta_{\alpha\beta}$. The Feynman rules of \claimref{field-theory.coupled-system-tree-level} give, with the units collected outside the product as in \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra} (the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ acting as the right unit, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$): fermion propagator $-k/Q(k)$ with one unit (numerator the vector $k$), vertex $-e\gamma_{\alpha}$ with one unit, photon $(\delta_{\alpha\beta} - (1-\xi)r_{\alpha}r_{\beta}/Q(r))/Q(r)$ (the covariant form, which needs the Krein-form premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}), and $-1$ per closed fermion loop. Per loop $e^{2}\int d^{d}k/(2\pi)^{d} = a(4\pi)^{\epsilon}\int d^{d}k/\pi^{d/2}$, $a = \alpha/(4\pi)$. The overall factors are $(-1)(-eI_{4})^{2}(-I_{4})^{2} = -e^{2}$ at one loop and $(-1)(-eI_{4})^{4}(-I_{4})^{4} = -e^{4}$ at two loops. The trace of a product of vectors is $4\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(1)); no unit enters a vector-like loop, so the units are coefficients and the unit result's obstruction to continuing $I_{4}$ does not arise. Dimensional regularisation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(i)) supplies the continuation in $d$ with poles at $d = 4$ and its Lorentz and vector-like gauge invariance. The following standard rules are its clause (iv) (\cite{ChetyrkinTkachov1981}; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(iv)): $\int d^{d}\ell/\pi^{d/2}\,Q(\ell)^{r}(Q(\ell) + \Delta)^{-N} = \Gamma(r + d/2)\Gamma(N - r - d/2)\Delta^{d/2 + r - N}/(\Gamma(d/2)\Gamma(N))$; symmetric integration $\ell^{\alpha_{1}}\cdots\ell^{\alpha_{2r}} \to Q(\ell)^{r}\{\delta^{r}\}/(d(d+2)\cdots(d+2r-2))$; translation invariance; the vanishing of scale-free integrals; and $\int d^{d}k\,\partial_{k}\cdot(\cdots) = 0$. The gauge parameter is kept general; since the result does not depend on it, it holds in the Feynman gauge, whose Fock space realises the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form, restated in the store as the trace form of Clifford conjugation (\claimref{synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-twistor-adjoint-and-its-trace-form-is-the-one-particle-gupta-bleuler-form}; a restatement, not a derivation of (K1)).

\emph{Step 1 (the algebra in $d$ dimensions).} For a vector $b$ and a product $X$ of vectors, $b\gamma_{\alpha} = -\gamma_{\alpha}b + 2b_{\alpha}$ gives $\gamma_{\alpha}Xb\gamma_{\alpha} = -(\gamma_{\alpha}X\gamma_{\alpha})b + 2bX$, and $\gamma_{\alpha}\gamma_{\alpha} = d$; by induction on the length of $X$ every contraction $\gamma_{\alpha}X\gamma_{\alpha}$ is a polynomial in $d$ times products of the vectors of $X$. Both rules hold in $\Cl(D, 0)$ and, with the reciprocal frame, in $\Cl(1, D-1)$ for every integer $D$; the check compares them with the explicit sums in $\Cl(D, 0)$, $D = 4, \ldots, 8$, and $\Cl(1, D-1)$, $D = 4, 5, 6$, on words of length up to four (control: $d = 4$ in place of $D = 6$ fails). The trace of a product of vectors follows from $\mathrm{tr}(a_{1}\cdots a_{n}) = \sum_{j \ge 2}(-1)^{j}(a_{1}\cdot a_{j})\,\mathrm{tr}(\cdots\hat a_{1}\cdots\hat a_{j}\cdots)$, $\mathrm{tr}\,1 = 4$, which uses only the anticommutator. The resulting traces are polynomials of degree at most two in $d$; the check compares every word below (Feynman and gauge parts, both projections) with $4\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ of the explicit products summed over a basis in $\Cl(D, 0)$, $D = 4, 5, 6$: agreement at three values of $d$ for a polynomial of degree two in $d$ is an identity in $d$, for the sampled momenta.

\emph{Step 2 (the diagrams).} The fermion loop carries $k$ and $k - q$; the internal photon carries $r = k - l$. With $\Pi_{\mu\nu}^{(2)} = -e^{4}\int\int \frac{d^{d}k\,d^{d}l}{(2\pi)^{2d}}\,\sum_{j}T_{j}$:
\[
T_{\mathrm{se}1} = \frac{\mathrm{tr}[\gamma_{\mu}k\gamma_{\alpha}l\gamma_{\beta}k\gamma_{\nu}(k-q)]P_{\alpha\beta}}{Q(k)^{2}Q(k-q)Q(l)Q(r)},\quad
T_{\mathrm{se}2} = \frac{\mathrm{tr}[\gamma_{\mu}k\gamma_{\nu}(k-q)\gamma_{\alpha}(l-q)\gamma_{\beta}(k-q)]P_{\alpha\beta}}{Q(k)Q(k-q)^{2}Q(l-q)Q(r)},
\]
\[
T_{\mathrm{vx}} = \frac{\mathrm{tr}[\gamma_{\mu}k\gamma_{\alpha}l\gamma_{\nu}(l-q)\gamma_{\beta}(k-q)]P_{\alpha\beta}}{Q(k)Q(k-q)Q(l)Q(l-q)Q(r)},\qquad P_{\alpha\beta} = \delta_{\alpha\beta} - (1-\xi)\frac{r_{\alpha}r_{\beta}}{Q(r)},
\]
the matrix order following the fermion line against its arrow, with momentum conserved at every vertex. The scalar function is $\Pi = \Pi_{\mu\mu}/((d-1)Q(q))$, and transversality is $q_{\mu}q_{\nu}\Pi_{\mu\nu} = 0$. At one loop $\Pi^{(1)}_{\mu\nu} = -e^{2}\int\mathrm{tr}[\gamma_{\mu}k\gamma_{\nu}(k-q)]/(Q(k)Q(k-q))$. By homogeneity $\Pi^{(n)} \propto Q(q)^{-n\epsilon}$, so one may set $Q(q) = 1$.

\emph{Step 3 (reduction).} With $D_{1} = Q(k)$, $D_{2} = Q(k-q)$, $D_{3} = Q(l)$, $D_{4} = Q(l-q)$, $D_{5} = Q(k-l)$ and $Q(q) = 1$: $k\cdot q = (D_{1} - D_{2} + 1)/2$, $l\cdot q = (D_{3} - D_{4} + 1)/2$, $k\cdot l = (D_{1} + D_{3} - D_{5})/2$, so every numerator is a polynomial in the $D_{i}$ and every term an integral $I(a_{1}, \ldots, a_{5}) = \int\int\prod D_{i}^{-a_{i}}$ (measure $d^{d}k\,d^{d}l/\pi^{d}$) with integer $a_{i}$. (a) $a_{5} \le 0$: expand $D_{5}^{n} = (D_{1} + D_{3} - 2k\cdot l)^{n}$; the $k$ integral of $(k\cdot l)^{j}$ over $D_{1}^{-A}D_{2}^{-B}$ is, by Feynman parameters and the integrals of the Conventions paragraph,
\[
\sum_{r}\binom{j}{2r}\frac{(2r-1)!!}{2^{r}}\,Q(l)^{r}(l\cdot q)^{j-2r}\,\frac{\Gamma(A + B - r - \tfrac d2)\Gamma(j - r + \tfrac d2 - A)\Gamma(r + \tfrac d2 - B)}{\Gamma(A)\Gamma(B)\Gamma(j + d - A - B)},
\]
zero if $A \le 0$ or $B \le 0$ (scale-free), and the $l$ integral is a bubble. (b) $a_{1} \le 0$ (or $a_{2} \le 0$; or, by $k \leftrightarrow l$, $a_{3}$ or $a_{4} \le 0$): shift $k = k' + q$ (or not), expand the numerator in $Q(k')$ and $k'\cdot q$, use the same formula with external momentum $P = l - q$ (or $l$), which leaves $Q(P)^{d/2 + r - A - B}$, and the $l$ integral is a bubble with one non-integer index. (c) All $a_{i} > 0$: integration by parts with $\partial_{k}\cdot(k - l)$ gives the triangle rule
\[
(d - a_{1} - a_{2} - 2a_{5})\,I = a_{1}\mathbf{1}^{+}(\mathbf{5}^{-} - \mathbf{3}^{-})I + a_{2}\mathbf{2}^{+}(\mathbf{5}^{-} - \mathbf{4}^{-})I,
\]
since $2k\cdot(k - l) = D_{1} + D_{5} - D_{3}$, $2(k - q)\cdot(k - l) = D_{2} + D_{5} - D_{4}$; each step lowers $a_{3} + a_{4} + a_{5}$ by one, so the recursion ends in (a) or (b). The bubble (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(iv)) is $G(\alpha, \beta) = \Gamma(\alpha + \beta - \tfrac d2)\Gamma(\tfrac d2 - \alpha)\Gamma(\tfrac d2 - \beta)/(\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)\Gamma(d - \alpha - \beta))$ \cite{ChetyrkinTkachov1981}. In (a) the Gamma functions have arguments $n \pm d/2$ and $n + d$ in the same numbers as in $M_{1} = G(1,1)^{2}$; in (b) as in $M_{2} = G(1,1)G(1, 3 - d/2)$ (arguments $n - d$ and $n + 3d/2$ once each); integer shifts of an argument $z$ give rational factors by $\Gamma(z + 1) = z\Gamma(z)$, so every $I$ is $R_{1}(d)M_{1} + R_{2}(d)M_{2}$ with $R_{1}, R_{2}$ rational. Benchmarks (checked): $I(1,1,1,1,0) = M_{1}$; $I(1,1,1,1,-1) = -\tfrac12M_{1}$ (from $\int k^{\mu}/(D_{1}D_{2}) = \tfrac12q^{\mu}G(1,1)$); $I(0,1,1,1,1) = M_{2}$; and $I(1,1,1,1,1) = 2(3 - d)M_{1}/(d - 4) + R_{2}M_{2} = 6\zeta_{3} + O(\epsilon)$.

\emph{Step 4 (expansion).} $G(1,1) = g(\epsilon)/\epsilon$ with $g = \Gamma(1+\epsilon)\Gamma(1-\epsilon)^{2}/((1-2\epsilon)\Gamma(1-2\epsilon))$, and
\[
\frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}} = \frac{G(1, 1+\epsilon)}{G(1,1)} = \frac{(1 - 2\epsilon)\,\Gamma(1+2\epsilon)\Gamma(1-2\epsilon)^{2}}{2(1 - 3\epsilon)\,\Gamma(1+\epsilon)^{2}\Gamma(1-\epsilon)\Gamma(1-3\epsilon)} = \frac{1 - 2\epsilon}{2(1 - 3\epsilon)}\exp\Bigl(-6\zeta_{3}\epsilon^{3} - 9\zeta_{4}\epsilon^{4} + \cdots\Bigr)
\]
by $\ln\Gamma(1 + z) = -\gamma z + \sum_{n \ge 2}(-1)^{n}\zeta_{n}z^{n}/n$ \cite{AbramowitzStegun1964}: the coefficients of $\gamma$ and $\zeta_{2}$ are $2 - 4 - 2 + 1 + 3 = 0$ and $\tfrac12(4 + 8 - 2 - 1 - 9) = 0$. The rational functions are expanded exactly at $d = 4 - 2\epsilon$. The $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ normalisation replaces $(4\pi)^{\epsilon}$ per loop by $e^{\gamma\epsilon}$, and $e^{\gamma\epsilon}g = 1 + 2\epsilon + O(\epsilon^{2})$.

\emph{Step 5 (one loop).} $\mathrm{tr}[\gamma_{\mu}k\gamma_{\mu}(k - q)] = 4(2 - d)\,k\cdot(k - q)$ and $k\cdot(k - q) = (D_{1} + D_{2} - 1)/2$, whose first two terms are scale free; so $\Pi^{(1)} = -\tfrac{2(d-2)}{d-1}a(4\pi)^{\epsilon}G(1,1)Q(q)^{-\epsilon} = a(4\pi)^{\epsilon}Q(q)^{-\epsilon}\,\tfrac{g(\epsilon)}{\epsilon}\bigl(-\tfrac43 + \tfrac49\epsilon + O(\epsilon^{2})\bigr)$; the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ constant is $\tfrac49 + 2(-\tfrac43) = -\tfrac{20}{9}$. With $e^{2}_{\mathrm{eff}}(q) = e_{0}^{2}/(1 - \Pi(Q(q)))$ (the Euclidean propagator $\sum_{n}Q(q)^{-1}\Pi^{n}$), $1/a_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/a_{0} - \Pi^{(1)}/a_{0} - \Pi^{(2)}/a_{0} + \cdots$, and $d(1/a_{\mathrm{eff}})/d\ln Q(q) = -\beta_{0} - \beta_{1}a$: the one-loop term gives $\beta_{0} = \tfrac43$, screening.

\emph{Step 6 (two loops).} The check computes the three traces (Step 1), reduces them (Step 3) and expands (Step 4). Results, exact in $d$: the coefficient of $(1 - \xi)$, summed over the three diagrams, is zero as a rational function of $d$ in both masters (it is not zero for the vertex diagram alone); $q_{\mu}q_{\nu}\Pi^{(2)}_{\mu\nu}$ is zero in both masters, in the Feynman part and the gauge part. With $\Pi^{(2)} = a^{2}(4\pi)^{2\epsilon}Q(q)^{-2\epsilon}(R_{1}M_{1} + R_{2}M_{2})$, the series $R_{1} + R_{2}M_{2}/M_{1}$ begins at $\epsilon^{1}$ with $-2\epsilon + (16\zeta_{3} - \tfrac{31}{3})\epsilon^{2}$: there is no pole of order three or two, $\Pi^{(2)} = a^{2}(-2/\epsilon + \cdots)$, and the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ constant is $16\zeta_{3} - \tfrac{31}{3} + 4(-2) = 16\zeta_{3} - \tfrac{55}{3}$. In the Feynman gauge the two self-energy insertions together give $+\tfrac43a^{2}/\epsilon^{2}$ and the vertex correction $-\tfrac43a^{2}/\epsilon^{2}$: the one-loop subdivergences, removed by the counterterms $Z_{2} - 1$ on the self-energy subgraphs and $Z_{1} - 1$ on the vertex subgraphs, cancel in the sum because $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ at one loop (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(4)), and the bare sum needs only the overall counterterm. In $1/a_{\mathrm{eff}}$ the term $-\Pi^{(2)}/a_{0} = -a(-2/\epsilon)Q(q)^{-2\epsilon} + \cdots$ has $\ln Q(q)$ coefficient $-4a$, so $\beta_{1} = 4$ and $Z_{3} = 1 - \tfrac43 a/\epsilon - 2a^{2}/\epsilon$; with $n_{f}$ fermions each diagram has one closed loop and both coefficients scale with $n_{f}$. In $\alpha$: $\mu\,d\alpha/d\mu = 2(4\pi)[\beta_{0}(\alpha/4\pi)^{2} + \beta_{1}(\alpha/4\pi)^{3}] = \tfrac{2}{3\pi}\alpha^{2} + \tfrac{1}{2\pi^{2}}\alpha^{3}$. Comparison (computed values against the literature, read 2026-11-02): Steinhauser's $Z_{3}$ at order $\alpha\alpha_{s}$ with $C_{F} \to 1$, $\alpha_{s} \to \alpha$ is $1 - (\alpha/\pi)/(3\epsilon) - (\alpha/\pi)^{2}/(8\epsilon) = 1 - \tfrac43a/\epsilon - 2a^{2}/\epsilon$ \cite{Steinhauser2002}; the constant $f_{2} = \tfrac{55}{12} - 4\zeta_{3}$ of \cite{FanchiottiKniehlSirlin1993}, with the one-loop $f_{1} = \tfrac53$ and the relative factor $\tfrac34\alpha/\pi = 3a$, gives $-\tfrac43a\cdot 3a\,(\tfrac{55}{12} - 4\zeta_{3}) = a^{2}(16\zeta_{3} - \tfrac{55}{3})$, as computed. The coefficient $\beta_{1}$ is that of \cite{JostLuttinger1950} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lsz-reduction-ward-identity-and-the-second-qed-beta-coefficient}(iii)).

\emph{Step 7 (Ward identity at two loops).} In $\Cl(1,3)$, $S(k) = (k - m)^{-1} = (k + m)/(Q(k) - m^{2})$ with the units of the Feynman rules outside the product, as the right unit $I_{4}$ (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(5)), and $S(k + h) - S(k) = S(k+h)[(k - m) - (k + h - m)]S(k) = -S(k + h)hS(k)$. For an open line $C(p) = V_{0}S(p_{1})V_{1}\cdots S(p_{n})V_{n}$ (the momenta $p_{j}$ differ from $p$ by loop momenta), let $T_{j}$ be the line with $p_{1}, \ldots, p_{j-1}$ shifted by $h$ and the rest not; the insertion of the vertex $h$ at line $j$ is $T$ with $S(p_{j})$ replaced by $S(p_{j} + h)hS(p_{j}) = -(S(p_{j} + h) - S(p_{j}))$, which is $-(T_{j+1} - T_{j})$, so the sum over $j$ is $-(C(p + h) - C(p))$. The two-loop self-energies have open lines of three propagators (rainbow, crossed) and one propagator (the line of the polarisation insertion), and the closed loop of the insertion telescopes in the same way to the difference of one integrand at loop momenta $l + h$ and $l$, which integrates to zero by translation invariance. Hence $h_{\mu}\Lambda^{(2)\mu}(p + h, p) = -(\Sigma^{(2)}(p + h) - \Sigma^{(2)}(p))$; to first order in $h$, $\frac{d}{dt}S(k + th)|_{0} = h/(Q(k) - m^{2}) - 2(k\cdot h)(k + m)/(Q(k) - m^{2})^{2} = -S(k)hS(k)$, so $\Lambda^{(2)\mu}(p, p) = -\partial\Sigma^{(2)}/\partial p_{\mu}$, and on shell $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ at two loops \cite{Ward1950}. The check verifies the three open-line identities, the closed-loop identity and the derivative identity exactly at rational momenta with $m = \tfrac32$, with two controls (the sum without the middle insertion, and $\gamma_{0}$ in place of $h$, both fail). Proved for the integrands; the passage to the regulated integrals uses the shift invariance of dimensional regularisation, and the vertex and self-energy diagrams are the standard ones (argued).

\emph{Status of the clauses.} (1) to (4) are exact computations given the imported rules of dimensional regularisation and the Gamma-function expansion (computed); (5) is proved for the integrands and argued for the integrals. Transport-absent; the spacetime algebra is convenient (the continuation in $d$ is one Clifford rule checked in every integer dimension from four to eight). The regulator is imported, not native.

synthesis.two-species-floor-pairing-has-.formal:
Let a floor carry $n_{b} \ge 1$ blocks, block $b$ holding three tower planes with null pairs $v_{i}(b) = \tfrac12(e_{i,b} + f_{i,b})$, $w_{i}(b) = \tfrac12(e_{i,b} - f_{i,b})$, $Q(e_{i,b}) = 1$, $Q(f_{i,b}) = -1$, $i = 1, 2, 3$; they obey the CAR with $v$ creating (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) and $v^{*} = w$; $\Omega_{0}$ is the vector annihilated by every $w_{i}(b)$. Modes $1, 2$ form a doublet $\psi$, mode $3$ a singlet $\chi$. Write $N_{i} = \sum_{b}v_{i}w_{i}$, $N_{\psi} = N_{1} + N_{2}$, $N_{\chi} = N_{3}$, $N = N_{\psi} + N_{\chi}$, $E_{ij} = \sum_{b}v_{i}(b)w_{j}(b)$, isospin $t_{+} = E_{12}$, $t_{-} = E_{21}$, $t_{3} = \tfrac12(N_{1} - N_{2})$ with Casimir $C_{I} = t_{3}^{2} + \tfrac12(t_{+}t_{-} + t_{-}t_{+})$, and $\Gamma$ the fermion parity. Let
\[
S = \sum_{b}w_{1}(b)w_{2}(b),\quad B_{\alpha} = \sum_{b}w_{\alpha}(b)w_{3}(b),\quad H = K_{\psi}N_{\psi} + K_{\chi}N_{\chi} - G_{S}S^{*}S - G_{D}\sum_{\alpha = 1,2}B_{\alpha}^{*}B_{\alpha},
\]
with real $K_{\psi}, K_{\chi}$ and $G_{S}, G_{D} \ge 0$ (on modes $1, 2$ alone, $H$ is the stored pairing element of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2)); the doublet quanta $Z_{2}^{*} = \sum_{b}w_{1}(b)v_{3}(b)$, $Z_{1}^{*} = \sum_{b}v_{3}(b)w_{2}(b)$; the pair sum $W = S^{*}S + \sum_{\alpha}B_{\alpha}^{*}B_{\alpha}$; and $x(n_{S}, n_{1}, n_{2}) = (S^{*})^{n_{S}}(B_{1}^{*})^{n_{1}}(B_{2}^{*})^{n_{2}}\Omega_{0}$, with $n = n_{1} + n_{2}$ and $P = n_{S} + n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charges and parity.)} $H$ commutes with $N_{1}$, $N_{2}$, $N_{3}$, $t_{\pm}$ and $\Gamma$. $S$, $B_{\alpha}$ and $Z_{\alpha}$ are even; $[t_{-}, B_{1}^{*}] = B_{2}^{*}$, $[t_{+}, Z_{2}^{*}] = Z_{1}^{*}$, $[t_{+}, B_{1}^{*}] = [t_{+}, Z_{1}^{*}] = [t_{\pm}, S^{*}] = 0$, so $(B_{1}^{*}, B_{2}^{*})$ and $(Z_{1}^{*}, Z_{2}^{*})$ are isospin doublets and $S$ a singlet; $Z_{\alpha}^{*}$ raises $N_{\chi}$ by one and lowers $N_{\psi}$ by one, and $[Z_{\alpha}^{*}, S^{*}] = B_{\alpha}^{*}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The band.)} In one block any two of the pair creators $v_{2}v_{1}$, $v_{3}v_{1}$, $v_{3}v_{2}$ multiply to zero. $x(n_{S}, n_{1}, n_{2}) \neq 0$ exactly when $P \le n_{b}$, and then $Hx = E(n_{S}, n)x$ with
\[
E(n_{S}, n) = K_{\psi}(2n_{S} + n) + K_{\chi}n - (G_{S}n_{S} + G_{D}n)(n_{b} - P + 1);
\]
at fixed $n_{S}$ and $n$ the $n + 1$ vectors span isospin $n/2$ ($C_{I} = \tfrac{n}{2}(\tfrac{n}{2} + 1)$).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Doublet quanta.)} $Z_{2}^{*}x(P - n, 0, n) = (P - n)\,x(P - n - 1, 0, n + 1)$, $[Z_{2}, Z_{2}^{*}] = N_{1} - N_{3}$, which is $P - 2n$ on $x(P - n, 0, n)$, and $E(P - n, n) = E(P, 0) + n\,\omega_{D}$ with
\[
\omega_{D} = (K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + (G_{S} - G_{D})(n_{b} - P + 1),
\]
exactly harmonic at fixed $P$. With $J$ the kernel bivector of a tower level containing these planes, $\phi = Z_{2} + Z_{2}^{*}$ and $\pi = J(Z_{2}^{*} - Z_{2})$ are self-adjoint and $[\phi, \pi] = 2J(N_{1} - N_{3})$, equal to $2(P - 2n)J$ on the ladder.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Two phases of the band.)} At fixed $P$ the band energy is affine in $n$ with slope $\omega_{D}$, so the two condensates coexist on the band only at $\omega_{D} = 0$. For $\omega_{D} > 0$ the lowest band vector is the singlet band $x(P, 0, 0)$ and each doublet quantum costs $\omega_{D}$. For $\omega_{D} < 0$ it is the doublet band ($n = P$), whose isospin-$P/2$ multiplet is exactly degenerate; $B_{1}^{*}$ and $B_{2}^{*}$ take it to the doublet band of $P + 1$ pairs, both at energy $E(0, P + 1)$; on the band, its excitations at fixed $P$ are return quanta $Z_{2}$, each at $-\omega_{D}$, each carrying two units of $N_{\psi} - N_{\chi}$, a charge the doublet condensate leaves unbroken. In the stretched sector $(N_{1}, N_{2}, N_{3}) = (0, P, P)$, $0 < P < n_{b}$, which holds exactly the levels of isospin $P/2$ at $N_{\psi} = N_{\chi} = P$, the next level lies exactly $G_{D}n_{b}$ above the doublet band, with none between: no level of the condensate's own isospin lies below pair breaking.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Threshold and binding.)} In the one-quantum sector $V_{P} = \{(N_{1}, N_{2}, N_{3}) = (P - 1, P, 1)\}$, $1 \le P \le n_{b}$, the lowest level at $G_{D} = 0$ is $E_{\mathrm{th}} = K_{\psi}(2P - 1) + K_{\chi} - G_{S}(P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1)$ (a free $\chi$ beside $P - 1$ singlet pairs and an unpaired $\psi_{2}$); the collective level $E_{D} = E(P - 1, 1)$ satisfies $E_{D} = E_{\mathrm{th}} - G_{D}(n_{b} - P + 1)$, $E_{D} - E(P, 0) = \omega_{D}$ and $E_{\mathrm{th}} - E(P, 0) = (K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + G_{S}(n_{b} - P + 1)$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Casimir identity.)} With $C_{3} = \sum_{i,j}E_{ij}E_{ji}$ and $C_{O} = \sum_{b < c}L_{bc}^{*}L_{bc}$, $L_{bc} = \sum_{i}(v_{i}(b)w_{i}(c) - v_{i}(c)w_{i}(b))$: $2W = N(n_{b} + 2) - C_{3} - C_{O}$, and $C_{O} \ge 0$.
\item[(vii)] \emph{(Reduction.)} Let $G_{S} \ge G_{D} \ge 0$ and let $X \ge X_{2}$ be the two largest eigenvalues of $W$ on $V_{P}$, counted with multiplicity. Every level of $H$ on $V_{P}$ is at least $E_{D} - G_{D}(X - P(n_{b} - P + 1))$, and every level but the lowest is at least $E_{\mathrm{th}} - G_{D}(X_{2} - (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1))$.
\item[(viii)] \emph{(Computed.)} For $n_{b} \le 6$ and every $P$: $X = (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1) + \max(n_{b} - P + 1, 3)$ for $P \ge 2$, $X = n_{b}$ for $P = 1$; and when $n_{b} - P + 1 > 3$ or $P = 1$, $X = P(n_{b} - P + 1)$ is simple and $X_{2} = (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1) + 3$ ($X_{2} = 0$ for $P = 1$). Hence, for $n_{b} \le 6$ and $G_{S} \ge G_{D} \ge 0$: if $n_{b} - P + 1 \ge 3$ the lowest level of $V_{P}$ is $E_{D}$, so the doublet gap at $N = 2P$, the gap between sector minima (lowest level with $N_{\chi} = 1$ less lowest level with $N_{\chi} = 0$, which is $E(P, 0)$), is exactly $\omega_{D}$; if $n_{b} - P + 1 > 3$ every other level lies at or above $E_{\mathrm{th}} - 3G_{D}$, so $E_{D}$ is split off by at least $G_{D}(n_{b} - P - 2)$; if $n_{b} - P + 1 < 3$ no level lies below $E_{D} - (P + 2 - n_{b})G_{D}$, and at $P = n_{b}$ that value is a level (a block holding all three modes). The formulas for $X$ and $X_{2}$ are conjectured for every $n_{b}$.
\item[(ix)] \emph{(The infinite floor.)} With $G_{S} = g_{S}/n_{b}$ and $G_{D} = g_{D}/n_{b}$, exactly $\omega_{D} = (K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + (g_{S} - g_{D})(1 - P/n_{b} + 1/n_{b})$, so at $P/n_{b} = f$ it differs from its limit $(K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + (g_{S} - g_{D})(1 - f)$ by exactly $(g_{S} - g_{D})/n_{b}$; the binding is $g_{D}(1 - f + 1/n_{b})$; and $\Phi = \phi/\sqrt{2P}$, $\Pi = \pi/\sqrt{2P}$ satisfy $[\Phi, \Pi] = (1 - 2n/P)J$ on the ladder. Under the conjecture in (viii), for $P \le n_{b} - 2$ the doublet gap is $\omega_{D}$ with no error, and for $P \le n_{b} - 3$ the rest of $V_{P}$ lies at or above $E_{\mathrm{th}} - 3g_{D}/n_{b}$.
\item[(x)] \emph{(Off the band, computed.)} The band need not hold the ground state at fixed $N$. At $K_{\psi} = K_{\chi} = 0$, $G_{S} = 1$ and $(n_{b}, P, G_{D}) = (5, 3, \tfrac12), (6, 3, \tfrac45), (7, 3, \tfrac{9}{10})$, where $\omega_{D} > 0$ and $n_{b} - P + 1 \ge 3$, the sector $(2, 2, 2)$ (two $\chi$ particles) has a level below the singlet band $E(P, 0)$, which is the lowest level with $N_{\chi} = 0$: so the gap of (viii) is a gap between sector minima, and an excitation gap of the ground state only where the singlet band is the ground state at $N = 2P$. At $K = 0$, $G_{S} = 1$, $G_{D} = 3$ ($\omega_{D} < 0$) and $(n_{b}, P) = (4, 2), (5, 2)$, the stretched sector has one level below the pair-breaking threshold $E(0, P) + G_{D}n_{b}$ while the sector $(1, P - 1, P)$, at the same $N_{\psi}$ and $N_{\chi}$, has $n_{b}^{2}$ ($16$, $25$), all but one of isospin below $P/2$, and none below the doublet band.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (i) to (vii) and (ix) without its last sentence are proved for every $n_{b}$; (viii) is proved by exact computation for $n_{b} \le 6$ and conjectured beyond; (x) is computed exactly at the couplings listed. \emph{Reading (argued).} The doublet quantum is the doublet-singlet composite of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower-and-its-modes-carry-no-even-doublet} (step 5), realised exactly: an even, helicity-unmodelled scalar doublet, bound below the pair-breaking threshold for every $G_{D} > 0$; where the singlet band is the ground state, isospin is unbroken and the doublet is a massive composite; it is a pseudo-Goldstone doublet of the point $G_{S} = G_{D}$, $K_{\chi} = K_{\psi}$, where the $Z_{\alpha}$ are symmetry generators and the gap closes, and it is light only near $\omega_{D} = 0$ (at $K_{\chi} = K_{\psi}$, $G_{D}$ near $G_{S}$; then $\omega_{D}/(E_{\mathrm{th}} - E(P, 0)) = 1 - G_{D}/G_{S}$). Once the band's doublet condenses, the band gives an exactly degenerate isospin multiplet and no level of the condensate's isospin below the pair-breaking threshold. So on the band no gapped doublet neutral under the unbroken $N_{\psi} - N_{\chi}$ accompanies a doublet condensate; the return quanta are gapped doublets charged under it. Off the band the ground state at fixed $N$ can change (clause (x)), so these statements concern the band. Being even in the tower the quantum is not the rung field, which is odd.
synthesis.two-species-floor-pairing-has-.technical:
Put three tower modes in every block of a floor: a doublet $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}$ and a singlet $\chi$. Two pair channels act: the singlet pair $\psi_{1}\psi_{2}$ with coupling $G_{S}$ and the doublet pairs $\psi_{\alpha}\chi$ with coupling $G_{D}$. Because any two pairs in one block share a mode, a block holds at most one pair, of one of three kinds, and on the block-symmetric even states the model is a three-kind version of the one-shell pairing band: the energy is $K_{\psi}(2n_{S} + n) + K_{\chi}n - (G_{S}n_{S} + G_{D}n)(n_{b} - P + 1)$, with $n_{S}$ singlet pairs, $n$ doublet pairs (isospin $n/2$) and $P$ pairs in all.

The operator $Z_{2}^{*} = \sum_{b}w_{1}v_{3}$ turns a singlet pair into a doublet pair. On the singlet band it creates a harmonic ladder of doublet quanta of energy $\omega_{D} = (K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + (G_{S} - G_{D})(n_{b} - P + 1)$ each, with $[Z_{2}, Z_{2}^{*}] = N_{1} - N_{\chi}$ ($P - 2n$ on the ladder), so with the kernel unit $J$ the Hermitian fields are canonical up to the defect $2n/P$. The quantum is even, an isospin doublet, and moves one unit from $\psi$ to $\chi$. On the band, if $\omega_{D} > 0$ the doublet is gapped and does not condense; if $\omega_{D} < 0$ the doublet band is lower, its isospin multiplet is exactly degenerate, both components add pairs alike, and in its own sector the next level is the pair-breaking one at $G_{D}n_{b}$. The band need not be the ground state at fixed $N$: computed exactly, a level with two $\chi$ lies below the singlet band at $P = 3$ for $n_{b} = 5, 6, 7$ although $\omega_{D} > 0$, so the doublet gap is one between sector minima; and with a doublet condensate, levels of lower isospin at the condensate's numbers lie below the pair-breaking threshold.

In the sector of one doublet quantum the collective level lies $G_{D}(n_{b} - P + 1)$ below the energy of a free $\chi$ beside a broken pair. Writing $H$ as a constant minus $(G_{S} - G_{D})S^{*}S$ minus $G_{D}W$, with $W$ the equal-coupling pair sum, bounds the whole sector by the two largest eigenvalues of $W$, and $2W = N(n_{b} + 2) - C_{3} - C_{O}$ (flavour and block-rotation Casimirs). Computed exactly for up to six blocks: below $n_{b} - 2$ pairs the collective level is the lowest and every other level is within $3G_{D}$ of the threshold or above; with more pairs a block holding all three modes lies lower by at most $2G_{D}$. With couplings $g/n_{b}$ the gap tends to $(K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + (g_{S} - g_{D})(1 - f)$ with error $(g_{S} - g_{D})/n_{b}$.
synthesis.two-species-floor-pairing-has-.lay: The series has asked whether the Higgs particle could be made of other particles bound together, the way a Cooper pair is made of two electrons. A single kind of particle on one energy shell was already known not to work. This result builds the simplest two-kind model on the series' tower: one kind comes in two versions (a doublet, like the Higgs's charges), the other in one version. Pairs can form in two ways; the model's symmetric band can be solved exactly, and the rest is computed for up to six blocks. One kind of pair can turn into the other, and that change behaves like a particle with the Higgs doublet's charges. On the band it costs energy, so it has a mass, only while the doublet pairs themselves do not take over. The mass shrinks to zero as the two pairing strengths become equal and the two kinds have the same energy. Once the doublet pairs do take over the band, the doublet's directions cost nothing and no extra bound state of the condensate's own isospin appears below the energy needed to break a pair. The band is not always the lowest-energy arrangement, though: for some strengths other arrangements lie lower. Read on the band (an interpretation, not a proof), the model gives either a massive composite doublet or a condensed one, not a condensed doublet together with a light neutral bound scalar of the Higgs kind.

proofs.main:
\begin{proof}
\emph{Setting.} The tower planes generate the CAR with $v$ creating and $w$ annihilating (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}): $\{w_{i}(b), v_{j}(c)\} = \delta_{ij}\delta_{bc}$, all other anticommutators zero. Every operator below is a sum of products of an even number of mode operators except where said, so it commutes with the parity $\Gamma$, which anticommutes with each $v$ and $w$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kernel-bivector-is-the-unit-of-hermitian-boson-fields-on-the-tower}(iv)). Commutators of bilinears follow from $[AB, CD] = A\{B, C\}D - AC\{B, D\} + \{A, C\}DB - C\{A, D\}B$ for mode operators $A, B, C, D$. The check realises one block in the Clifford algebra of three tower planes and a kernel plane with GA's product, and the floors in GA's exterior model of the CAR (creation by wedge, annihilation by contraction), as in the stored pairing checks.

\emph{(i).} $S^{*}S$ and $B_{\alpha}^{*}B_{\alpha}$ move a pair between blocks, so they conserve each $N_{i}$. With the identity above, $[t_{-}, B_{1}^{*}] = \sum_{b}[v_{2}w_{1}, v_{3}v_{1}] = -v_{2}v_{3}$ summed, which is $B_{2}^{*}$; $[t_{+}, Z_{2}^{*}] = \sum_{b}[v_{1}w_{2}, w_{1}v_{3}] = \sum_{b}v_{3}w_{2} = Z_{1}^{*}$; $[t_{+}, B_{1}^{*}] = 0$ and $[t_{+}, Z_{1}^{*}] = 0$ (no matching pair of indices), and $[t_{\pm}, S^{*}] = 0$ because $t_{\pm}$ exchanges modes $1$ and $2$ inside $v_{2}v_{1}$, which is antisymmetric in them. With $[t_{3}, \cdot\,]$ giving $\pm\tfrac12$ on these, $(B_{1}^{*}, B_{2}^{*})$ and $(Z_{1}^{*}, Z_{2}^{*})$ are doublets and $S$ is a singlet, so $\sum_{\alpha}B_{\alpha}^{*}B_{\alpha}$ and $S^{*}S$ commute with $t_{\pm}$, and so does $H$ (the check confirms $[H, t_{\pm}] = 0$ on every Fock vector of the floors $n_{b} = 1, 2$ at four couplings). $[Z_{2}^{*}, S^{*}] = \sum_{b}[w_{1}v_{3}, v_{2}v_{1}] = \sum_{b}v_{3}v_{2} = B_{2}^{*}$ and $[Z_{1}^{*}, S^{*}] = \sum_{b}v_{3}v_{1} = B_{1}^{*}$; $Z_{\alpha}^{*}$ contains one $v_{3}$ and one $w$ of mode $1$ or $2$, hence the charges.

\emph{(ii).} Two distinct pairs of $\{1, 2, 3\}$ share a mode, so a product of two pair creators of one block contains a $v_{i}(b)$ twice and vanishes (checked in the Clifford algebra). The even vectors of one block are therefore $\Omega_{0}$ and the three pair vectors $\pi_{ij}^{*}\Omega_{0}$, $\pi_{12}^{*} = v_{2}v_{1}$, $\pi_{13}^{*} = v_{3}v_{1}$, $\pi_{23}^{*} = v_{3}v_{2}$, and on this four-dimensional space $\pi_{ij}^{*}$ maps $\Omega_{0}$ to the pair vector and annihilates the others, while $\pi_{ij} = (\pi_{ij}^{*})^{*}$ maps the pair vector back. Even operators of different blocks commute, so the even vectors of the floor form the tensor product of $n_{b}$ copies of this space, and the totals $S^{*} = \sum_{b}\pi_{12}^{*}$, $B_{1}^{*} = \sum_{b}\pi_{13}^{*}$, $B_{2}^{*} = \sum_{b}\pi_{23}^{*}$ act on its symmetric part as $a_{ij}^{\dagger}a_{0}$ in the standard boson description of a symmetric tensor power (bosons $a_{0}$ for an empty block and $a_{ij}$ for a block holding the pair $ij$, $n_{0} + \sum n_{ij} = n_{b}$). Hence $x(n_{S}, n_{1}, n_{2})$ is a nonzero multiple of the symmetric vector with $n_{12} = n_{S}$, $n_{13} = n_{1}$, $n_{23} = n_{2}$, $n_{0} = n_{b} - P$ when $P \le n_{b}$, and vanishes when $P > n_{b}$; and $\pi^{*}\pi$ for one kind acts as $a_{ij}^{\dagger}a_{0}a_{0}^{\dagger}a_{ij} = n_{ij}(n_{0} + 1) = n_{ij}(n_{b} - P + 1)$. The kinetic terms count $N_{\psi} = 2n_{S} + n$ and $N_{\chi} = n$, which gives $E(n_{S}, n)$. This is the stored one-shell band of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2) (pairs of one kind, $n_{ij}(n_{b} - n_{ij} + 1)$) with three kinds sharing the empty blocks. At fixed $n_{S}$ and $n$, $S^{*}$ commutes with $t_{\pm}$ and the $B_{\alpha}^{*}$ commute with each other and form a doublet, so the span of the $x(n_{S}, n_{1}, n - n_{1})$ is a nonzero image of the symmetric power of a doublet, which is irreducible of isospin $n/2$ and has dimension $n + 1$; the vectors are nonzero for each $n_{1}$, so the span is that irreducible module. The check verifies $Hx = E(n_{S}, n)x$ and $C_{I}x = \tfrac{n}{2}(\tfrac{n}{2} + 1)x$ exactly for every $(n_{S}, n_{1}, n_{2})$ with $P \le n_{b}$, $n_{b} = 1, \ldots, 4$, at four couplings, and that $x$ vanishes for $P = n_{b} + 1$.

\emph{(iii).} $Z_{2}^{*}\Omega_{0} = 0$; $[Z_{2}^{*}, S^{*}] = B_{2}^{*}$ by (i); $[B_{2}^{*}, S^{*}] = 0$; and $[Z_{2}^{*}, B_{2}^{*}] = \sum_{b}[w_{1}v_{3}, v_{3}v_{2}] = 0$ (each term contains $v_{3}(b)$ twice or no contraction). So $Z_{2}^{*}(S^{*})^{m}(B_{2}^{*})^{n}\Omega_{0} = m(S^{*})^{m - 1}(B_{2}^{*})^{n + 1}\Omega_{0}$, which is the ladder relation with $m = P - n$. Per block, $[w_{3}v_{1}, w_{1}v_{3}] = v_{1}w_{1}w_{3}v_{3} - v_{3}w_{3}w_{1}v_{1} = n_{1}(1 - n_{3}) - n_{3}(1 - n_{1}) = n_{1} - n_{3}$, so $[Z_{2}, Z_{2}^{*}] = N_{1} - N_{3}$, and on $x(P - n, 0, n)$, $N_{1} = P - n$, $N_{3} = n$. From (ii), $E(P - n, n) - E(P, 0) = n(K_{\chi} - K_{\psi}) + n(G_{S} - G_{D})(n_{b} - P + 1) = n\omega_{D}$. In a tower level whose planes include these, the kernel bivector $J$ commutes with every plane generator and $J^{*} = -J$, and for any $X$ in the plane algebra $\phi_{X} = X + X^{*}$, $\pi_{X} = J(X^{*} - X)$ are self-adjoint with $[\phi_{X}, \pi_{X}] = 2J[X, X^{*}]$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kernel-bivector-is-the-unit-of-hermitian-boson-fields-on-the-tower}(ii), (v)); with $X = Z_{2}$ this is $2J(N_{1} - N_{3})$. The defect $2n/P$ is that of the stored collective pair of the quasi-spin (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}): here the quasi-spin is the transfer between two kinds of pair, which is exact on the band. The check verifies the ladder relation, the commutator on the ladder, the harmonic energies at four couplings for $n_{b} \le 4$ and every $P$, the charges of $Z_{2}^{*}x$, $[t_{+}, Z_{2}^{*}]x = Z_{1}^{*}x$, and the operator identity $[Z_{2}, Z_{2}^{*}] = N_{1} - N_{3}$ on every Fock vector of $n_{b} = 1, 2$.

\emph{(iv).} At fixed $P$, $E(P - n, n) = E(P, 0) + n\omega_{D}$ for $0 \le n \le P$ is affine, so its minimum over the band is at $n = 0$ for $\omega_{D} > 0$, at $n = P$ for $\omega_{D} < 0$, and no interior $n$ is strictly lowest; at $\omega_{D} = 0$ all are equal. On the doublet band $E(0, P)$ does not depend on $n_{1}$, so the whole isospin-$P/2$ multiplet of (ii) is degenerate; $B_{\alpha}^{*}x(0, n_{1}, n_{2})$ is a nonzero multiple of $x(0, n_{1} + \delta_{\alpha1}, n_{2} + \delta_{\alpha2})$ for $P < n_{b}$, both at energy $E(0, P + 1)$ (not $E(0, P)$). Lowering $n$ from $P$ at fixed $P$ costs $-\omega_{D}$ per step, through $Z_{2}$ on the stretched vector; $Z_{2}$ adds a $\psi_{1}$ and removes a $\chi$, so it changes $N_{\psi} - N_{\chi}$ by $2$, while every $B_{\alpha}$ changes $N_{\psi}$ and $N_{\chi}$ alike and so leaves $N_{\psi} - N_{\chi}$ unbroken. In the sector $(0, P, P)$ no mode $1$ is occupied, so $S^{*}S$ and $B_{1}^{*}B_{1}$ vanish there and $H = (K_{\psi} + K_{\chi})P - G_{D}B_{2}^{*}B_{2}$ is the stored pairing element on the modes $2, 3$ of each block (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2)), whose band is lowest and whose next level is exactly $G_{D}n_{b}$ higher with none between for $0 < P < n_{b}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(i), (ii)). The stretched sector has $t_{3} = -P/2$ and $N_{\psi} = P$, so its levels are exactly those of total isospin $P/2$ at these numbers, the condensate's own isospin. These statements are on the band and in that sector; other sectors at the same numbers are treated in (x). The check verifies the degeneracy and the two pair additions at four couplings for $n_{b} \le 4$, and the sector statement by exact inertia of $H - E$ at $E$ the band value and the band value plus $G_{D}n_{b}$.

\emph{(v).} At $G_{D} = 0$, $H = K_{\psi}N_{\psi} + K_{\chi}N_{\chi} - G_{S}S^{*}S$ and $S^{*}S$ acts on the modes $1, 2$ only; on $V_{P}$ the mode-$3$ particle is a spectator and the modes $1, 2$ are in the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c}) = (P - 1, P)$ of the stored element. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(i) its levels are $K(2p + s_{a} + s_{c}) - G_{S}(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$; the largest value of $S^{*}S$ there is $(P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1)$, at $s_{a} = 0$, $s_{c} = 1$, $p = P - 1$ and top quasi-spin on the $n_{b} - 1$ other blocks. So the lowest level on $V_{P}$ is $E_{\mathrm{th}}$, and $0 \le S^{*}S \le (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1)$ on $V_{P}$ for all couplings. $x(P - 1, 0, 1) \in V_{P}$, and by (ii) its energy is $E_{D} = K_{\psi}(2P - 1) + K_{\chi} - (G_{S}(P - 1) + G_{D})(n_{b} - P + 1) = E_{\mathrm{th}} - G_{D}(n_{b} - P + 1)$; subtracting $E(P, 0) = 2K_{\psi}P - G_{S}P(n_{b} - P + 1)$ gives the two differences. The check certifies $E_{\mathrm{th}}$ as the lowest level at $G_{D} = 0$ by exact inertia for $n_{b} \le 4$. The lowest level of $H$ with $N_{\chi} = 0$ and $N = 2P$ is $E(P, 0)$: there $H$ is the stored element on modes $1, 2$, its sector $(P, P)$ has the band lowest (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(i)), and every isospin multiplet with $N_{1} + N_{2} = 2P$ meets that sector. Likewise every level with $N_{\chi} = 1$, $N = 2P$ has half-integer isospin and so a member in $V_{P}$ or its image under $t_{+}$, which has the same levels; this is why $V_{P}$ decides the doublet gap.

\emph{(vi).} Put $\rho_{bc} = \sum_{i}v_{i}(b)w_{i}(c)$, so $L_{bc} = \rho_{bc} - \rho_{cb}$, $L_{bc}^{*} = -L_{bc}$, and let $\sigma_{bc} = \rho_{bc} + \rho_{cb}$. Normal ordering with the CAR gives, summed over all indices: $C_{3} = 3N - Q$ and $\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb} = n_{b}N + Q$ with the same quartic $Q = \sum v_{i}(b)v_{j}(c)w_{j}(b)w_{i}(c)$, so $C_{3} + \sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb} = (n_{b} + 3)N$. Next $\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb} = \tfrac14(\sigma_{bc}^{2} - L_{bc}^{2} + [L_{bc}, \sigma_{bc}])$ and the commutator terms cancel between $(b, c)$ and $(c, b)$, so $\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb} = \tfrac14\sum_{b,c}\sigma_{bc}^{2} + \tfrac12C_{O}$. Finally $\sum_{b,c}\sigma_{bc}^{2} = 2\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{bc} + 2\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb}$ and, normal ordering again, $\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{bc} = N + \sum_{i,j}\sum_{b,c}v_{j}(b)v_{i}(b)w_{i}(c)w_{j}(c) = N + 2W$, because $W = \tfrac12\sum_{i \ne j}\pi_{ij}^{*}\pi_{ij}$ summed over blocks is that quartic. Combining, $\tfrac12\sum_{b,c}\rho_{bc}\rho_{cb} = \tfrac12N + W + \tfrac12C_{O}$, so $2W = (n_{b} + 3)N - C_{3} - N - C_{O} = N(n_{b} + 2) - C_{3} - C_{O}$. $C_{O}$ is a sum of $L^{*}L$, hence $C_{O} \ge 0$. The check verifies the identity on every Fock vector of $n_{b} = 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(vii).} On $V_{P}$ all number operators are constant, so $H = K_{\psi}(2P - 1) + K_{\chi} - (G_{S} - G_{D})S^{*}S - G_{D}W$. With $G_{S} - G_{D} \ge 0$, $S^{*}S \le (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1)$ by (v) and $W \le X$, every level is at least $K_{\psi}(2P - 1) + K_{\chi} - (G_{S} - G_{D})(P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1) - G_{D}X$, which is $E_{D} - G_{D}(X - P(n_{b} - P + 1))$. For the second level, Weyl's inequality for Hermitian $A$ and $B$, $\lambda_{2}(A + B) \ge \lambda_{1}(A) + \lambda_{2}(B)$ (levels in increasing order with multiplicity; from the min-max characterisation), with $A = -(G_{S} - G_{D})S^{*}S$, $\lambda_{1}(A) \ge -(G_{S} - G_{D})(P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1)$, and $B = -G_{D}W$, $\lambda_{2}(B) = -G_{D}X_{2}$, gives $\lambda_{2}(H) \ge E_{\mathrm{th}} + G_{D}(P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1) - G_{D}X_{2}$.

\emph{(viii).} By computation. The check builds $W$ on $V_{P}$ for $n_{b} = 2, \ldots, 6$ and every $P$ (dimensions up to $1800$) and counts its eigenvalues above $X$ and above $X_{2}$ by exact congruence diagonalisation of $W - a$ ($a = X$: none above, $a$ an eigenvalue; $a = X_{2}$ when $n_{b} - P + 1 > 3$ or $P = 1$: exactly one above, $a$ an eigenvalue), cross-checked against GA's congruence signature for $n_{b} \le 3$; it confirms $Wx(P - 1, 0, 1) = P(n_{b} - P + 1)x(P - 1, 0, 1)$. With these values (vii) gives: for $n_{b} - P + 1 \ge 3$, $X = P(n_{b} - P + 1)$ and every level is at least $E_{D}$, which is a level; for $n_{b} - P + 1 > 3$, $X_{2} - (P - 1)(n_{b} - P + 1) = 3$; for $n_{b} - P + 1 < 3$, $X - P(n_{b} - P + 1) = P + 2 - n_{b}$. Hence the ground state at $N = 2P$ is not the singlet band there although $\omega_{D} > 0$, and the difference of sector minima in (viii) is then not an excitation gap of the ground state. For the doublet-condensed coupling the check computes the inertia of $H - E$ on $(0, P, P)$ and $(1, P - 1, P)$ at $E = E(0, P) + G_{D}n_{b}$ (one and $n_{b}^{2}$ negative entries) and at $E = E(0, P)$ on $(1, P - 1, P)$ (none negative, one zero: the band member); the sector $(1, P - 1, P)$ has $t_{3} = 0$ and holds every isospin from $0$ up, and only one isospin-$P/2$ level lies below the threshold (that of the stretched sector), so the others have isospin below $P/2$.

\emph{Reading (argued).} The result realises the doublet-singlet route named in \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower-and-its-modes-carry-no-even-doublet} (step 5): its even doublets are products of a doublet mode and a singlet mode, as clause (3) there requires, and the doublet quantum is of that kind. synthesis.uniform-pair-channel-of-a-towe.formal:
Let the modes be tower planes, $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$, satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations (Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) on the Fock space $\mathcal{F}$, with its positive inner product and the adjoint $*$ ($v^{*} = w$, Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}). Let $Q_{1}, \dots, Q_{r}$ be commuting self-adjoint elements (charges) and $H$ a self-adjoint element commuting with each; a \emph{sector} is a nonzero joint eigenspace $\mathcal{F}_{s}$ ($Q_{i} = s_{i}$), and $E(s)$ is the lowest eigenvalue of $H$ on it. An element $X$ has charge $h \in \mathbb{R}^{r}$ if $[Q_{i}, X] = h_{i}X$ for all $i$; then $X\mathcal{F}_{s} \subset \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$ and $X^{*}$ has charge $-h$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(No order parameter in a sector.)} If $h \ne 0$, $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = 0$ for every $\psi$ in a sector. A one-dimensional eigenspace of $H$ lies in a sector; so an eigenvector $\psi$ of $H$ with $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle \ne 0$ exists only if the eigenspace meets two sectors $s$ and $s + h$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Variational bound.)} Let $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $H\psi = E(s)\psi$. If $X\psi \ne 0$, $E(s + h) - E(s) \le \langle X\psi, [H, X]\psi\rangle/\langle X\psi, X\psi\rangle$; if $X^{*}\psi \ne 0$, $E(s - h) - E(s) \le \langle X^{*}\psi, [H, X^{*}]\psi\rangle/\langle X^{*}\psi, X^{*}\psi\rangle$; each with equality exactly when $X\psi$ (respectively $X^{*}\psi$) is a lowest eigenvector of its sector.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Finite Goldstone bound for pairing-type elements.)} Let $H = H_{0} - GXX^{*}$, $G > 0$, $H_{0}$ self-adjoint commuting with the charges and $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$, $\varepsilon$ real, and let $C = [X, X^{*}]$ act on each sector as a scalar $c(s)$. Then the two quotients of (ii) are $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, so whenever $X\psi \ne 0 \ne X^{*}\psi$,
\[
E(s + h) + E(s - h) - 2E(s) \le G\bigl(c(s) - c(s - h)\bigr) ,
\]
and if the ground state of $H$ lies in $\mathcal{F}_{s^{*}}$ with $X\psi \ne 0 \ne X^{*}\psi$, both $E(s^{*} \pm h) - E(s^{*})$ lie in $[0, G(c(s^{*}) - c(s^{*} - h))]$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The single shell.)} For the stored element $H_{4} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) - GP^{*}P$, $P = \sum_{b}w_{a}w_{c}$, on $n_{b} \ge 2$ blocks, $K \ge 0$, $G > 0$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2)), with charges $N_{a}, N_{c}$ and $X = P^{*}$ ($h = (1, 1)$, $\varepsilon = 2K$, $C = N_{a} + N_{c} - n_{b}$), the bound of (iii) is $2G$ and is attained. The ground energy of $H_{4}$ is $\min_{n}E(n)$, $E(n) = 2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1) = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$, $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$, attained at the band vector $\psi_{n^{*}} = (P^{*})^{n^{*}}\Omega$, $n^{*}$ an integer in $[0, n_{b} - 1]$ nearest $\gamma$ (and $0$ if $\gamma < \tfrac12$); the ground eigenspace is spanned by the $\psi_{n}$ with $E(n) = \min E$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Condensed: $Gn_{b} > 2K$.)} $n^{*} \ge 1$, $E(n^{*} \pm 1) - E(n^{*}) = G(1 \pm 2(n^{*} - \gamma)) \in [0, 2G]$ with sum $2G$, and $(P + P^{*})\psi_{n^{*}} = \psi_{n^{*}+1} + n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\psi_{n^{*}-1}$, $\|P^{*}\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2} = (n^{*} + 1)(n_{b} - n^{*})\|\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2}$, $\|P\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2} = n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\|\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2}$: the uniform pair channel has all its weight on the two neighbouring band levels. Against the pair-breaking threshold $Gn_{b}$ at fixed numbers (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(ii)) the larger of the two is at most $2/n_{b}$ of it, and at the gap equation $Gn_{b} = 2E$ it is at most $4E/n_{b}$, which tends to $0$ as $n_{b} \to \infty$ at fixed $E$ while the threshold stays $2E$.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Symmetric: $Gn_{b} < 2K$.)} $\Omega$ is the unique ground state, and $P^{*}\Omega$ is an eigenvector at $2K - Gn_{b} > 0$, below the broken-pair level $2K$ of the same sector: the uniform pair is gapped, and its gap closes exactly at the condensation threshold $Gn_{b} = 2K$.
\item[(c)] \emph{(Degenerate couplings.)} At $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$, $n \in \{0, \dots, \lfloor n_{b}/2\rfloor\}$ (so that $K \ge 0$), $E(n) = E(n + 1) = \min E$ and $\psi = \psi_{n} + \psi_{n+1}$ is a ground state with $\langle\psi, P\psi\rangle = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} \ne 0$; at every other coupling every ground state of $H_{4}$ has $\langle P\rangle = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (i) to (iv) are proved. \emph{Reading (argued).} With a condensate the uniform helicity-zero composite scalar of a floor is the Goldstone rotor of the broken pair phase, the finite-size form of the flat phase direction of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(4): gapless in the collective limit at fixed mean-field gap, with no weight at the pair-breaking threshold. A gapped uniform composite exists only without a condensate. For a composite Higgs doublet, (i) applies to every charge the doublet carries, and the directions of its broken charges are of this rotor kind where (iii) applies; a gapped composite doublet would then have to be one that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet). The doublet floor and inter-condensate couplings, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is not a function of the charges, are not treated here.
synthesis.uniform-pair-channel-of-a-towe.technical: For pairing-type elements, whose pair commutator $[X, X^{*}]$ is a function of the charges: take tower modes on their Fock space, a set of commuting charges and a Hamiltonian commuting with them; sectors are the joint eigenspaces and $E(s)$ the lowest energy in sector $s$. (i) A field of nonzero charge has no expectation in any vector of one sector, so a finite system shows an order parameter only in an energy eigenspace that spans two sectors. (ii) Applying a charged field $X$ to a lowest vector of sector $s$ gives a trial vector for sector $s + h$, so $E(s + h) - E(s)$ is at most $\langle X\psi, [H, X]\psi\rangle/\|X\psi\|^{2}$, and likewise downwards with $X^{*}$. (iii) For $H = H_{0} - GXX^{*}$ with $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ and $[X, X^{*}]$ equal to a function $c$ of the charges, the two quotients are $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, so the second difference of the sector ground energies is at most $G(c(s) - c(s - h))$ at every size, and if the ground state's sector is one where $X$ and $X^{*}$ both act nontrivially both neighbouring sector energies are within that bound. (iv) For the stored single-shell pairing element, $c$ steps by $2$, so the bound is $2G$, and it is attained: the band $E(n) = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$ with $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$ holds the ground state at the integer nearest $\gamma$. With a condensate ($Gn_{b} > 2K$) the two neighbouring band levels are within $2G$, they carry all of $(P + P^{*})\psi$, and against the pair-breaking threshold $Gn_{b} = 2E$ they are at most $2/n_{b}$ of it ($4E/n_{b}$ at fixed $E$). Without one ($Gn_{b} < 2K$) the vacuum is the unique ground state and the bound pair sits at $2K - Gn_{b}$, below the broken-pair level $2K$, closing at the condensation threshold. Only at the degenerate couplings $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$ does a ground state carry $\langle P\rangle \ne 0$. The doublet floor and coupled condensates, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is not a function of the charges, are not covered. Reading (argued): for pairing-type elements a condensate's uniform composite scalar is its Goldstone rotor, and a gapped uniform composite needs no condensate; a gapped composite doublet would have to be a doublet that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet).
synthesis.uniform-pair-channel-of-a-towe.lay: When fermions pair up and the pairs condense, the condensate picks a phase, and changing that phase costs no energy in the idealised infinite system: the textbook Goldstone mode. This result asks what happens on a finite stack of the tower's modes, where everything is exact. The uniform pair mode then does not become a separate massive particle: all of its response sits on two neighbouring levels whose spacing shrinks in proportion to one over the number of pair sites, while the energy needed to break a pair stays fixed. In this model a genuinely gapped uniform pair state exists only when nothing condenses. The result covers this kind of pairing only: it does not cover a doublet of paired fermions on one stack, or two condensates coupled to each other, where the pairs' bookkeeping depends on more than the charges. As a reading (argued, on this model), a composite Higgs built from a condensate of this kind would not be the condensate's own uniform pair mode; it would have to be a mode outside that pair channel, or a doublet that does not condense.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The modes are tower planes with $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$; by Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors} and Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit} they satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations and act on the Fock space $\mathcal{F}$ with its positive inner product, for which $*$ is the adjoint; $v^{*} = w$ is the mutual adjointness of the ladder pairs in Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}. Everything below is finite-dimensional linear algebra on $\mathcal{F}$ with real coefficients; no unit is needed. Since the $Q_{i}$ are commuting self-adjoint operators, $\mathcal{F}$ is the orthogonal sum of the sectors $\mathcal{F}_{s}$, and since $H$ commutes with every $Q_{i}$ it maps each sector into itself, so $E(s)$, the lowest eigenvalue of $H$ on $\mathcal{F}_{s}$, is defined for every nonzero sector. If $X$ has charge $h$ then for $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $Q_{i}X\psi = XQ_{i}\psi + h_{i}X\psi = (s_{i} + h_{i})X\psi$, so $X\mathcal{F}_{s} \subset \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$; taking adjoints of $[Q_{i}, X] = h_{i}X$ gives $[Q_{i}, X^{*}] = -h_{i}X^{*}$, so $X^{*}$ has charge $-h$.

\emph{(i).} For $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$ and $h \ne 0$, $X\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$, which is orthogonal to $\mathcal{F}_{s}$ (eigenspaces of a self-adjoint $Q_{i}$ with $h_{i} \ne 0$ for different eigenvalues), so $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = 0$. Each $Q_{i}$ commutes with $H$ and so maps each eigenspace of $H$ into itself; a one-dimensional eigenspace is then spanned by a common eigenvector of the $Q_{i}$, that is, it lies in a sector. More generally an eigenspace $V$ of $H$ is the orthogonal sum of its intersections $V_{s}$ with the sectors, and for $\psi = \sum_{s}\psi_{s}$ one has $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = \sum_{s}\langle\psi_{s+h}, X\psi_{s}\rangle$, which vanishes unless some $V_{s}$ and $V_{s+h}$ are both nonzero.

\emph{(ii).} Let $H\psi = E(s)\psi$, $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, and $X\psi \ne 0$. Then $X\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$ and $E(s+h)$ is at most its Rayleigh quotient, $E(s+h) \le \langle X\psi, HX\psi\rangle/\langle X\psi, X\psi\rangle$, with equality if and only if $X\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H$ for the eigenvalue $E(s+h)$ (finite dimension, $H$ self-adjoint on $\mathcal{F}_{s+h}$). Write $HX\psi = XH\psi + [H, X]\psi = E(s)X\psi + [H, X]\psi$; this gives the first bound. The second is the same argument for $X^{*}$, of charge $-h$.

\emph{(iii).} From $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ with $\varepsilon$ real and $H_{0}$ self-adjoint, the adjoint gives $[H_{0}, X^{*}] = -\varepsilon X^{*}$. With $C = [X, X^{*}]$,
\[
[XX^{*}, X] = X[X^{*}, X] = -XC, \qquad [XX^{*}, X^{*}] = [X, X^{*}]X^{*} = CX^{*},
\]
so $[H, X] = \varepsilon X + GXC$ and $[H, X^{*}] = -\varepsilon X^{*} - GCX^{*}$. On $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $XC\psi = c(s)X\psi$, and $X^{*}\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s-h}$ gives $CX^{*}\psi = c(s - h)X^{*}\psi$. Hence the two quotients of (ii) are exactly $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, which are the two inequalities, and adding them bounds the second difference by $G(c(s) - c(s - h))$. If the ground state of $H$ lies in $\mathcal{F}_{s^{*}}$, then $E(s^{*}) \le E(s^{*} \pm h)$, so both differences are nonnegative, and their sum, hence each, is at most $G(c(s^{*}) - c(s^{*} - h))$.

\emph{(iv).} For $H_{4}$ take the charges $N_{a}$, $N_{c}$ and $X = P^{*} = \sum_{b}v_{c}v_{a}$, which raises each by one: $h = (1, 1)$. $H_{0} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) = KN$ with $N = N_{a} + N_{c}$ has $[N, P^{*}] = 2P^{*}$, so $\varepsilon = 2K$. By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}, $[P, P^{*}] = n_{b} - N$, so $C = [P^{*}, P] = N - n_{b}$, which on the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ is the scalar $N_{a} + N_{c} - n_{b}$; on $(n, n)$, $c = 2n - n_{b}$, and $c(n, n) - c(n - 1, n - 1) = 2$. So (iii) applies with the bound $2G$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(i), every level of the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ is $K(2p + s_{a} + s_{c}) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$ with $p$ pairs on $\Omega = n_{b} - s_{a} - s_{c}$ blocks; the last factor is largest at $j = \Omega/2$, where it is $p(\Omega - p + 1)$. So every level with $p$ pairs and $s = s_{a} + s_{c}$ singly occupied blocks is at least
\[
2Kp + Ks - Gp(n_{b} - s - p + 1) = E(p) + Ks + Gps \ge E(p), \qquad E(n) = 2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1),
\]
the band of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2), the lowest level of the sector $(n, n)$; its vector is $\psi_{n} = (P^{*})^{n}\Omega$, the quasi-spin state of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr} with $j = n_{b}/2$, $j_{z} = n - n_{b}/2$. Hence the ground energy of $H_{4}$ on all of $\mathcal{F}$ is $\min_{n}E(n)$. Completing the square, $E(n) = Gn^{2} - (G(n_{b} + 1) - 2K)n = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$ with $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$, so the minimum over integers $0 \le n \le n_{b}$ is at the integer $n^{*}$ nearest $\gamma$ (clamped to $0$ when $\gamma < \tfrac12$); since $\gamma \le (n_{b} + 1)/2 \le n_{b} - \tfrac12$ for $n_{b} \ge 2$, a minimiser $n^{*} \le n_{b} - 1$ can always be chosen; the equality $\gamma = n_{b} - \tfrac12$ occurs only at $n_{b} = 2$, $K = 0$, where $E(1) = E(2)$ is the degenerate coupling $n = 1$ of (c). The quasi-spin ladder gives $P^{*}\psi_{n} = \psi_{n+1}$, $P\psi_{n} = n(n_{b} - n + 1)\psi_{n-1}$, and $\|P^{*}\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (j - j_{z})(j + j_{z} + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2}$, $\|P\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} = n(n_{b} - n + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2}$.

(a) $n^{*} \ge 1$ exactly when $\gamma > \tfrac12$, that is $Gn_{b} > 2K$ (at $Gn_{b} = 2K$, $E(0) = E(1)$). Then $E(n^{*} \pm 1) - E(n^{*}) = G((n^{*} \pm 1 - \gamma)^{2} - (n^{*} - \gamma)^{2}) = G(1 \pm 2(n^{*} - \gamma))$, and $|n^{*} - \gamma| \le \tfrac12$ puts both in $[0, 2G]$ with sum $2G$: the bound of (iii) holds with equality, as (ii) says it must, since $P^{*}\psi_{n^{*}}$ and $P\psi_{n^{*}}$ are lowest vectors of their sectors. $(P + P^{*})\psi_{n^{*}} = \psi_{n^{*}+1} + n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\psi_{n^{*}-1}$, with the norms above. The pair-breaking threshold at fixed numbers is $Gn_{b}$ above the band (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(ii)), so the larger rotor difference over the threshold is at most $2G/(Gn_{b}) = 2/n_{b}$; at the gap equation $Gn_{b} = 2E$ of (iii) there, the rotor is at most $4E/n_{b}$.

(b) If $Gn_{b} < 2K$ then $\gamma < \tfrac12$, $n^{*} = 0$, and every other level is positive: band levels $E(p) = p(2K - G(n_{b} - p + 1)) \ge p(2K - Gn_{b}) > 0$ for $p \ge 1$, and levels with $s \ge 1$ exceed $E(p) + Ks > 0$ ($K > Gn_{b}/2 > 0$). So $\Omega$ is the unique ground state, $P^{*}\Omega = \psi_{1}$ has energy $E(1) = 2K - Gn_{b} > 0$, and the sector $(1, 1)$ also contains the level $2K$ (one $a$ and one $c$ on different blocks, $p = 0$, $s_{a} = s_{c} = 1$). As $Gn_{b} \to 2K$ from below, $E(1) \to 0$.

(c) At $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$ with $0 \le n \le \lfloor n_{b}/2\rfloor$ an integer (the range where $K \ge 0$, which the bound $E(p) + Ks + Gps \ge E(p)$ uses), $\gamma = n + \tfrac12$, so $E(n) = E(n + 1) = \min E$ and the ground eigenspace contains $\psi_{n}$ and $\psi_{n+1}$; for $\psi = \psi_{n} + \psi_{n+1}$, $\langle\psi, P\psi\rangle = \langle\psi_{n}, P\psi_{n+1}\rangle = \|P^{*}\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} \ne 0$. The ground eigenspace is always the span of the band vectors $\psi_{n}$ with $E(n) = \min E$: a level with $s = 0$ and $j < n_{b}/2$ lies strictly above $E(p)$, since $(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1) = j(j + 1) - j_{z}(j_{z} - 1)$ increases strictly with $j$; a level with $s \ge 1$ is at least $E(p) + Ks + Gps$, which exceeds $\min E$ unless $K = 0$ and $p = 0$, and then it equals $E(0) = 0 > E(n^{*})$, because $K = 0$ gives $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 \ge \tfrac32$ and $E(n^{*}) = -Gn^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1) < 0$. So at every other coupling, where the minimiser $n^{*}$ is unique, the ground state is $\psi_{n^{*}}$ up to a factor, it lies in the sector $(n^{*}, n^{*})$, and by (i) it has $\langle P\rangle = 0$.

\emph{Reading (argued).} The uniform pair field is the helicity-zero composite scalar of the floor. Clauses (iv)(a) and (iv)(b) say exactly how its gap behaves: with a condensate ($n^{*} \ge 1$) its whole weight from the ground state sits on the two neighbouring band levels, within $2G$, and no weight at the threshold; this is the Goldstone rotor of the broken pair phase (the flat phase direction of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(4) seen at finite size), and in the collective limit at fixed mean-field gap it closes as $4E/n_{b}$. Without a condensate the bound pair is gapped, at $2K - Gn_{b}$, and the gap closes where condensation begins. Clause (i) is what makes a finite order parameter need degeneracy across sectors, and (iii) is the finite form of the Goldstone theorem for a pairing-type element: it needs only $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ and a commutator $[X, X^{*}]$ that is a function of the charges, so it covers several species paired by one uniform field with a common shell energy, and any extra term in $H_{0}$ that commutes with $X$. For a composite Higgs doublet, (i) applies to each charge the doublet carries; in a condensed doublet the directions of the broken charges are of this rotor kind, so a gapped composite doublet would have to be one that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet). The doublet floor and two-condensate couplings, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is no longer a function of the charges, are not treated here.
